   884	// resolveShadowRef returns the shadow branch reference, preferring a pre-resolved
   885	// ref when available and falling back to a repo lookup.
   886	func resolveShadowRef(repo *git.Repository, branchName string, preResolved *plumbing.Reference) (ref *plumbing.Reference, exists bool) {
   887		if preResolved != nil {
   888			return preResolved, true
   889		}
   890		refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(branchName)
   891		resolved, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   892		if err != nil {
   893			return nil, false
   894		}
   895		return resolved, true
   896	}
   897	
   898	// filterFilesTouched narrows sessionData.FilesTouched to files present in
   899	// committedFiles. When no prior files were recorded, it falls back to the
   900	// committed set (minus Entire metadata) — but only when sessionHasEvidenceOfWork
   901	// is true. The fallback was originally unconditional, which let sessions that
   902	// were registered at SessionStart but never produced anything (e.g. ephemeral
   903	// Codex sessions whose hooks fired with a null transcript_path and never
   904	// reached SaveStep) inherit another session's committed files.
   905	func filterFilesTouched(sessionData *ExtractedSessionData, committedFiles map[string]struct{}, state *SessionState) {
   906		if len(committedFiles) == 0 {
   907			return
   908		}
   909		if len(sessionData.FilesTouched) > 0 {
   910			filtered := make([]string, 0, len(sessionData.FilesTouched))
   911			for _, f := range sessionData.FilesTouched {
   912				if _, ok := committedFiles[f]; ok {
   913					filtered = append(filtered, f)
   914				}
   915			}
   916			sessionData.FilesTouched = filtered
   917			return
   918		}
   919		if !sessionHasEvidenceOfWork(sessionData, state) {
   920			return
   921		}
   922		sessionData.FilesTouched = committedFilesExcludingMetadata(committedFiles)
   923	}
   924	
   925	// sessionHasEvidenceOfWork returns true when the session looks like a real
   926	// participant — either it produced a readable transcript or a prior SaveStep
   927	// recorded a checkpoint (StepCount > 0). False means the session was likely
   928	// registered but never did anything; treating such a session as the author of
   929	// the committed files would attribute another session's work to it.
   930	// Task records deliberately do NOT count here: a record-bearing session may
   931	// have touched no files at all (read-only subagent), so letting records
   932	// qualify the session for the committed-files fallback would be the exact
   933	// mis-attribution this guard prevents.
   934	func sessionHasEvidenceOfWork(sessionData *ExtractedSessionData, state *SessionState) bool {
   935		if len(sessionData.Transcript) > 0 {
   936			return true
   937		}
   938		return state != nil && state.StepCount > 0
   939	}
   940	
   941	// extractOrCreateSessionData tries to extract session data from the shadow branch,
   942	// live transcript, or creates empty session data as a fallback. The empty case is
   943	// handled by the skip gate in CondenseSession.
   944	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) extractOrCreateSessionData(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, ag agent.Agent, shadowHash plumbing.Hash, hasShadowBranch bool, state *SessionState) (*ExtractedSessionData, error) {
   945		switch {
   946		case hasShadowBranch:
   947			// Shadow branch exists (from SaveStep commits) — extract transcript and
   948			// metadata from the branch tree, preferring the live transcript if fresher.
   949			data, err := s.extractSessionData(ctx, repo, shadowHash, state.SessionID, state.FilesTouched, state.AgentType, state.TranscriptPath, state.CheckpointTranscriptStart, state.Phase.IsActive())
   950			if err != nil {
   951				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to extract session data: %w", err)
   952			}
   953			return data, nil
   954		case state.TranscriptPath != "":
   955			// No shadow branch but a live transcript path is known — read directly
   956			// from disk. This handles mid-session commits before SaveStep runs.
   957			if state.Phase.IsActive() {
   958				prepareTranscriptIfNeeded(ctx, ag, state.TranscriptPath)
   959			}
   960			data, err := s.extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript(ctx, state)
   961			if err != nil {
   962				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to extract session data from live transcript: %w", err)
   963			}
   964			return data, nil
   965		default:
   966			// No shadow branch and no transcript path — create empty session data.
   967			// This happens for sessions where the agent never set TranscriptPath
   968			// (e.g., Codex hooks may send null transcript_path). The skip gate in
   969			// CondenseSession will skip condensation if nothing is found.
   970			logging.Debug(logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint"),
   971				"no shadow branch and no transcript path, returning empty session data",
   972				slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),

   679	// condensationSessionWriteRequest returns the write request for one
   680	// condensation. Every condensation write is ReservedSession, unconditionally.
   681	//
   682	// The tempting refinement — send ReservedSession only when this session's own
   683	// pending attempt matches the checkpoint ID, and plain Session otherwise —
   684	// is wrong, and wrong in a worse direction than the problem it solves. A
   685	// checkpoint can hold several sessions, and only the one that reserved the ID
   686	// carries the reservation in its state. Routing per session would send the
   687	// reserving session's write to the backend the ID belongs to and every sibling's
   688	// write to the configured primary, splitting one checkpoint across both
   689	// backends. Reads are not symmetrical about that: a ULID resolves from git-refs
   690	// only, so the siblings written to the branch would simply be invisible. See
   691	// TestCondensationSessionWrites_KeepSharedReservedCheckpointInOneBackend.
   692	//
   693	// The cost of routing everything by ID format is narrow. It only diverges from
   694	// the configured primary when the ID's format disagrees with the primary, and
   695	// the two fail-soft defaults agree: GenerateCheckpointID mints hex when the
   696	// checkpoints config cannot be read, and resolvePrimaryType defaults to
   697	// git-branch on the same unreadable config. Reaching a mismatch on a *fresh* ID
   698	// therefore takes a config read that succeeds for one call and fails for the
   699	// other — and even then the checkpoint stays readable, because a hex ID under a
   700	// git-refs primary falls through to the branch on read.
   701	//
   702	// If the per-checkpoint routing decision ever does need to be conditional, it
   703	// has to be made once for the whole checkpoint (from the commit trailer or a
   704	// checkpoint-level flag), never per session.
   705	func condensationSessionWriteRequest(opts cpkg.WriteOptions) cpkg.WriteRequest {
   706		return cpkg.ReservedSession(opts)
   707	}

   898	// filterFilesTouched narrows sessionData.FilesTouched to files present in
   899	// committedFiles. When no prior files were recorded, it falls back to the
   900	// committed set (minus Entire metadata) — but only when sessionHasEvidenceOfWork
   901	// is true. The fallback was originally unconditional, which let sessions that
   902	// were registered at SessionStart but never produced anything (e.g. ephemeral
   903	// Codex sessions whose hooks fired with a null transcript_path and never
   904	// reached SaveStep) inherit another session's committed files.
   905	func filterFilesTouched(sessionData *ExtractedSessionData, committedFiles map[string]struct{}, state *SessionState) {
   906		if len(committedFiles) == 0 {
   907			return
   908		}
   909		if len(sessionData.FilesTouched) > 0 {
   910			filtered := make([]string, 0, len(sessionData.FilesTouched))
   911			for _, f := range sessionData.FilesTouched {
   912				if _, ok := committedFiles[f]; ok {
   913					filtered = append(filtered, f)
   914				}
   915			}
   916			sessionData.FilesTouched = filtered
   917			return
   918		}

   920			return
   921		}
   922		sessionData.FilesTouched = committedFilesExcludingMetadata(committedFiles)

  1028	// buildSummaryGenerator returns a Generator based on the configured summary provider.
  1029	// Returns nil if no provider is configured (GenerateFromTranscript falls back to ClaudeGenerator).
  1030	//
  1031	// The return type is the summarize.Generator interface rather than the concrete
  1032	// adapter pointer so callers can't accidentally hold a non-nil interface that
  1033	// wraps a nil pointer (the classic Go nil-interface footgun).
  1034	func buildSummaryGenerator(ctx context.Context) summarize.Generator {
  1035		s, err := settings.Load(ctx)
  1036		if err != nil {
  1037			// Warn (not Debug): this is the auto-summarize hot path on every commit.
  1038			// A settings-load failure silently downgrades the user's configured
  1039			// provider to the default, and Debug would hide that from operators.
  1040			logging.Warn(ctx, "could not load settings for summary provider, using default",
  1041				"error", err.Error())
  1042			return nil
  1043		}
  1044		if s.SummaryGeneration == nil || s.SummaryGeneration.Provider == "" {
  1045			return nil
  1046		}
  1047	
  1048		providerName := types.AgentName(s.SummaryGeneration.Provider)
  1049		ag, err := agent.Get(providerName)
  1050		if err != nil {
  1051			discoverExternalSummaryProviders(ctx)
  1052			ag, err = agent.Get(providerName)
  1053			if err != nil {
  1054				logging.Warn(ctx, "configured summary provider not available, using default",
  1055					"provider", s.SummaryGeneration.Provider, "error", err.Error())
  1056				return nil
  1057			}
  1058		}
  1059	
  1060		tg, ok := agent.AsTextGenerator(ag)
  1061		if !ok {
  1062			logging.Warn(ctx, "configured summary provider does not support text generation, using default",
  1063				"provider", s.SummaryGeneration.Provider)
  1064			return nil
  1065		}

  1068		// for development while a different agent generates summaries. Fall back
  1069		// silently (Warn log) because this runs in the post-commit hook and a
  1070		// hard error would block the commit.
  1071		if !external.IsExternal(ag) && !isSummaryProviderCLIAvailable(providerName) {

  1073				"provider", s.SummaryGeneration.Provider)
  1074			return nil
  1075		}
  1076	
  1077		return &summarize.TextGeneratorAdapter{
  1078			TextGenerator: tg,
  1079			Model:         summarize.ResolveModel(providerName, s.SummaryGeneration.Model),

   132	// refBase resolves a checkpoint ref's current tip commit (the parent for the
   133	// next write) and subtree object (the checkpoint's current contents) with a
   134	// LOCAL-ONLY lookup. A missing ref yields (ZeroHash, nil) so the next write
   135	// becomes an orphan commit — correct for creates, whose ref never exists yet
   136	// (locally or remotely); probing the remote would add a doomed round-trip to
   137	// every condensation and, with a fetcher configured, fail offline writes.
   138	// Backfills, which target an existing checkpoint, use refBaseForBackfill
   139	// instead. Migration (migrate.go) also uses refBase deliberately: it imports
   140	// from the LOCAL v1 branch and must never probe the remote, even though its
   141	// target ref may already exist. One writeSession caller does target an
   142	// existing checkpoint — attach, which adds a session to it — but attach
   143	// pre-fetches and verifies the ref's presence itself (refreshCheckpoint)
   144	// before writing, so the local-only probe is safe there too.
   145	func (s *gitRefsStore) refBase(cid id.CheckpointID) (plumbing.Hash, *object.Tree, error) {
   146		refName, err := RefName(cid)
   147		if err != nil {
   148			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, err
   149		}
   150		ref, err := s.repo.Reference(refName, true)
   151		if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   152			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, nil // no ref yet → new checkpoint (orphan)
   153		}
   154		if err != nil {
   155			// A real lookup failure (IO/corruption), not an absent ref: surface it
   156			// rather than silently starting a fresh orphan history over the ref.
   157			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve checkpoint ref %s: %w", refName, err)
   158		}
   159		return s.refTip(cid, ref)
   160	}
   161	
   162	// refBaseForBackfill resolves like refBase, but a ref missing locally is
   163	// first fetched once from the remote (resolveRefMaybeFetch) when a fetcher is
   164	// configured: a backfill targets an EXISTING checkpoint that may have been
   165	// written or migrated on another machine, and declaring it absent without
   166	// looking remotely diverges from the read path — the backfill would be
   167	// handled as targeting a nonexistent checkpoint while reads, which DO fetch,
   168	// serve the refs copy, leaving the backfilled data permanently invisible.
   169	// A ref absent even after the fetch yields (ZeroHash, nil), which the
   170	// backfill helpers report as ErrCheckpointNotFound — the signal that the
   171	// checkpoint does not exist in this backend. A fetch FAILURE is returned
   172	// as-is: transient unavailability must never masquerade as absence, because
   173	// a caller or routing layer acting on a false "absent" would misdirect the
   174	// backfill (e.g. onto a stale copy in another backend) instead of retrying.
   175	func (s *gitRefsStore) refBaseForBackfill(ctx context.Context, cid id.CheckpointID) (plumbing.Hash, *object.Tree, error) {
   176		ref, err := s.resolveRefMaybeFetch(ctx, cid)
   177		if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   178			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, nil // genuinely absent → backfill reports not-found
   179		}
   180		if err != nil {
   181			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, err
   182		}
   183		return s.refTip(cid, ref)
   184	}

   186	// refTip reads the commit and tree at a resolved checkpoint ref.
   187	func (s *gitRefsStore) refTip(cid id.CheckpointID, ref *plumbing.Reference) (plumbing.Hash, *object.Tree, error) {
   188		commit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   189		if err != nil {
   190			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, fmt.Errorf("read checkpoint commit %s: %w", ref.Hash(), err)
   191		}
   192		tree, err := commit.Tree()
   193		if err != nil {
   194			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, fmt.Errorf("read checkpoint tree for %s: %w", cid, err)
   195		}
   196		return ref.Hash(), tree, nil
   197	}

   199	// enqueueForPush records refName in the push-discovery queue, logging (never
   200	// returning) on failure so the local ref write still succeeds.
   201	//
   202	// The queue is resolved with the cancellation stripped from ctx. By the time we
   203	// get here the ref is already written locally, and the queue is the ONLY
   204	// push-discovery mechanism there is — see the
   205	// pushQueueFileName doc. A ref that misses the queue is never pushed, and the
   206	// writers above are idempotent, so a re-run skips it as already-present and
   207	// never re-enqueues it: it stays local-only forever. Resolving the queue shells
   208	// out to `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, which fails instantly on a canceled

   210	// that already happened. This local, sub-millisecond step therefore completes
   211	// even during shutdown (a second Ctrl-C still force-quits the process).

   216				slog.String("ref", refName.String()), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   217			return
   218		}
   219		if err := q.Enqueue(refName); err != nil {
   220			logging.Warn(ctx, "checkpoint: enqueue checkpoint ref for push failed",
   221				slog.String("ref", refName.String()), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   222		}
   223	}

   123		case SessionSummary:

   125		case CheckpointAttribution:

   132	// refBase resolves a checkpoint ref's current tip commit (the parent for the
   133	// next write) and subtree object (the checkpoint's current contents) with a
   134	// LOCAL-ONLY lookup. A missing ref yields (ZeroHash, nil) so the next write
   135	// becomes an orphan commit — correct for creates, whose ref never exists yet
   136	// (locally or remotely); probing the remote would add a doomed round-trip to
   137	// every condensation and, with a fetcher configured, fail offline writes.
   138	// Backfills, which target an existing checkpoint, use refBaseForBackfill
   139	// instead. Migration (migrate.go) also uses refBase deliberately: it imports
   140	// from the LOCAL v1 branch and must never probe the remote, even though its
   141	// target ref may already exist. One writeSession caller does target an
   142	// existing checkpoint — attach, which adds a session to it — but attach
   143	// pre-fetches and verifies the ref's presence itself (refreshCheckpoint)
   144	// before writing, so the local-only probe is safe there too.
   145	func (s *gitRefsStore) refBase(cid id.CheckpointID) (plumbing.Hash, *object.Tree, error) {
   146		refName, err := RefName(cid)
   147		if err != nil {
   148			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, err
   149		}
   150		ref, err := s.repo.Reference(refName, true)
   151		if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   152			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, nil // no ref yet → new checkpoint (orphan)
   153		}
   154		if err != nil {
   155			// A real lookup failure (IO/corruption), not an absent ref: surface it
   156			// rather than silently starting a fresh orphan history over the ref.
   157			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve checkpoint ref %s: %w", refName, err)
   158		}
   159		return s.refTip(cid, ref)
   160	}
   161	
   162	// refBaseForBackfill resolves like refBase, but a ref missing locally is
   163	// first fetched once from the remote (resolveRefMaybeFetch) when a fetcher is
   164	// configured: a backfill targets an EXISTING checkpoint that may have been
   165	// written or migrated on another machine, and declaring it absent without
   166	// looking remotely diverges from the read path — the backfill would be
   167	// handled as targeting a nonexistent checkpoint while reads, which DO fetch,
   168	// serve the refs copy, leaving the backfilled data permanently invisible.
   169	// A ref absent even after the fetch yields (ZeroHash, nil), which the
   170	// backfill helpers report as ErrCheckpointNotFound — the signal that the
   171	// checkpoint does not exist in this backend. A fetch FAILURE is returned
   172	// as-is: transient unavailability must never masquerade as absence, because
   173	// a caller or routing layer acting on a false "absent" would misdirect the
   174	// backfill (e.g. onto a stale copy in another backend) instead of retrying.
   175	func (s *gitRefsStore) refBaseForBackfill(ctx context.Context, cid id.CheckpointID) (plumbing.Hash, *object.Tree, error) {
   176		ref, err := s.resolveRefMaybeFetch(ctx, cid)
   177		if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   178			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, nil // genuinely absent → backfill reports not-found
   179		}
   180		if err != nil {
   181			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, err
   182		}
   183		return s.refTip(cid, ref)
   184	}

   186	// refTip reads the commit and tree at a resolved checkpoint ref.
   187	func (s *gitRefsStore) refTip(cid id.CheckpointID, ref *plumbing.Reference) (plumbing.Hash, *object.Tree, error) {
   188		commit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   189		if err != nil {
   190			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, fmt.Errorf("read checkpoint commit %s: %w", ref.Hash(), err)
   191		}
   192		tree, err := commit.Tree()
   193		if err != nil {
   194			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, fmt.Errorf("read checkpoint tree for %s: %w", cid, err)
   195		}
   196		return ref.Hash(), tree, nil
   197	}

   199	// enqueueForPush records refName in the push-discovery queue, logging (never
   200	// returning) on failure so the local ref write still succeeds.
   201	//
   202	// The queue is resolved with the cancellation stripped from ctx. By the time we
   203	// get here the ref is already written locally, and the queue is the ONLY
   204	// push-discovery mechanism there is — see the
   205	// pushQueueFileName doc. A ref that misses the queue is never pushed, and the
   206	// writers above are idempotent, so a re-run skips it as already-present and
   207	// never re-enqueues it: it stays local-only forever. Resolving the queue shells
   208	// out to `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, which fails instantly on a canceled
   209	// ctx, so honoring cancellation here would drop the bookkeeping for a write
   210	// that already happened. This local, sub-millisecond step therefore completes
   211	// even during shutdown (a second Ctrl-C still force-quits the process).
   212	func (s *gitRefsStore) enqueueForPush(ctx context.Context, refName plumbing.ReferenceName) {
   213		q, err := PushQueueForRepo(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), s.repo)
   214		if err != nil {
   215			logging.Warn(ctx, "checkpoint: resolve push queue failed; ref not enqueued",
   216				slog.String("ref", refName.String()), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   217			return
   218		}
   219		if err := q.Enqueue(refName); err != nil {
   220			logging.Warn(ctx, "checkpoint: enqueue checkpoint ref for push failed",
   221				slog.String("ref", refName.String()), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   222		}
   223	}

   226		ctx context.Context,
   227		cid id.CheckpointID,
   228		base func() (plumbing.Hash, *object.Tree, error),
   229		build func(parentHash plumbing.Hash, existing *object.Tree) (plumbing.Hash, error),
   230	) error {
   231		refName, err := RefName(cid)
   232		if err != nil {
   233			return err
   234		}
   235		err = updatePersistentRef(ctx, s.repo, refName, func() (plumbing.Hash, plumbing.Hash, error) {
   236			parentHash, existing, baseErr := base()
   237			if baseErr != nil {
   238				return plumbing.ZeroHash, plumbing.ZeroHash, baseErr

   244			return err
   245		}

   115	// the root tree itself (the per-checkpoint-ref layout, where the whole tree is

   117	func (s *treeWriter) subtreeObjAt(rootTreeHash plumbing.Hash, path string) (*object.Tree, error) {

   138	// checkpointSubtreePath joins a checkpoint-relative git tree path from a base and
   139	// trailing segments using path.Join. Git tree paths are always "/"-separated, so
   140	// this uses the stdlib path package (never path/filepath, which would emit "\" on
   141	// Windows and corrupt tree keys). path.Join cleans separators, so base may be ""
   142	// (per-checkpoint-ref root), a clean dir ("a3/b2.../0"), or a trailing-slash dir
   143	// ("a3/b2.../"): checkpointSubtreePath("", "0", "metadata.json") == "0/metadata.json"
   144	// and checkpointSubtreePath("a3/b2.../", "0", "metadata.json") == "a3/b2.../0/metadata.json".

   146	func checkpointSubtreePath(base string, segs ...string) string {

   149			// git tree key. At the ref root the correct key is ""; for a non-empty
   150			// base, clean it to keep the trailing-slash-stripping behavior.
   151			if base == "" {
   152				return ""
   153			}
   154			return path.Clean(base)
   155		}
   156		return path.Join(append([]string{base}, segs...)...)

  554→ func (s *treeWriter) writeStandardCheckpointEntries(ctx context.Context, opts WriteOptions, basePath string, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) error {
  555→ 	// Read existing summary to get current session count
  556→ 	var existingSummary *CheckpointSummary
  557→ 	metadataPath := checkpointSubtreePath(basePath, paths.MetadataFileName)
  558→ 	if entry, exists := entries[metadataPath]; exists {
  559→ 		existing, err := s.readSummaryFromBlob(entry.Hash)
  560→ 		if err == nil {
  561→ 			existingSummary = existing
  562→ 		} else {
  563→ 			logging.Debug(ctx, "writeStandardCheckpointEntries: readSummaryFromBlob failed",
  564→ 				slog.String("metadata_path", metadataPath),
  565→ 				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
  566→ 		}
  567→ 	}
  568→ 
  569→ 	// Determine session index: reuse existing slot if session ID matches, otherwise append
  570→ 	sessionIndex := s.findSessionIndex(ctx, basePath, existingSummary, entries, opts.SessionID)
  571→ 
  572→ 	// Refuse if slot 0 already holds metadata for a DIFFERENT session ID.
  573→ 	// findSessionIndex only returns 0 when existingSummary is nil (fresh write)
  574→ 	// or when the summary claims slot 0 belongs to us — either way, the tree
  575→ 	// actually holding session-0 metadata for someone else is a corruption /
  576→ 	// stale-summary shape. Writing through it would overwrite data we don't
  577→ 	// know about. Bail instead of silently clobbering.
  578→ 	//
  579→ 	// We read and capture BEFORE writeSessionToSubdirectory clears the subtree,
  580→ 	// otherwise we'd only ever see our own write.

  337→ 	//

  340→ 	// extraction re-derives events from transcript offset 0 on every pass and

  343→ 	// re-enables double-reporting for exactly the long sessions a cap would

  347→ 	// i.e. every hook, including PostToolUse — because state is read and written
  348→ 	// whole. Measured JSON round-trip: 0 events / 106 B / 1.6us; 10 / 6.0 KB /
  349→ 	// 42us; 50 / 29.7 KB / 201us; 200 / 119 KB / 785us, i.e. ~594 B per event
  350→ 	// and sub-millisecond at any realistic N. The steady-state dedupe rebuild is
  351→ 	// cheap by comparison: 13us at 200 existing events.

  354→ 	// does need shrinking, the move is a narrower ledger — persist only the
  355→ 	// dedupe keys (~40 B/event) and keep the full events transient — not a
  356→ 	// truncation, which would break exactly-once.
  357→ 	SkillEvents []agent.SkillEvent `json:"skill_events,omitempty"`

  362→ 	// --amend` re-runs PostCommit with the SAME trailer checkpoint ID (an
  363→ 	// ACTIVE session re-condenses unconditionally), so without this ledger one
  364→ 	// logical commit is counted twice in both halves of the miss-rate ratio.

  366→ 	// retries cleanly; a crash between save and emit loses the row, which is

  368→ 	CommitCondensedSignalCheckpointID string `json:"commit_condensed_signal_checkpoint_id,omitempty"`

  372→ 	SessionTurnCount  int   `json:"session_turn_count,omitempty"`
  373→ 	ContextTokens     int   `json:"context_tokens,omitempty"`
  374→ 	ContextWindowSize int   `json:"context_window_size,omitempty"`

689	func handleLifecycleTurnEnd(ctx context.Context, ag agent.Agent, event *agent.Event) error {
   690		logCtx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(ctx, "lifecycle"), ag.Name())
   691		logging.Info(logCtx, "turn-end",
   692			slog.String("event", event.Type.String()),
   693			slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
   694			slog.String("session_ref", event.SessionRef),
   695			slog.String("model", event.Model),
   696		)
   697	
   698		sessionID := event.SessionID
   699		if sessionID == "" {
   700			sessionID = unknownSessionID
   701		}
   702	
   703		// Fill model from hint file if the agent didn't provide it on this hook
   704		if event.Model == "" && sessionID != unknownSessionID {
   705			if hint := strategy.LoadModelHint(ctx, sessionID); hint != "" {
   706				event.Model = hint
   707				logging.Debug(logCtx, "loaded model from hint file",
   708					slog.String("model", hint))
   709			}
   710		}
   711	
   712		transcriptRef := event.SessionRef
   713		if transcriptRef == "" {
   714			return errors.New("transcript file not specified")
   715		}
   716	
   717		// If agent implements TranscriptPreparer, materialize the transcript file.
   718		// This must run BEFORE fileExists: agents like OpenCode lazily fetch transcripts
   719		// via `opencode export`, so the file doesn't exist until PrepareTranscript creates it.
   720		// Claude Code's PrepareTranscript just flushes (always succeeds). Agents without
   721		// TranscriptPreparer (Gemini, Droid) are unaffected.
   722		_, prepareSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "prepare_and_validate_transcript")
   723		if preparer, ok := agent.AsTranscriptPreparer(ag); ok {
   724			if err := preparer.PrepareTranscript(ctx, transcriptRef); err != nil {
   725				logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to prepare transcript",
   726					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   727			}
   728		}
   729	
   730		if !fileExists(transcriptRef) {
   731			prepareSpan.RecordError(fmt.Errorf("transcript file not found: %s", transcriptRef))
   732			prepareSpan.End()
   733			return fmt.Errorf("transcript file not found: %s", transcriptRef)
   734		}
   735	
   736		// Early check: bail out quickly if the repo has no commits yet.
   737		// Return nil (not an error) so the hook exits 0 — agents treat non-zero
   738		// exit codes as hook failures. The user was already warned at session start.
   739		if repo, err := strategy.OpenRepository(ctx); err == nil {
   740			defer repo.Close()
   741			if strategy.IsEmptyRepository(repo) {
   742				prepareSpan.End()
   743				logging.Info(logCtx, "skipping checkpoint - will activate after first commit")
   744				return nil
   745			}
   746		}
   747		prepareSpan.End()
   748	
   749		// Create session metadata directory
   750		_, copySpan := perf.Start(ctx, "copy_transcript")
   751		// sessionDir is the repo-relative path that ends up in commit trailers and
   752		// in the checkpoint tree; sessionName is the same directory addressed from
   753		// the .entire root, which is what every read and write below uses.
   754		sessionDir := paths.SessionMetadataDirFromSessionID(sessionID)
   755		sessionName := sessionMetadataName(sessionID)
   756		entireRoot, err := entiredir.Open(ctx)
   757		if err != nil {
   758			copySpan.RecordError(err)
   759			copySpan.End()
   760			return fmt.Errorf("failed to open %s: %w", paths.EntireDir, err)
   761		}
   762		if err := osroot.MkdirAllNoSymlink(entireRoot, sessionName, 0o750); err != nil {
   763			copySpan.RecordError(err)
   764			copySpan.End()
   765			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create session directory: %w", err)
   766		}
   767	
   768		// Copy transcript to session directory
   769		transcriptData, err := ag.ReadTranscript(transcriptRef)
   770		if err != nil {
   771			copySpan.RecordError(err)
   772			copySpan.End()
   773			return fmt.Errorf("failed to read transcript: %w", err)
   774		}
   775		// Sanitize before writing: this copy is what the shadow-branch walk blobs and
   776		// redacts on every Stop. See agent.TranscriptSanitizer for why order matters.
   777		// The agent's own rollout is untouched.
   778		storedTranscript := agent.SanitizeTranscriptForStorage(ag, transcriptData)
   779		logFile := sessionName + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileName
   780		if err := entiredir.WriteFile(entireRoot, logFile, storedTranscript, 0o600); err != nil {
   781			copySpan.RecordError(err)
   782			copySpan.End()
   783			return fmt.Errorf("failed to write transcript: %w", err)
   784		}
   785		logging.Debug(logCtx, "copied transcript",
   786			slog.String("path", sessionDir+"/"+paths.TranscriptFileName),
   787			slog.Int("raw_bytes", len(transcriptData)),
   788			slog.Int("stored_bytes", len(storedTranscript)))
   789		copySpan.End()
   790	
   791		// Load pre-prompt state (captured on TurnStart)
   792		_, extractSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "extract_metadata")
   793		preState, err := LoadPrePromptState(ctx, sessionID)
   794		if err != nil {
   795			logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to load pre-prompt state",
   796				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   797		}
   798	
   799		// Determine transcript offset
   800		transcriptOffset := resolveTranscriptOffset(ctx, preState, sessionID)
   801	
   802		// Backfill prompt.txt from transcript when prompt data is missing.
   803		// This handles agents whose exec mode doesn't fire UserPromptSubmit (e.g., Factory AI
   804		// Droid). The transcript is the source of truth — if ExtractPrompts returns nothing,
   805		// there genuinely were no prompts. We track whether backfill occurred so we can
   806		// update session state after SaveStep (which may reinitialize state).
   807		var backfilledPrompt string
   808		promptName := sessionName + "/" + paths.PromptFileName
   809		existingPrompt, readPromptErr := entiredir.ReadFile(entireRoot, promptName)
   810		if readPromptErr != nil && !errors.Is(readPromptErr, fs.ErrNotExist) {
   811			logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to read prompt.txt, skipping backfill",
   812				slog.String("error", readPromptErr.Error()))
   813		} else if len(existingPrompt) == 0 {
   814			if extractor, ok := agent.AsPromptExtractor(ag); ok {
   815				prompts, extractErr := extractor.ExtractPrompts(transcriptRef, transcriptOffset)
   816				if extractErr != nil {
   817					logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to extract prompts from transcript",
   818						slog.String("error", extractErr.Error()))
   819				} else if len(prompts) > 0 {
   820					content := strings.Join(prompts, "\n\n---\n\n")
   821					if writeErr := entiredir.WriteFile(entireRoot, promptName, []byte(content), 0o600); writeErr != nil {
   822						logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to backfill prompt.txt from transcript",
   823							slog.String("error", writeErr.Error()))
   824					} else {
   825						logging.Debug(logCtx, "backfilled prompt.txt from transcript",
   826							slog.Int("prompt_count", len(prompts)))
   827						backfilledPrompt = prompts[len(prompts)-1]
   828					}
   829				}
   830			}

   280	func detectFileChanges(ctx context.Context, previouslyUntracked []string, statusFn func(context.Context, *git.Repository) (git.Status, error)) (*FileChanges, error) {
   281		repo, err := openRepository(ctx)
   282		if err != nil {
   283			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open repository: %w", err)
   284		}
   285		defer repo.Close()

   287		status, err := statusFn(ctx, repo)
   288		if err != nil {
   289			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get status: %w", err)
   290		}
   291	
   292		// Build set of pre-existing untracked files for quick lookup
   293		var preExisting map[string]bool
   294		if previouslyUntracked != nil {
   295			preExisting = make(map[string]bool, len(previouslyUntracked))
   296			for _, f := range previouslyUntracked {
   297				preExisting[f] = true
   298			}
   299		}
   300	
   301		var changes FileChanges
   302		for file, st := range status {
   303			if shouldIgnoreSessionTrackingPath(file) {
   304				continue
   305			}
   306	
   307			switch {
   308			case st.Worktree == git.Untracked:
   309				if preExisting != nil {
   310					if !preExisting[file] {
   311						changes.New = append(changes.New, file)
   312					}
   313				} else {
   314					changes.New = append(changes.New, file)
   315				}
   316			case st.Worktree == git.Deleted || st.Staging == git.Deleted:
   317				changes.Deleted = append(changes.Deleted, file)
   318			case st.Worktree == git.Modified || st.Staging == git.Modified ||
   319				st.Worktree == git.Added || st.Staging == git.Added:
   320				changes.Modified = append(changes.Modified, file)
   321			}
   322		}
   323	
   324		return &changes, nil
   325	}

   327	// filterToUncommittedFiles removes files from the list that are already committed to HEAD
   328	// with matching content. This prevents re-adding files that an agent committed mid-turn
   329	// (already condensed by PostCommit) back to FilesTouched via SaveStep. Files not in
   330	// HEAD or with different content in the working tree are kept. Fails open: if any git
   331	// operation errors, returns the original list unchanged.
   332	func filterToUncommittedFiles(ctx context.Context, files []string, repoRoot string) []string {
   333		if len(files) == 0 {
   334			return files
   335		}
   336	
   337		repo, err := openRepository(ctx)
   338		if err != nil {
   339			return files // fail open
   340		}
   341		defer repo.Close()
   342	
   343		head, err := repo.Head()
   344		if err != nil {
   345			return files // fail open (empty repo, detached HEAD, etc.)
   346		}
   347	
   348		commit, err := repo.CommitObject(head.Hash())
   349		if err != nil {
   350			return files // fail open
   351		}
   352	
   353		headTree, err := commit.Tree()
   354		if err != nil {
   355			return files // fail open
   356		}
   357	
   358		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "filter-uncommitted")
   359	
   360		var result []string
   361		for _, relPath := range files {
   362			headFile, err := headTree.File(relPath)
   363			if err != nil {
   364				// File not in HEAD — it's uncommitted
   365				logging.Debug(logCtx, "file not in HEAD tree, keeping",
   366					slog.String("file", relPath),
   367					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   368				result = append(result, relPath)
   369				continue
   370			}
   371	
   372			// File is in HEAD — compare content with working tree, through the
   373			// worktree's shared root. relPath comes from git, so it is already the
   374			// coordinate the root reads in.
   375			workingContent, ok := readWorktreeFileSafely(repoRoot, relPath)
   376			if !ok {
   377				// Can't read working tree file (deleted?) — keep it
   378				result = append(result, relPath)
   379				continue
   380			}
   381	
   382			headContent, err := headFile.Contents()
   383			if err != nil {
   384				result = append(result, relPath)
   385				continue
   386			}
   387	
   388			if string(workingContent) != headContent {
   389				// Working tree differs from HEAD — uncommitted changes
   390				result = append(result, relPath)
   391			}
   392			// else: content matches HEAD — already committed, skip
   393		}
   394	
   395		return result
   396	}

1	// hook_registry.go provides hook command registration for agents.
     2	// The lifecycle dispatcher (DispatchLifecycleEvent) handles all lifecycle events.
     3	// PostTodo is the only hook that's handled directly (not via lifecycle dispatcher).
     4	package cli
     5	
     6	import (
     7		"context"
     8		"errors"
     9		"fmt"
    10		"io"
    11		"log/slog"
    12		"strings"
    13	
    14		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent"
    15		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode"
    16		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/geminicli"
    17		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/types"
    18		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpointpolicy"
    19		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo"
    20		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
    21		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths"
    22		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/settings"
    23		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy"
    24		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/telemetry"
    25		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck"
    26		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo"
    27		"github.com/entireio/cli/perf"
    28	
    29		"github.com/spf13/cobra"
    30	)
    31	
    32	// currentHookAgentName stores the agent name for the currently executing hook.
    33	// Set by newAgentHookVerbCmdWithLogging before calling the handler.
    34	// This allows handlers to know which agent invoked the hook without guessing.
    35	var currentHookAgentName types.AgentName
    36	
    37	// GetCurrentHookAgent returns the agent for the currently executing hook.
    38	// Returns the agent based on the hook command structure (e.g., "entire hooks claude-code ...")
    39	// rather than guessing from directory presence.
    40	// Falls back to GetAgent() if not in a hook context.
    41	func GetCurrentHookAgent() (agent.Agent, error) {
    42		if currentHookAgentName == "" {
    43			return nil, errors.New("not in a hook context: agent name not set")
    44		}
    45	
    46		ag, err := agent.Get(currentHookAgentName)
    47		if err != nil {
    48			return nil, fmt.Errorf("getting hook agent %q: %w", currentHookAgentName, err)
    49		}
    50		return ag, nil
    51	}
    52	
    53	// newAgentHooksCmd creates a hooks subcommand for an agent that implements HookSupport.
    54	// It dynamically creates subcommands for each hook the agent supports.
    55	func newAgentHooksCmd(agentName types.AgentName, handler agent.HookSupport) *cobra.Command {
    56		cmd := &cobra.Command{
    57			Use:    string(agentName),
    58			Short:  handler.Description() + " hook handlers",
    59			Hidden: true,
    60			PersistentPreRun: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) {
    61				// withHookSession scans session state and loads redactors, so it must
    62				// not run in a repo that never enabled Entire. Same fail-closed gate
    63				// the git-hook tree applies before its own call.
    64				if !settings.IsSetUpAndEnabled(cmd.Context()) {
    65					return
    66				}
    67				// Cobra invokes this PersistentPreRun with the leaf command, so
    68				// SetContext hands the session-stamped context straight to the
    69				// hook verb's RunE via cmd.Context().
    70				cmd.SetContext(withHookSession(cmd.Context()))
    71			},
    72		}
    73	
    74		for _, hookName := range handler.HookNames() {
    75			cmd.AddCommand(newAgentHookVerbCmdWithLogging(agentName, hookName))
    76		}
    77	
    78		return cmd
    79	}
    80	
    81	// getHookType returns the hook type based on the hook name.
    82	// Returns "subagent" for task-related hooks (pre-task, post-task, post-todo,
    83	// subagent-stop), "tool" for tool-related hooks (before-tool, after-tool),
    84	// "agent" for all other agent hooks.
    85	func getHookType(hookName string) string {
    86		switch hookName {
    87		case claudecode.HookNamePreTask, claudecode.HookNamePostTask, claudecode.HookNamePostTodo,
    88			claudecode.HookNameSubagentStop:
    89			return "subagent"
    90		case geminicli.HookNameBeforeTool, geminicli.HookNameAfterTool:
    91			return "tool"
    92		default:
    93			return "agent"
    94		}
    95	}
    96	
    97	// executeAgentHook runs the core hook execution logic for a given agent and hook name.
    98	// It handles git repo checks, enabled checks, the hook logging context, event
    99	// parsing, and lifecycle dispatch.
   100	// Used by both the registered subcommand path and the RunE fallback for external agents.
   101	// When stampSession is true, it attaches the hook session context itself (used by
   102	// the RunE fallback since it doesn't go through PersistentPreRun). Built-in agent
   103	// subcommands pass false since their parent command's PersistentPreRun already
   104	// did it.
   105	func executeAgentHook(cmd *cobra.Command, agentName types.AgentName, hookName string, stampSession bool) error {
   106		// Skip silently if not in a git repository - hooks shouldn't prevent the agent from working
   107		worktreeRoot, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(cmd.Context())
   108		if err != nil {
   109			return nil
   110		}
   111	
   112		// Skip if Entire is not set up and enabled. This must fail closed: any
   113		// settings read error (missing file, corrupted JSON, transient I/O
   114		// failure) is treated as disabled so a hook never silently falls through
   115		// to full lifecycle work just because settings couldn't be read. Using
   116		// IsEnabled here previously failed OPEN on error (`err == nil && !enabled`
   117		// only short-circuits when the read succeeded), which meant a corrupted
   118		// or unreadable settings file made every hook invocation pay the full
   119		// dispatch cost instead of exiting fast (#524).
   120		// settings.IsSetUpAndEnabled is the same fail-closed gate the git hooks
   121		// use (see PersistentPreRun in hooks_git_cmd.go).
   122		if !settings.IsSetUpAndEnabled(cmd.Context()) {
   123			return nil
   124		}
   125	
   126		if stampSession {
   127			cmd.SetContext(withHookSession(cmd.Context()))
   128		}
   129	
   130		// Initialize logging context with agent name
   131		ctx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(cmd.Context(), "hooks"), agentName)
   132	
   133		// Strategy name for logging
   134		strategyName := strategy.StrategyNameManualCommit
   135	
   136		hookType := getHookType(hookName)
   137	
   138		// Start root perf span — child spans in lifecycle handlers and strategy
   139		// methods will automatically nest under this span.
   140		ctx, span := perf.Start(ctx, hookName,
   141			slog.String("hook_type", hookType))
   142		defer span.End()
   143	
   144		logging.Debug(ctx, "hook invoked",
   145			slog.String("hook", hookName),
   146			slog.String("hook_type", hookType),
   147			slog.String("strategy", strategyName),
   148		)
   149	
   150		// Set the current hook agent so handlers can retrieve it
   151		currentHookAgentName = agentName
   152		defer func() { currentHookAgentName = "" }()
   153	
   154		// Use the lifecycle dispatcher for all hooks
   155		var hookErr error
   156		ag, agentErr := agent.Get(agentName)
   157		if agentErr != nil {
   158			return fmt.Errorf("failed to get agent %q: %w", agentName, agentErr)
   159		}
   160	
   161		handler, ok := agent.AsHookSupport(ag)
   162		if !ok {
   163			return fmt.Errorf("agent %q does not support hooks", agentName)
   164		}
   165	
   166		// Use cmd.InOrStdin() to support testing with cmd.SetIn()
   167		event, parseErr := handler.ParseHookEvent(ctx, hookName, cmd.InOrStdin())
   168		if parseErr != nil {
   169			return fmt.Errorf("failed to parse hook event: %w", parseErr)
   170		}
   171	
   172		claudePostTodoCheckpointHook := event == nil && agentName == agent.AgentNameClaudeCode && hookName == claudecode.HookNamePostTodo
   173		eventType := agent.EventType(0)
   174	
   175		if event != nil {
   176			// Cross-agent guard: when Cursor IDE invokes a hook configured under
   177			// .claude/settings.json (because .cursor/hooks.json is missing), the
   178			// hook payload's transcript_path proves the session belongs to Cursor.
   179			// Skip dispatch so the session isn't claimed for the wrong agent (#1262).
   180			if shouldSkipForwardedHook(ctx, ag, event) {
   181				logging.Debug(ctx, "skipping forwarded hook: transcript belongs to another agent",
   182					slog.String("hook", hookName),
   183					slog.String("firing_agent", string(agentName)),
   184					slog.String("session_ref", event.SessionRef),
   185				)
   186				return nil
   187			}
   188			eventType = event.Type
   189		}
   190	
   191		if eventType == agent.SessionStart {
   192			skipSessionStart, err := shouldSkipSessionStartForPolicy(ctx, cmd.ErrOrStderr(), agentName, ag, worktreeRoot)
   193			if err != nil {
   194				span.RecordError(err)
   195				return err
   196			}
   197			if skipSessionStart {
   198				return nil
   199			}
   200		} else if hookWritesCheckpointData(eventType, claudePostTodoCheckpointHook) {
   201			writeHook := agentWriteHookLabel(eventType, claudePostTodoCheckpointHook)
   202			if err := rejectUnsupportedCheckpointWritePolicy(ctx, cmd.ErrOrStderr(), agentName, writeHook, worktreeRoot); err != nil {
   203				span.RecordError(err)
   204				return err
   205			}
   206		}
   207	
   208		if event != nil {
   209			// Lifecycle event — use the generic dispatcher
   210			hookErr = DispatchLifecycleEvent(ctx, ag, event)
   211		} else if claudePostTodoCheckpointHook {
   212			// PostTodo is Claude-specific: creates incremental checkpoints during subagent execution
   213			hookErr = handleClaudeCodePostTodo(ctx)
   214		}
   215		// Other pass-through hooks (nil event, no special handling) are no-ops
   216	
   217		span.RecordError(hookErr)
   218		return hookErr
   219	}
   220	
   221	func agentHookPolicy(ctx context.Context, worktreeRoot string) (checkpointpolicy.Policy, error) {
   222		repo, err := gitrepo.OpenPath(worktreeRoot)
   223		if err != nil {
   224			return checkpointpolicy.Policy{}, unreadableCheckpointPolicyError(err)
   225		}
   226		defer repo.Close()
   227	
   228		return checkpointPolicyForCheckpointData(ctx, repo)
   229	}

    60			PersistentPreRun: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) {

    63				// the git-hook tree applies before its own call.
    64				if !settings.IsSetUpAndEnabled(cmd.Context()) {

    68				// SetContext hands the session-stamped context straight to the

    81	// getHookType returns the hook type based on the hook name.

    83	// subagent-stop), "tool" for tool-related hooks (before-tool, after-tool),
    84	// "agent" for all other agent hooks.
    85	func getHookType(hookName string) string {

    97	// executeAgentHook runs the core hook execution logic for a given agent and hook name.

    99	// parsing, and lifecycle dispatch.

   102	// the RunE fallback since it doesn't go through PersistentPreRun). Built-in agent
   103	// subcommands pass false since their parent command's PersistentPreRun already
   104	// did it.

   110		}

   116		// IsEnabled here previously failed OPEN on error (`err == nil && !enabled`

   118		// or unreadable settings file made every hook invocation pay the full
   119		// dispatch cost instead of exiting fast (#524).

   121		// use (see PersistentPreRun in hooks_git_cmd.go).
   122		if !settings.IsSetUpAndEnabled(cmd.Context()) {
   123			return nil
   124		}

   126		if stampSession {
   127			cmd.SetContext(withHookSession(cmd.Context()))
   128		}
   129	
   130		// Initialize logging context with agent name
   131		ctx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(cmd.Context(), "hooks"), agentName)
   132	
   133		// Strategy name for logging
   134		strategyName := strategy.StrategyNameManualCommit
   135	
   136		hookType := getHookType(hookName)
   137	
   138		// Start root perf span — child spans in lifecycle handlers and strategy
   139		// methods will automatically nest under this span.
   140		ctx, span := perf.Start(ctx, hookName,
   141			slog.String("hook_type", hookType))
   142		defer span.End()
   143	
   144		logging.Debug(ctx, "hook invoked",
   145			slog.String("hook", hookName),
   146			slog.String("hook_type", hookType),
   147			slog.String("strategy", strategyName),
   148		)

   150		// Set the current hook agent so handlers can retrieve it
   151		currentHookAgentName = agentName
   152		defer func() { currentHookAgentName = "" }()

   159		}

   164		}

   167		event, parseErr := handler.ParseHookEvent(ctx, hookName, cmd.InOrStdin())
   168		if parseErr != nil {
   169			return fmt.Errorf("failed to parse hook event: %w", parseErr)
   170		}
   171	
   172		claudePostTodoCheckpointHook := event == nil && agentName == agent.AgentNameClaudeCode && hookName == claudecode.HookNamePostTodo
   173		eventType := agent.EventType(0)
   174	
   175		if event != nil {
   176			// Cross-agent guard: when Cursor IDE invokes a hook configured under
   177			// .claude/settings.json (because .cursor/hooks.json is missing), the
   178			// hook payload's transcript_path proves the session belongs to Cursor.
   179			// Skip dispatch so the session isn't claimed for the wrong agent (#1262).
   180			if shouldSkipForwardedHook(ctx, ag, event) {
   181				logging.Debug(ctx, "skipping forwarded hook: transcript belongs to another agent",
   182					slog.String("hook", hookName),
   183					slog.String("firing_agent", string(agentName)),
   184					slog.String("session_ref", event.SessionRef),
   185				)
   186				return nil
   187			}
   188			eventType = event.Type
   189		}
   190	
   191		if eventType == agent.SessionStart {
   192			skipSessionStart, err := shouldSkipSessionStartForPolicy(ctx, cmd.ErrOrStderr(), agentName, ag, worktreeRoot)
   193			if err != nil {
   194				span.RecordError(err)
   195				return err
   196			}
   197			if skipSessionStart {
   198				return nil
   199			}

   204				return err
   205			}
   206		}

   210			hookErr = DispatchLifecycleEvent(ctx, ag, event)
   211		} else if claudePostTodoCheckpointHook {
   212			// PostTodo is Claude-specific: creates incremental checkpoints during subagent execution
   213			hookErr = handleClaudeCodePostTodo(ctx)
   214		}

   216	
   217		span.RecordError(hookErr)
   218		return hookErr
   219	}
   220	
   221	func agentHookPolicy(ctx context.Context, worktreeRoot string) (checkpointpolicy.Policy, error) {
   222		repo, err := gitrepo.OpenPath(worktreeRoot)
   223		if err != nil {
   224			return checkpointpolicy.Policy{}, unreadableCheckpointPolicyError(err)
   225		}
   226		defer repo.Close()

   228		return checkpointPolicyForCheckpointData(ctx, repo)

    13	)
    14	
    15	var (
    16		registryMu sync.RWMutex
    17		registry   = make(map[types.AgentName]Factory)
    18	)
    19	
    20	// Factory creates a new agent instance
    21	type Factory func() Agent
    22	
    23	// Register adds an agent factory to the registry.
    24	// Called from init() in each agent implementation.
    25	func Register(name types.AgentName, factory Factory) {
    26		registryMu.Lock()
    27		defer registryMu.Unlock()
    28		registry[name] = factory
    29	}
    30	
    31	// Get retrieves an agent by name.
    32	//
    33	
    34	func Get(name types.AgentName) (Agent, error) {
    35		registryMu.RLock()
    36		defer registryMu.RUnlock()
    37	
    38		factory, ok := registry[name]
    39		if !ok {
    40			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown agent: %s (available: %v)", name, List())
    41		}
    42		return factory(), nil
    43	}
    44	
    45	// List returns all registered agent names in sorted order.
    46	func List() []types.AgentName {
    47		registryMu.RLock()
    48		defer registryMu.RUnlock()
    49	
    50		names := make([]types.AgentName, 0, len(registry))
    51		for name := range registry {
    52			names = append(names, name)
    53		}
    54		slices.Sort(names)
    55		return names
    56	}
    57	
    58	// StringList returns user-facing agent names, excluding test-only agents.
    59	func StringList() []string {
    60		registryMu.RLock()
    61		defer registryMu.RUnlock()
    62	
    63		names := make([]string, 0, len(registry))
    64		for name, factory := range registry {
    65			if to, ok := factory().(TestOnly); ok && to.IsTestOnly() {
    66				continue
    67			}
    68			names = append(names, string(name))
    69		}
    70		slices.Sort(names)
    71		return names
    72	}
    73	
    74	// DetectAll returns all agents whose DetectPresence reports true.
    75	// Agents are checked in sorted name order (via List()) for deterministic results.
    76	// Returns an empty slice when no agent is detected.
    77	func DetectAll(ctx context.Context) []Agent {
    78		names := List() // sorted, lock-safe
    79	
    80		var detected []Agent
    81		for _, name := range names {
    82			ag, err := Get(name)
    83			if err != nil {
    84				continue
    85			}
    86			if present, err := ag.DetectPresence(ctx); err == nil && present {
    87				detected = append(detected, ag)
    88			}
    89		}
    90		return detected
    91	}
    92	
    93	// AgentForTranscriptPath returns the registered agent whose session directory
    94	// for repoPath contains the given transcript path. Used to disambiguate which
    95	// agent owns a session when multiple agents' hooks fire for the same session
    96	// ID — a Cursor transcript path uniquely identifies a Cursor session even
    97	// when Claude Code's hook is the one firing.
    98	//
    99	// Returns (nil, false) if transcriptPath is empty, no agent claims it, or any
   100	// registry lookup fails. Match is by directory prefix (with a separator) so
   101	// "/x/.claude/projects/abc.jsonl" doesn't accidentally match an agent rooted
   102	// at "/x/.claude/projects/ab".
   103	//
   104	//nolint:revive // AgentForTranscriptPath: stutter is intentional for package callers (agent.AgentForTranscriptPath reads naturally)
   105	func AgentForTranscriptPath(transcriptPath, repoPath string) (Agent, bool) {
   106		if transcriptPath == "" {
   107			return nil, false
   108		}
   109		abs, err := filepath.Abs(transcriptPath)
   110		if err != nil {
   111			abs = transcriptPath
   112		}
   113		for _, name := range List() {
   114			ag, err := Get(name)
   115			if err != nil {
   116				continue
   117			}
   118			dir, err := ag.GetSessionDir(repoPath)
   119			if err != nil || dir == "" {
   120				continue
   121			}
   122			dirAbs, err := filepath.Abs(dir)
   123			if err != nil {
   124				dirAbs = dir
   125			}

content.text:
At the capture layer, the important mental model is “two witnesses”:

1. The transcript identifies agent-intended edits, prompts, tool/subagent activity, model, skills, and tokens.
2. Git status identifies the actual working-tree delta, including edits made through tools the adapter does not recognize.

Turn-end merges those witnesses, filters infrastructure/out-of-repo paths, and snapshots only uncommitted work. This is why capture can degrade gracefully when one source is incomplete without silently treating every pre-existing untracked file as agent-created.

   468	func runCodeSearch(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, opts codeSearchOpts) error {
   469		if opts.query == "" {
   470			return errors.New("query required for code search. Usage: entire search --code <query>")
   471		}
   472	
   473		w := cmd.OutOrStdout()
   474		textOutput := !opts.jsonOutput && interactive.IsTerminalWriter(w)
   475	
   476		// Text output shows up to maxCodeSearchFiles files with a few matches
   477		// each, so fetch a deeper result set than the default --limit (which is
   478		// tuned for flat JSON output) unless the user asked for a specific limit.
   479		if textOutput && !opts.limitExplicit {
   480			opts.limit = codeSearchTextFetchLimit
   481		}
   482	
   483		// Always fan out via searchAllCells — it fetches the repo index,
   484		// resolves slugs to ULIDs, and handles single- vs multi-jurisdiction.
   485		// searchAllCells emits the outcome telemetry itself, so the TUI's code
   486		// tab (which calls it directly) is covered too.
   487		resp, err := searchAllCells(ctx, opts)
   488		if err != nil {
   489			return err
   490		}

   492		if !textOutput {
   493			return writeCodeSearchJSON(w, resp)
   494		}

   496		writeCodeSearchText(w, resp, newStatusStyles(w), opts.caseSensitive)

   500	// searchAllCells fans out code search across all cells that host the user's
   501	// repos, using the shared cell-routing foundation (cell_fanout.go):
   502	//  1. List repos from the control plane (entire-core) to discover cells
   503	//  2. Resolve repo slug filters to ULIDs
   504	//  3. Group by cell and resolve baseURLs via the shared helpers
   505	//  4. Fan out via fanOutCells with per-cell codesearch.Search calls
   506	//  5. Merge results (sorted by score, capped to limit)

   508	// Every call emits one cli_search_completed outcome — this is the code-search
   509	// seam shared by the one-shot --code path and the TUI's code tab, so
   510	// instrumenting here covers both by construction.
   511	func searchAllCells(ctx context.Context, opts codeSearchOpts) (resp *codesearch.SearchResponse, err error) {
   512		start := time.Now()
   513		defer func() {
   514			var result searchOutcomeResult
   515			if resp != nil {
   516				result = searchOutcomeResult{
   517					count:              len(resp.Results),
   518					coverageIncomplete: len(resp.FailedJurisdictions) > 0 || len(resp.SkippedRepos) > 0,
   519				}
   520			}
   521			emitSearchOutcome(ctx, opts.commandPath, telemetry.SearchModeCode, result, time.Since(start), err)
   522		}()
   523		// Step 1: Get repos index from the control plane. *coreapi.Client
   524		// satisfies cellCoreClient (passed to resolveCellBaseURLs below as such).
   525		coreClient, err := coreapi.New()
   526		if err != nil {
   527			if errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn) {
   528				return nil, loginHintErr(err)
   529			}
   530			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolving control-plane client: %w", err)
   531		}
   532	
   533		reposCtx, reposCancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
   534		defer reposCancel()
   535	
   536		repoIndex, err := coreClient.ListRepos(reposCtx, coreapi.ListReposParams{})
   537		if err != nil {
   538			return nil, fmt.Errorf("listing repos for cell discovery: %w", err)
   539		}
   540	
   541		if repoIndex.Truncated {
   542			logging.Warn(ctx, "repo index truncated; code search results may be incomplete")
   543		}
   544	
   545		// Step 2: Resolve repo slug filters to ULIDs and narrow to matching cells.
   546		indexRepos := repoIndex.Repos
   547		if len(opts.repoFilters) > 0 {
   548			resolved, filtered := resolveRepoFilters(opts.repoFilters, repoIndex.Repos)
   549			if len(resolved) == 0 {
   550				hint := ""
   551				if repoIndex.Truncated {
   552					hint = " (repo index was truncated — the repo may exist but was not included)"
   553				}
   554				return nil, fmt.Errorf("no matching repositories found for filter %q%s", opts.repoFilters, hint)
   555			}
   556			opts.resolvedRepoIDs = resolved
   557			indexRepos = filtered
   558		}
   559	
   560		// Step 3: Group repos by cell and resolve baseURLs via shared helpers.
   561		// Routes by routedRepoPlacement like semantic search (see its doc). The
   562		// CLI is deliberately ahead of the BFF's code-search.ts here, which stays
   563		// canonical until its code-read chain (/symbols, /usages, file viewer)
   564		// flips with it — identical behavior until then, and core electing
   565		// divergent primaries is gated on that web flip (tracked on ENT-1776).

   567		cells, skippedRepos := groupReposByCell(indexRepos)
   568		skippedRepos = reportableSkippedRepos(ctx, pinned, len(cells), skippedRepos)
   569		if len(cells) == 0 {
   570			return &codesearch.SearchResponse{SkippedRepos: skippedRepos}, nil
   571		}
   572		resolveCellBaseURLs(ctx, coreClient, cells)
   573	
   574		// Step 4: Fan out via the shared fanOutCells helper.
   575		// Each cell gets the full limit for single-cell, or 2x for multi-cell so
   576		// the merge sees enough candidates from every region for proper global
   577		// ranking. mergeSearchResults applies the final cap.
   578		perCellLimit := opts.limit
   579		if len(cells) > 1 && perCellLimit > 0 {
   580			perCellLimit *= 2
   581		}
   582		results, err := fanOutCells(ctx, opts.insecureHTTP, codeSearchCellTimeout, cells, func(ctx context.Context, group cellGroup, client *api.Client) (*codesearch.SearchResponse, error) {
   583			var repoIDs []string
   584			if len(opts.resolvedRepoIDs) > 0 {
   585				repoIDs = group.repoIDs
   586			}
   587			req := codesearch.SearchRequest{
   588				Query:         opts.query,
   589				Repos:         repoIDs,
   590				CaseSensitive: opts.caseSensitive,
   591			}
   592			if perCellLimit > 0 {
   593				req.MaxResults = perCellLimit
   594			}
   595			return codesearch.Search(ctx, client, req)
   596		})
   597		if err != nil {
   598			if errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn) {
   599				return nil, loginHintErr(err)
   600			}
   601			return nil, fmt.Errorf("code search: %w", err)
   602		}
   603	
   604		merged, err := mergeSearchResults(ctx, opts.limit, results)
   605		if err != nil {
   606			return nil, err
   607		}
   608		merged.SkippedRepos = skippedRepos
   609		return merged, nil
   610	}

   370	type codeSearchOpts struct {
   371		query           string
   372		repoFilters     []string
   373		resolvedRepoIDs []string // ULIDs resolved from repoFilters via repo index
   374		limit           int
   375		limitExplicit   bool // user passed --limit; don't override for text display
   376		caseSensitive   bool
   377		jsonOutput      bool
   378		insecureHTTP    bool
   379		// commandPath is the invoking cobra command path, carried here because

   385	// extractInlineRepoFilters extracts only repo: prefixed filters from a query
   386	// string, returning the remaining query text and the list of repo values.
   387	// Unlike search.ParseSearchInput, this does NOT consume author:, date:, or
   388	// branch: tokens — those are checkpoint-search-only and should be treated as
   389	// literal text in code search queries.
   390	func extractInlineRepoFilters(query string) (remaining string, repos []string) {
   391		var kept []string
   392		for _, part := range strings.Fields(query) {
   393			if strings.HasPrefix(part, "repo:") {
   394				// Split comma-separated values (repo:a,b → [a, b]), matching
   395				// checkpoint search's parseListFilter behavior. Trim quotes so
   396				// repo:"gh/owner/repo" works like the unquoted form.
   397				for _, v := range strings.Split(part[5:], ",") {
   398					v = strings.Trim(v, `"'`)
   399					if v != "" {
   400						repos = append(repos, v)
   401					}
   402				}
   403			} else {
   404				kept = append(kept, part)
   405			}
   406		}
   407		return strings.Join(kept, " "), repos
   408	}

   410	// hasAllReposFilter returns true if repos contains the wildcard "*" filter.

   413			if r == search.AllReposFilter {
   414				return true
   415			}

   417		return false

   431	// buildCodeSearchOpts returns a *codeSearchOpts pre-populated with repo filters.
   432	// It honors --repo, --all-repos, and inline repo: filters from the command line;
   433	// when none are specified, it falls back to the current git origin slug.
   434	func buildCodeSearchOpts(ctx context.Context, commandPath, owner, repoName string, repos []string, allRepos, insecureHTTP bool) *codeSearchOpts {
   435		var repoFilters []string
   436		switch {
   437		case allRepos:
   438			// nil repoFilters → searchAllCells searches all repos
   439		case len(repos) > 0:
   440			repoFilters = repos
   441		default:
   442			// Use forge-prefixed slug (e.g. "et/proj/repo") so Entire forge
   443			// repos match the index FullName. Falls back to owner/repo for
   444			// GitHub repos (gh/ prefix is stripped by resolveRepoFilters).
   445			if slug := currentRepoSlugWithForge(ctx); slug != "" {
   446				repoFilters = []string{slug}
   447			} else {
   448				repoFilters = []string{owner + "/" + repoName}
   449			}
   450		}
   451		return &codeSearchOpts{
   452			repoFilters:  repoFilters,
   453			limit:        search.DefaultLimit,
   454			insecureHTTP: insecureHTTP,
   455			commandPath:  commandPath,

   459	// codeSearchCellTimeout bounds each per-cell search call (token exchange + API).
   460	const codeSearchCellTimeout = 30 * time.Second
   461	
   462	// runCodeSearch handles the --code flag path: search code content via peregrine.
   463	//
   464	// When a repo filter is specified, it routes to that repo's owning cell.
   465	// Without a filter, it fans out across all cells that host the user's repos
   466	// (mirroring the BFF's /api/v1/stream endpoint): list repos from the control
   467	// plane, group by cell/jurisdiction, search each cell in parallel, merge.
   468	func runCodeSearch(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, opts codeSearchOpts) error {
   469		if opts.query == "" {
   470			return errors.New("query required for code search. Usage: entire search --code <query>")
   471		}
   472	
   473		w := cmd.OutOrStdout()
   474		textOutput := !opts.jsonOutput && interactive.IsTerminalWriter(w)
   475	
   476		// Text output shows up to maxCodeSearchFiles files with a few matches
   477		// each, so fetch a deeper result set than the default --limit (which is
   478		// tuned for flat JSON output) unless the user asked for a specific limit.
   479		if textOutput && !opts.limitExplicit {
   480			opts.limit = codeSearchTextFetchLimit
   481		}
   482	
   483		// Always fan out via searchAllCells — it fetches the repo index,
   484		// resolves slugs to ULIDs, and handles single- vs multi-jurisdiction.
   485		// searchAllCells emits the outcome telemetry itself, so the TUI's code
   486		// tab (which calls it directly) is covered too.
   487		resp, err := searchAllCells(ctx, opts)
   488		if err != nil {
   489			return err
   490		}
   491	
   492		if !textOutput {
   493			return writeCodeSearchJSON(w, resp)
   494		}
   495	
   496		writeCodeSearchText(w, resp, newStatusStyles(w), opts.caseSensitive)
   497		return nil
   498	}
   499	
   500	// searchAllCells fans out code search across all cells that host the user's
   501	// repos, using the shared cell-routing foundation (cell_fanout.go):
   502	//  1. List repos from the control plane (entire-core) to discover cells
   503	//  2. Resolve repo slug filters to ULIDs
   504	//  3. Group by cell and resolve baseURLs via the shared helpers
   505	//  4. Fan out via fanOutCells with per-cell codesearch.Search calls
   506	//  5. Merge results (sorted by score, capped to limit)
   507	//
   508	// Every call emits one cli_search_completed outcome — this is the code-search
   509	// seam shared by the one-shot --code path and the TUI's code tab, so
   510	// instrumenting here covers both by construction.
   511	func searchAllCells(ctx context.Context, opts codeSearchOpts) (resp *codesearch.SearchResponse, err error) {
   512		start := time.Now()
   513		defer func() {
   514			var result searchOutcomeResult
   515			if resp != nil {
   516				result = searchOutcomeResult{
   517					count:              len(resp.Results),
   518					coverageIncomplete: len(resp.FailedJurisdictions) > 0 || len(resp.SkippedRepos) > 0,
   519				}
   520			}
   521			emitSearchOutcome(ctx, opts.commandPath, telemetry.SearchModeCode, result, time.Since(start), err)
   522		}()
   523		// Step 1: Get repos index from the control plane. *coreapi.Client
   524		// satisfies cellCoreClient (passed to resolveCellBaseURLs below as such).
   525		coreClient, err := coreapi.New()
   526		if err != nil {
   527			if errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn) {
   528				return nil, loginHintErr(err)
   529			}
   530			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolving control-plane client: %w", err)
   531		}
   532	
   533		reposCtx, reposCancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
   534		defer reposCancel()
   535	
   536		repoIndex, err := coreClient.ListRepos(reposCtx, coreapi.ListReposParams{})
   537		if err != nil {
   538			return nil, fmt.Errorf("listing repos for cell discovery: %w", err)
   539		}
   540	
   541		if repoIndex.Truncated {
   542			logging.Warn(ctx, "repo index truncated; code search results may be incomplete")
   543		}
   544	
   545		// Step 2: Resolve repo slug filters to ULIDs and narrow to matching cells.
   546		indexRepos := repoIndex.Repos
   547		if len(opts.repoFilters) > 0 {
   548			resolved, filtered := resolveRepoFilters(opts.repoFilters, repoIndex.Repos)
   549			if len(resolved) == 0 {
   550				hint := ""
   551				if repoIndex.Truncated {
   552					hint = " (repo index was truncated — the repo may exist but was not included)"
   553				}
   554				return nil, fmt.Errorf("no matching repositories found for filter %q%s", opts.repoFilters, hint)
   555			}
   556			opts.resolvedRepoIDs = resolved
   557			indexRepos = filtered
   558		}
   559	
   560		// Step 3: Group repos by cell and resolve baseURLs via shared helpers.
   561		// Routes by routedRepoPlacement like semantic search (see its doc). The
   562		// CLI is deliberately ahead of the BFF's code-search.ts here, which stays
   563		// canonical until its code-read chain (/symbols, /usages, file viewer)
   564		// flips with it — identical behavior until then, and core electing
   565		// divergent primaries is gated on that web flip (tracked on ENT-1776).
   566		pinned := len(opts.repoFilters) > 0
   567		cells, skippedRepos := groupReposByCell(indexRepos)
   568		skippedRepos = reportableSkippedRepos(ctx, pinned, len(cells), skippedRepos)
   569		if len(cells) == 0 {
   570			return &codesearch.SearchResponse{SkippedRepos: skippedRepos}, nil
   571		}
   572		resolveCellBaseURLs(ctx, coreClient, cells)
   573	
   574		// Step 4: Fan out via the shared fanOutCells helper.
   575		// Each cell gets the full limit for single-cell, or 2x for multi-cell so
   576		// the merge sees enough candidates from every region for proper global
   577		// ranking. mergeSearchResults applies the final cap.
   578		perCellLimit := opts.limit
   579		if len(cells) > 1 && perCellLimit > 0 {
   580			perCellLimit *= 2
   581		}
   582		results, err := fanOutCells(ctx, opts.insecureHTTP, codeSearchCellTimeout, cells, func(ctx context.Context, group cellGroup, client *api.Client) (*codesearch.SearchResponse, error) {
   583			var repoIDs []string
   584			if len(opts.resolvedRepoIDs) > 0 {
   585				repoIDs = group.repoIDs
   586			}
   587			req := codesearch.SearchRequest{
   588				Query:         opts.query,
   589				Repos:         repoIDs,
   590				CaseSensitive: opts.caseSensitive,
   591			}
   592			if perCellLimit > 0 {
   593				req.MaxResults = perCellLimit
   594			}
   595			return codesearch.Search(ctx, client, req)
   596		})
   597		if err != nil {
   598			if errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn) {
   599				return nil, loginHintErr(err)
   600			}
   601			return nil, fmt.Errorf("code search: %w", err)
   602		}
   603	
   604		merged, err := mergeSearchResults(ctx, opts.limit, results)
   605		if err != nil {
   606			return nil, err
   607		}
   608		merged.SkippedRepos = skippedRepos
   609		return merged, nil
   610	}
   611	
   612	// resolveRepoFilters matches user-provided filters against the repo index,
   613	// returning the ULID list for peregrine and the subset of index entries whose
   614	// repos matched (for cell grouping).
   615	//
   616	// Matching mirrors the BFF (code-search.ts lines 315-319):
   617	//
   618	//	slug = filter starts with "gh/" ? strip prefix : filter unchanged
   619	//	match = id === filter || full_name === slug || full_name === filter
   620	//

   370	type codeSearchOpts struct {
   371		query           string
   372		repoFilters     []string
   373		resolvedRepoIDs []string // ULIDs resolved from repoFilters via repo index
   374		limit           int

   376		caseSensitive   bool

   378		insecureHTTP    bool
   379		// commandPath is the invoking cobra command path, carried here because
   380		// searchAllCells emits outcome telemetry and the TUI's code tab calls it

   384	
   385	// extractInlineRepoFilters extracts only repo: prefixed filters from a query
   386	// string, returning the remaining query text and the list of repo values.
   387	// Unlike search.ParseSearchInput, this does NOT consume author:, date:, or
   388	// branch: tokens — those are checkpoint-search-only and should be treated as
   389	// literal text in code search queries.
   390	func extractInlineRepoFilters(query string) (remaining string, repos []string) {
   391		var kept []string
   392		for _, part := range strings.Fields(query) {
   393			if strings.HasPrefix(part, "repo:") {
   394				// Split comma-separated values (repo:a,b → [a, b]), matching
   395				// checkpoint search's parseListFilter behavior. Trim quotes so
   396				// repo:"gh/owner/repo" works like the unquoted form.
   397				for _, v := range strings.Split(part[5:], ",") {
   398					v = strings.Trim(v, `"'`)
   399					if v != "" {
   400						repos = append(repos, v)
   401					}
   402				}
   403			} else {
   404				kept = append(kept, part)
   405			}
   406		}
   407		return strings.Join(kept, " "), repos
   408	}

   410	// hasAllReposFilter returns true if repos contains the wildcard "*" filter.
   411	func hasAllReposFilter(repos []string) bool {

   413			if r == search.AllReposFilter {
   414				return true
   415			}
   416		}
   417		return false

   431	// buildCodeSearchOpts returns a *codeSearchOpts pre-populated with repo filters.
   432	// It honors --repo, --all-repos, and inline repo: filters from the command line;
   433	// when none are specified, it falls back to the current git origin slug.
   434	func buildCodeSearchOpts(ctx context.Context, commandPath, owner, repoName string, repos []string, allRepos, insecureHTTP bool) *codeSearchOpts {
   435		var repoFilters []string
   436		switch {
   437		case allRepos:
   438			// nil repoFilters → searchAllCells searches all repos
   439		case len(repos) > 0:
   440			repoFilters = repos
   441		default:
   442			// Use forge-prefixed slug (e.g. "et/proj/repo") so Entire forge
   443			// repos match the index FullName. Falls back to owner/repo for
   444			// GitHub repos (gh/ prefix is stripped by resolveRepoFilters).
   445			if slug := currentRepoSlugWithForge(ctx); slug != "" {
   446				repoFilters = []string{slug}
   447			} else {
   448				repoFilters = []string{owner + "/" + repoName}
   449			}
   450		}
   451		return &codeSearchOpts{
   452			repoFilters:  repoFilters,
   453			limit:        search.DefaultLimit,
   454			insecureHTTP: insecureHTTP,
   455			commandPath:  commandPath,
   456		}
