   458	
   459	// codeSearchCellTimeout bounds each per-cell search call (token exchange + API).
   460	const codeSearchCellTimeout = 30 * time.Second
   461	
   462	// runCodeSearch handles the --code flag path: search code content via peregrine.
   463	//
   464	// When a repo filter is specified, it routes to that repo's owning cell.
   465	// Without a filter, it fans out across all cells that host the user's repos
   466	// (mirroring the BFF's /api/v1/stream endpoint): list repos from the control
   467	// plane, group by cell/jurisdiction, search each cell in parallel, merge.
   468	func runCodeSearch(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, opts codeSearchOpts) error {
   469		if opts.query == "" {
   470			return errors.New("query required for code search. Usage: entire search --code <query>")
   471		}
   472	
   473		w := cmd.OutOrStdout()
   474		textOutput := !opts.jsonOutput && interactive.IsTerminalWriter(w)
   475	
   476		// Text output shows up to maxCodeSearchFiles files with a few matches
   477		// each, so fetch a deeper result set than the default --limit (which is
   478		// tuned for flat JSON output) unless the user asked for a specific limit.
   479		if textOutput && !opts.limitExplicit {
   480			opts.limit = codeSearchTextFetchLimit
   481		}
   482	
   483		// Always fan out via searchAllCells — it fetches the repo index,
   484		// resolves slugs to ULIDs, and handles single- vs multi-jurisdiction.
   485		// searchAllCells emits the outcome telemetry itself, so the TUI's code
   486		// tab (which calls it directly) is covered too.
   487		resp, err := searchAllCells(ctx, opts)
   488		if err != nil {
   489			return err
   490		}
   491	
   492		if !textOutput {
   493			return writeCodeSearchJSON(w, resp)
   494		}
   495	
   496		writeCodeSearchText(w, resp, newStatusStyles(w), opts.caseSensitive)
   497		return nil
   498	}
   499	
   500	// searchAllCells fans out code search across all cells that host the user's
   501	// repos, using the shared cell-routing foundation (cell_fanout.go):
   502	//  1. List repos from the control plane (entire-core) to discover cells
   503	//  2. Resolve repo slug filters to ULIDs
   504	//  3. Group by cell and resolve baseURLs via the shared helpers
   505	//  4. Fan out via fanOutCells with per-cell codesearch.Search calls
   506	//  5. Merge results (sorted by score, capped to limit)
   507	//
   508	// Every call emits one cli_search_completed outcome — this is the code-search
   509	// seam shared by the one-shot --code path and the TUI's code tab, so
   510	// instrumenting here covers both by construction.
   511	func searchAllCells(ctx context.Context, opts codeSearchOpts) (resp *codesearch.SearchResponse, err error) {
   512		start := time.Now()
   513		defer func() {
   514			var result searchOutcomeResult
   515			if resp != nil {
   516				result = searchOutcomeResult{
   517					count:              len(resp.Results),
   518					coverageIncomplete: len(resp.FailedJurisdictions) > 0 || len(resp.SkippedRepos) > 0,
   519				}
   520			}
   521			emitSearchOutcome(ctx, opts.commandPath, telemetry.SearchModeCode, result, time.Since(start), err)
   522		}()
   523		// Step 1: Get repos index from the control plane. *coreapi.Client
   524		// satisfies cellCoreClient (passed to resolveCellBaseURLs below as such).
   525		coreClient, err := coreapi.New()
   526		if err != nil {
   527			if errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn) {
   528				return nil, loginHintErr(err)
   529			}
   530			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolving control-plane client: %w", err)
   531		}
   532	
   533		reposCtx, reposCancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
   534		defer reposCancel()
   535	
   536		repoIndex, err := coreClient.ListRepos(reposCtx, coreapi.ListReposParams{})
   537		if err != nil {
   538			return nil, fmt.Errorf("listing repos for cell discovery: %w", err)
   539		}
   540	
   541		if repoIndex.Truncated {
   542			logging.Warn(ctx, "repo index truncated; code search results may be incomplete")
   543		}
   544	
   545		// Step 2: Resolve repo slug filters to ULIDs and narrow to matching cells.
   546		indexRepos := repoIndex.Repos
   547		if len(opts.repoFilters) > 0 {
   548			resolved, filtered := resolveRepoFilters(opts.repoFilters, repoIndex.Repos)
   549			if len(resolved) == 0 {
   550				hint := ""
   551				if repoIndex.Truncated {
   552					hint = " (repo index was truncated — the repo may exist but was not included)"
   553				}
   554				return nil, fmt.Errorf("no matching repositories found for filter %q%s", opts.repoFilters, hint)
   555			}
   556			opts.resolvedRepoIDs = resolved
   557			indexRepos = filtered
   558		}
   559	
   560		// Step 3: Group repos by cell and resolve baseURLs via shared helpers.
   561		// Routes by routedRepoPlacement like semantic search (see its doc). The
   562		// CLI is deliberately ahead of the BFF's code-search.ts here, which stays
   563		// canonical until its code-read chain (/symbols, /usages, file viewer)
   564		// flips with it — identical behavior until then, and core electing
   565		// divergent primaries is gated on that web flip (tracked on ENT-1776).
   566		pinned := len(opts.repoFilters) > 0
   567		cells, skippedRepos := groupReposByCell(indexRepos)
   568		skippedRepos = reportableSkippedRepos(ctx, pinned, len(cells), skippedRepos)
   569		if len(cells) == 0 {
   570			return &codesearch.SearchResponse{SkippedRepos: skippedRepos}, nil
   571		}
   572		resolveCellBaseURLs(ctx, coreClient, cells)
   573	
   574		// Step 4: Fan out via the shared fanOutCells helper.
   575		// Each cell gets the full limit for single-cell, or 2x for multi-cell so
   576		// the merge sees enough candidates from every region for proper global
   577		// ranking. mergeSearchResults applies the final cap.
   578		perCellLimit := opts.limit
   579		if len(cells) > 1 && perCellLimit > 0 {
   580			perCellLimit *= 2
   581		}
   582		results, err := fanOutCells(ctx, opts.insecureHTTP, codeSearchCellTimeout, cells, func(ctx context.Context, group cellGroup, client *api.Client) (*codesearch.SearchResponse, error) {
   583			var repoIDs []string
   584			if len(opts.resolvedRepoIDs) > 0 {
   585				repoIDs = group.repoIDs
   586			}
   587			req := codesearch.SearchRequest{
   588				Query:         opts.query,
   589				Repos:         repoIDs,
   590				CaseSensitive: opts.caseSensitive,
   591			}
   592			if perCellLimit > 0 {
   593				req.MaxResults = perCellLimit
   594			}
   595			return codesearch.Search(ctx, client, req)
   596		})
   597		if err != nil {
   598			if errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn) {
   599				return nil, loginHintErr(err)
   600			}
   601			return nil, fmt.Errorf("code search: %w", err)
   602		}
   603	
   604		merged, err := mergeSearchResults(ctx, opts.limit, results)
   605		if err != nil {
   606			return nil, err
   607		}
   608		merged.SkippedRepos = skippedRepos
   609		return merged, nil
   610	}
   611	
   612	// resolveRepoFilters matches user-provided filters against the repo index,
   613	// returning the ULID list for peregrine and the subset of index entries whose
   614	// repos matched (for cell grouping).
   615	//
   616	// Matching mirrors the BFF (code-search.ts lines 315-319):
   617	//
   618	//	slug = filter starts with "gh/" ? strip prefix : filter unchanged
   619	//	match = id === filter || full_name === slug || full_name === filter
   620	//

   117	func (r *apiCheckpointReader) Read(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) (*checkpoint.CheckpointSummary, error) {

    26	// PersistentStore provides the production persistent checkpoint storage surface:
    27	// checkpoint-level reads, session-level reads, and the unified Write. Writes go
    28	// through Writer.Write(ctx, WriteRequest); the concrete per-operation methods
    29	// live on the git implementation as the methods Write dispatches to.
    30	type PersistentStore interface {
    31		CheckpointReader
    32		SessionReader
    33		Writer
    34	}
    35	
    36	// WriteRequest is a single persistent-store write command. The set is closed to
    37	// other packages: only types in this package can implement it, sealed via the
    38	// unexported isWriteRequest marker. A store dispatches on the concrete type; a
    39	// mirror/fan-out store forwards the same value to each backend's Write.
    40	//
    41	// Four requests are session-level (Session, ReservedSession, SessionTranscript,
    42	// SessionSummary) and one is checkpoint-level (CheckpointAttribution). Adding
    43	// a write operation is a new request type plus one dispatch case in every
    44	// backend. The Store interface stays unchanged, so seam tests must exercise the
    45	// full union because Go does not exhaustively check type switches.

    14	// kindRoutingStore resolves id-keyed reads across the two git backends so a repo
    15	// running git-refs and git-branch side by side (or mid-migration between them)
    16	// can read checkpoints of BOTH formats without reconfiguring:
    17	//
    18	//   - A ULID checkpoint only ever lives in the git-refs store, so a ULID ID is
    19	//     read from refs and NEVER from the branch (regardless of the active backend).
    20	//   - A legacy-hex ID is read from the active (configured) primary first. When the
    21	//     active primary is git-refs, it also falls back to the git-branch store,
    22	//     because a hex checkpoint may still sit on the pre-migration v1 branch. Under
    23	//     a git-branch primary the branch is authoritative for hex, so refs is not
    24	//     consulted.
    25	//
    26	// List unions both backends (disjoint ID spaces). Fresh creates (Session) are NOT
    27	// kind-routed: they go to the configured primary (+ mirrors) via writer, since
    28	// a new checkpoint's ID is already minted to match the primary's format (see
    29	// checkpoint.GenerateCheckpointID). ReservedSession writes preserve the backend
    30	// chosen before an interrupted write; when a migrated copy already exists in the
    31	// read-preferred backend, they update that copy too. Backfills update an existing
    32	// checkpoint, so they follow the same store order as reads, though only
    33	// ErrCheckpointNotFound falls through (stricter than reads) — see Write.
    34	type kindRoutingStore struct {
    35		writer      PersistentStore // configured primary + mirrors (fanout); handles Write
    36		branch      PersistentStore // git-branch store; serves hex reads
    37		refs        PersistentStore // git-refs store; serves ULID reads (+ hex under refs primary)
    38		primaryType string
    39	}
    40	
    41	// newKindRoutingStore wraps the write fanout plus the two git read stores. It
    42	// preserves the optional AuthorReader capability (explain relies on it) when both
    43	// read stores provide it — the built-in git backends always do.
    44	func newKindRoutingStore(writer, branch, refs PersistentStore, primaryType string) PersistentStore {
    45		s := &kindRoutingStore{writer: writer, branch: branch, refs: refs, primaryType: primaryType}
    46		if _, ok := branch.(AuthorReader); ok {
    47			if _, ok := refs.(AuthorReader); ok {
    48				return &kindRoutingStoreWithAuthor{kindRoutingStore: s}
    49			}
    50		}
    51		return s
    52	}
    53	
    54	// readOrder returns the stores to consult for checkpointID, in priority order,
    55	// per the routing rules above.
    56	func (s *kindRoutingStore) readOrder(checkpointID id.CheckpointID) []PersistentStore {
    57		if checkpointID.Kind() == id.KindULID {
    58			return []PersistentStore{s.refs} // ULIDs only ever live in refs
    59		}
    60		switch s.primaryType {
    61		case BackendTypeGitBranch:
    62			return []PersistentStore{s.branch} // branch is authoritative for hex
    63		case BackendTypeGitRefs:
    64			return []PersistentStore{s.refs, s.branch} // active refs, then pre-migration branch
    65		default:
    66			// A non-branch/refs git-backed primary is not a real configuration today;
    67			// try both git stores so a hex ID still resolves wherever it landed.
    68			return []PersistentStore{s.branch, s.refs}
    69		}
    70	}
    71	
    72	// firstResolved calls read on each store in order and returns the first genuine
    73	// hit (a non-absent result with no error). A non-final store that reports absent
    74	// OR errors falls through to the next store, so a transient failure in one
    75	// backend (e.g. a git-refs on-demand fetch error) does not hide a checkpoint that
    76	// resolves in the fallback backend. The final store's result is returned as-is
    77	// (hit, absent, or error), so callers still see the backend's own not-found /
    78	// error signal when nothing resolved.
    79	func firstResolved[T any](stores []PersistentStore, read func(PersistentStore) (T, error), absent func(T, error) bool) (T, error) {
    80		var v T
    81		var err error
    82		for i, st := range stores {
    83			v, err = read(st)
    84			if i == len(stores)-1 || (err == nil && !absent(v, err)) {
    85				return v, err
    86			}
    87		}
    88		return v, err
    89	}
    90	
    91	// checkpointNotFound reports the checkpoint-level "absent" signal: Read returns
    92	// (nil, nil) — not an error — when a checkpoint does not exist.
    93	func checkpointNotFound(v *CheckpointSummary, err error) bool {
    94		return err == nil && v == nil
    95	}
    96	
    97	// sessionNotFound reports the session-level "absent" signal: the session readers
    98	// return ErrCheckpointNotFound when the checkpoint (or session) is missing.
    99	func sessionNotFound[T any](_ T, err error) bool {
   100		return errors.Is(err, ErrCheckpointNotFound)
   101	}
   102	
   103	func (s *kindRoutingStore) Read(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) (*CheckpointSummary, error) {

   107		)
   108	}

   112		if err != nil {
   113			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // in-package store error surfaced verbatim
   114		}
   115		refsList, err := s.refs.List(ctx)
   116		if err != nil {
   117			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // in-package store error surfaced verbatim
   118		}
   119		merged := make([]CheckpointInfo, 0, len(branchList)+len(refsList))
   120		merged = append(merged, branchList...)
   121		merged = append(merged, refsList...)
   122		sortCheckpointInfosByRecency(merged)
   123		// Dedup by ID: during coexistence/migration the same checkpoint can appear in
   124		// both backends (a ULID mirrored to the branch, or a hex still on the branch

   132			}
   133			seen[info.CheckpointID] = struct{}{}

   135		}
   136		return deduped, nil
   137	}

   139	// sortCheckpointInfosByRecency orders checkpoints most-recent-first by CreatedAt.
   140	// Shared by the git-branch, git-refs, and routing List implementations so they
   141	// present a consistent order.
   142	func sortCheckpointInfosByRecency(checkpoints []CheckpointInfo) {
   143		sort.Slice(checkpoints, func(i, j int) bool {
   144			return checkpoints[i].CreatedAt.After(checkpoints[j].CreatedAt)
   145		})
   146	}
   147	
   148	func (s *kindRoutingStore) ReadSessionContent(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, sessionIndex int) (*SessionContent, error) {
   149		return firstResolved(s.readOrder(checkpointID),

   155	}

   158		return firstResolved(s.readOrder(checkpointID),

   162			sessionNotFound[*Metadata],

   164	}

   167		return firstResolved(s.readOrder(checkpointID),

   115	// Read fetches the checkpoint envelope and maps it onto the local
   116	// CheckpointSummary shape the renderers consume.
   117	func (r *apiCheckpointReader) Read(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) (*checkpoint.CheckpointSummary, error) {

   123		// Sessions carries cardinality only: the renderers use len(Sessions) and
   124		// index into it, and read the actual per-session data through
   125		// SessionReader. The local shape's path fields name blobs in a git tree,
   126		// which has no meaning over HTTP, so they stay empty rather than carrying

   128		sessions := make([]checkpoint.SessionFilePaths, len(info.Sessions))

   131		// the checkpoint was CREATED on; the cell reports the branches that
   132		// currently CONTAIN the commit (a checkpoint made on a feature branch and
   133		// since merged reports "main"). Those are different facts, and putting the

   135		// consumer of `explain --json`.

   138			Strategy:         "manual-commit",
   139			CommitSHA:        info.CommitSha,
   140			CheckpointsCount: info.TotalSteps,
   141			FilesTouched:     info.FilesTouched,
   142			Sessions:         sessions,

   145				CacheCreationTokens: int(info.CacheCreationTokens),

Refuse what os.Root only confined

The anchors landed in the previous three commits. This is the tail, and
most of it is one bug wearing several hats: os.Root contains a path
without saying anything about what the path is.

fs.WalkDir takes its walk root's DirEntry from fs.Stat, which follows a
symlink, and only the entries below it from ReadDir, which does not.
Every symlink guard here inspected d.Type() inside the callback, so none
of them covered the root: a symlinked .entire/metadata/<session> was
descended into and its target redacted, committed and pushed.
filepath.Walk lstat'd its root, so this was lost in the conversion, not
absent from the start. osroot.WalkDirNoSymlinks lstats the root and
refuses a symlink at both levels; the two checkpoint metadata walks,
clean's tmp walk and doctor's reporter use it. redact.LoadPacks gets the
same check through fs.ReadLinkFS, which os.Root.FS() implements, so it
keeps its fs.FS-only API and its dependency-free position. A symlinked
.entire is refused rather than followed now, so doctor and CLAUDE.md stop
telling the user that intentional setups keep working.

jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicIn leaves <base>.<16 hex>.tmp beside its target,
and .entire/metadata/<session> is copied wholesale into every checkpoint
tree. A hook killed between the create and the rename left an orphan that
was committed on every checkpoint from then on, and ParseChunkIndex read
it back as a transcript CHUNK: fmt.Sscanf("%03d") stops at the first
non-digit, so full.jsonl.123abc...tmp parsed as chunk 123 and was
reassembled into the transcript. Both walks skip jsonutil.IsTempName, and
a chunk suffix must now be entirely digits.

SessionStore resolved its root through osroot.Shared, a registry that
never evicts. searchTranscriptInProjectDirs opens a store for every
candidate directory it walks under an agent's session base dir, so each
probe retained a directory fd for the life of the process, measured at
one per directory against zero for the os.Stat it replaced. A store is
not a long-lived anchor: it opens a root per operation and closes it
again. plugin_install_remote took a shared root on a staging directory it
then RemoveAll'd, with no Forget.

Smaller, same theme: createBlobFromFile read WORKTREE files through
entiredir, binding them to .entire's policy; removeEntireDirectory
guessed cwd for a recursive delete on any WorktreeRoot failure rather
than only on git's positive not-a-repository verdict; the session-state
read path opened a child root with no symlink check, which
osroot.OpenChild now performs; and settings.readConfinedIn was a second
copy of osroot.OpenNoFollow.

on settings.Load falling back to a cwd-relative path when the anchor
failed. That fallback is gone, so they name the worktree root in the

Give every tree Entire writes to a single os.Root anchor

Entire does filesystem I/O in six trees, and until now each read and write
assembled its own absolute path and handed it to os.ReadFile/os.WriteFile.
Containment was therefore a property each call site had to keep honouring
by hand, and several of them carried comments saying so outright:
PluginDataDir "guarantees ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR always points inside the
managed data subtree", investigate.RunDir noted that "an unvalidated id
would be a path-traversal sink" feeding os.RemoveAll.

Each tree now has one package that owns a shared *os.Root over it, and the
names that reach those roots are relative to them:

  .entire                    entiredir
  git common dir             gitdir
  the working tree           worktreedir
  an agent's session store   agent.SessionStore
  per-user config / cache    userdirs.ConfigRoot / CacheRoot
  managed plugin tree        pluginRoot

The roots memoize through one registry, osroot.Shared, replacing three
separate copies of that map. Directory creation goes through
osroot.MkdirAllNoSymlink, which refuses a component that already exists as
a symlink -- os.Root blocks a symlink that escapes a root but follows one
pointing elsewhere inside it, and an escaping one otherwise surfaces as an
opaque errno far from the cause. entire doctor reports the symlinks that
are already there.

Two anchors are worth calling out because they close a real gap rather
than formalising an existing one. agent.SessionStore is where a hook
payload's session ID becomes a path via the agent's own
ResolveSessionFile; SessionFile converts the result back to a name inside
the store and rejects an ID that walked out of it, which a plain
filepath.Join produced silently. worktreedir covers the checkpoint tree
entries rewind restores, which may have been fetched from a remote --
rewind's restore half already opened a root for that reason; the reads
beside it did not.

paths.WorktreeRoot is now the single answer to "where is the repository",
and entiredir.anchor falls back to the current directory only on git's
positive ErrNotARepository verdict. The fallback it replaces fired on any
resolve failure, `git` off $PATH included, and then silently gave an agent
working in a subdirectory of a real repo its own .entire beside itself. A
root is only as trustworthy as the directory it is opened on, so a base
that cannot be resolved is not a base to guess at.

settings.readConfined keeps its symlink refusal on every branch, through
one readConfinedIn: the .entire branch briefly read straight through
osroot.ReadFile, which follows an in-root symlink silently -- precisely
the .entire/settings.local.json -> planted.json case the check exists for.

Follow the rename through strings, comments, skill and docs

The identifier rename in the previous commit left the prose behind. This
is the prose, plus a handful of comments that described the restore path
#2178 deleted.

User-facing text. `checkpoint list --pending` said "No pending rewind
points found." and "Pending rewind points are created automatically
during active agent sessions."; the --pending flag help and the command's
Long text advertised "shadow-branch rewind points"; the two error paths
said "failed to find rewind points". All now say pending checkpoints.
Two assertions in checkpoint_list_test.go pinned the empty-list string
and are updated with it -- they are the only tests that pin any string
this commit touches, and both are exact-match Contains calls, so nothing
else could have silently drifted.

The first-turn context injection told every agent to leave "(enable,
disable, clean, rewind, auth)" to the user. `entire rewind` has not
existed since #1747, so a third of that warning pointed at nothing.
trail_injection_text_test.go asserts only the prefix "Leave setup and
destructive commands", so it still passes; deprecated_strings_test.go
keeps "entire rewind" on its never-advertise list, which is the one place
the name should survive.

Comments. Three were wrong about mechanisms rather than just names, and
those were checked against the code rather than reworded:

  - gitrepo/status.go named "review, rewind" as the paths that keep the
    unbounded Status walk. The rewind one is gone; the two real callers
    are review_target.go and detectFileChangesUnbounded (`session
    adopt`), and the comment now names both.
  - manual_commit_session.go attributed FindSessionsForCommit and
    ClearSessionState to "the rewind reset command". They are called by
    `entire clean` (clean.go:177) and `entire doctor` (doctor.go:406)
    respectively -- different commands, so they get different comments.
  - common.go's DeleteBranchCLI cited HardResetWithProtection as the
    sibling go-git v5 workaround. That function does not exist anywhere
    in the tree; the real one is CheckoutBranch in git_operations.go, and
    the comment now points there.

The rest are vocabulary: agent.go's ProtectedDirs and the mirrored
comments in checkpoint/, session/state.go, api/checkpoint/metadata.go
(comment only -- nothing exported in api/ is renamed), explain.go,
resume.go, transcript.go and strategy/.

Historical references stay, because they explain why the current shape is
what it is: every `rewind --list` mention in checkpoint_list.go and
checkpoint_group.go (that bridge is the reason the JSON is frozen), the
"former interactive rewind picker" that pendingCheckpointLabel inherited
its format from, and manual_commit_workflow_test.go's note about the
assertions that replaced the rewind observations. Also untouched: every
"rewind" that means moving a git ref backwards (fetch_rewind_protection_test.go,
safely_advance_local_ref_test.go, checkpoint_remote_test.go, the
explain fetch tests) and internal/remotehelper/transport/proxy.go, whose
rewinding is of HTTP request bodies.

Skill and scripts. The harness verb list-rewind-points is now
list-pending-checkpoints, which is two characters wider than the old
longest verb, so the usage block's description column was re-padded to
match. scripts/test-attribution-e2e.sh only ever echoed the phrase; it
already called `checkpoint list --pending --json`.

Docs. CLAUDE.md's method list and Key Files entries pick up the new
identifiers and file name, and sessions-and-checkpoints.md's "## Rewind"
section is "## Pending Checkpoints" with a sentence defining the term
against condensation rather than against a command that no longer exists.
AGENTS.md is a symlink and untouched.

  1353				slog.String("tool_use_id", event.ToolUseID),
  1354				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
  1355			return nil
  1356		}

  1360			// there is nothing here to attach it to, and re-creating session state
  1361			// for a late event would resurrect a zombie session. Nothing to
  1362			// complete either: the record lived on that same missing state.
  1363			logging.Info(logCtx, "skipping subagent-stop capture: session state not found",
  1364				slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),

  1372			// post-task (foreground task), or another Final event for the same
  1373			// ToolUseID (a duplicate SubagentStop, or a race against the
  1374			// SessionEnd final capture) already completed it. Skip.

  1325	// handleSubagentStopFinal is the authoritative final capture, run for
  1326	// SubagentStop (event.Final == true) and, via captureInFlightTaskFinal, for
  1327	// SessionEnd's sweep of any task still in flight when the session closes. It
  1328	// guards against a late SubagentStop resurrecting an ended/swept session —
  1329	// creating parent state here would mint a zombie session, the exact class the
  1330	// session sweep exists to prevent — then completes the record (bypassing the
  1331	// no-changes skip gate: a read-only subagent still produced a transcript worth
  1332	// materializing). Completion happens LAST, inside completeSubagentTaskRecord's
  1333	// exactly-once mutation (strategy.CompleteTaskRecord), so a failed capture —
  1334	// analyzer error, worktree error — leaves the record live for the SessionEnd
  1335	// sweep to retry, and two Final events racing for the same ToolUseID complete
  1336	// it exactly once (the loser's extraction is discarded; nothing was written).
  1337	//
  1338	// The state loaded at the top of the function is only good for the zombie
  1339	// guard above (state missing entirely), the live-record skip check, and
  1340	// logging: it predates the capture that follows, and a racing SessionEnd can
  1341	// land during that window (both serialize on the per-session gate, so the
  1342	// interleaving reduces to ordering). The eager-condense decision near the end
  1343	// of the function therefore reloads session state and decides on that fresh
  1344	// phase, never on this initial snapshot.

  1346		state, err := strategy.LoadSessionState(logCtx, event.SessionID)
  1347		if err != nil {
  1348			// A real load failure (corrupt/unreadable state file) — distinct from
  1349			// the state simply not existing, for which LoadSessionState returns
  1350			// (nil, nil) and the branch below logs truthfully.
  1351			logging.Warn(logCtx, "skipping subagent-stop capture: failed to load session state",
  1352				slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
  1353				slog.String("tool_use_id", event.ToolUseID),
  1354				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
  1355			return nil
  1356		}
  1357		if state == nil {
  1358			// Session state missing entirely (ended and swept, or never existed).
  1359			// The subagent transcript remains on disk in the agent's own directory;
  1360			// there is nothing here to attach it to, and re-creating session state
  1361			// for a late event would resurrect a zombie session. Nothing to
  1362			// complete either: the record lived on that same missing state.
  1363			logging.Info(logCtx, "skipping subagent-stop capture: session state not found",
  1364				slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
  1365				slog.String("tool_use_id", event.ToolUseID))
  1366			return nil
  1367		}
  1368	
  1369		marker := state.FindTaskRecord(event.ToolUseID)
  1370		if marker == nil || !marker.CompletedAt.IsZero() {
  1371			// No live marker: this ToolUseID was already completed at launch-time
  1372			// post-task (foreground task), or another Final event for the same
  1373			// ToolUseID (a duplicate SubagentStop, or a race against the
  1374			// SessionEnd final capture) already completed it. Skip.
  1375			// An event carrying a SubagentID or a subagent transcript path is the
  1376			// louder variant: those fields mean a real subagent completed, so an
  1377			// unclaimed skip is either the expected foreground dedup, a duplicate
  1378			// event, or a misintegrated agent that sets Final without ever
  1379			// emitting the launch-time marker — worth surfacing over Debug.
  1380			if event.SubagentID != "" || event.SubagentTranscriptPath != "" {
  1381				logging.Warn(logCtx, "no in-flight marker for completed subagent — foreground dedup, a duplicate event, or a misintegrated agent setting Final without launch markers",
  1382					slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
  1383					slog.String("tool_use_id", event.ToolUseID),
  1384					slog.String("agent_id", event.SubagentID))
  1385				return nil
  1386			}
  1387			logging.Debug(logCtx, "no live in-flight marker for subagent-stop; skipping duplicate/foreground/racing capture",

  1393		// SubagentStop payloads carry no tool_input, so event.SubagentType/

  1395		// recorded all three at launch time. Each field falls back independently —
  1396		// not as an all-or-nothing pair — so a marker that only captured one of
  1397		// them (e.g. a legacy marker written before a field existed) still
  1398		// contributes what it has instead of being discarded wholesale.

  1401		}
  1402		if marker.TaskDescription != "" {
  1403			event.TaskDescription = marker.TaskDescription
  1404		}

  1406			event.SubagentID = marker.AgentID
  1407		}

  1409		// analyzerFilesOnly: true because reaching this point means a live marker

  1411		// a background task (foreground tasks complete immediately at launch and

  1420		// The eager-condense decision below must use the FRESH phase, not the
  1421		// snapshot loaded at the top of this function. That snapshot is only
  1422		// valid for the zombie guard (missing state), the live-record check, and
  1423		// logging above — the capture we just did is exactly the window where a
  1424		// racing SessionEnd can flip the session to PhaseEnded (both serialize on
  1425		// the per-session gate, so this reduces to ordering). Deciding on the
  1426		// stale pre-capture phase would miss that transition and skip the eager
  1427		// condense, leaving the record we just completed unmaterialized until some
  1428		// later condensation that may never come.
  1429		freshPhase := state.Phase

  1432			// the stale snapshot already said ended, fall back to it rather than
  1433			// treating the reload failure as "not ended".
  1434			logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to reload session state after subagent-stop capture; falling back to pre-capture phase for condense decision",

  1436				slog.String("tool_use_id", event.ToolUseID),
  1437				slog.String("error", reloadErr.Error()))

  1439			freshPhase = freshState.Phase

  1442			// or endSessionNow) condenses as part of ending the session, so the

  1448				slog.String("tool_use_id", event.ToolUseID))
  1449		}

  1451		if freshPhase == session.PhaseEnded {

  1453			// Trigger the same eager condense SessionEnd uses so the
  1454			// newly-completed record is materialized into a permanent checkpoint

  1456			if condErr := GetStrategy(logCtx).CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed(logCtx, event.SessionID); condErr != nil {
  1457				logging.Warn(logCtx, "eager condense after late subagent-stop capture failed",
  1458					slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
  1459					slog.String("error", condErr.Error()))
  1460			}
  1461		}
  1462	
  1463		return nil
  1464	}

  1471		// changes were detected. Only set for Final (SubagentStop) captures: a

  1473		// transcript worth materializing, and this is the only chance to record it.

  1479		// files. Set ONLY for background Final (SubagentStop) captures — see the

  1481		// rationale. Never set for the foreground launch-time path, which keeps

  1492	// completeSubagentTaskRecord detects a completed subagent invocation's changes
  1493	// and completes its durable task record (#2058): files, labels, tokens, and the
  1494	// declared transcript path land on the record; condensation later materializes
  1495	// the transcript into the checkpoint. No shadow task step is written.
  1496	func completeSubagentTaskRecord(logCtx context.Context, ag agent.Agent, event *agent.Event, opts subagentCaptureOptions) error {

  1498		// Cursor all carry agent_transcript_path); see Event.SubagentTranscriptPath.
  1499		// The layout probe is the fallback for launch-time PostToolUse events, which
  1500		// don't carry it.

  1503			subagentTranscriptPath = ResolveAgentTranscriptPath(filepath.Dir(event.SessionRef), event.SessionID, event.SubagentID)
  1504		}

  1506		// Log context
  1507		subagentEndAttrs := []any{
  1508			slog.String("event", event.Type.String()),
  1509			slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
  1510			slog.String("tool_use_id", event.ToolUseID),
  1511		}

  1513			subagentEndAttrs = append(subagentEndAttrs, slog.String("agent_id", event.SubagentID))
  1514		}
  1515		if subagentTranscriptPath != "" {
  1516			subagentEndAttrs = append(subagentEndAttrs, slog.String("subagent_transcript", subagentTranscriptPath))
  1517		}
  1518		logging.Info(logCtx, "subagent completed", subagentEndAttrs...)

  1521		var modifiedFiles []string
  1522		modifiedFiles = append(modifiedFiles, event.ModifiedFiles...)

  1524		case !ok:
  1525			// No analyzer: modifiedFiles stays event.ModifiedFiles only.
  1526		case opts.analyzerFilesOnly && subagentTranscriptPath == "":
  1527			// Background Final capture with no resolvable subagent transcript:
  1528			// falling back to scanning event.SessionRef (the PARENT transcript)
  1529			// from offset 0 would attribute the whole session's file activity to
  1530			// this one background task. Skip the analyzer scan entirely — the
  1531			// capture proceeds with only event.ModifiedFiles (typically empty,
  1532			// yielding a transcript-less, file-less record). The foreground
  1533			// path (analyzerFilesOnly unset) keeps the parent-scan fallback: there
  1534			// the worktree-diff merge below dominates the file lists anyway.
  1535			logging.Warn(logCtx, "subagent transcript unresolvable; final capture proceeding without file attribution",
  1536				slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
  1537				slog.String("tool_use_id", event.ToolUseID),
  1538				slog.String("agent_id", event.SubagentID))

  1540			transcriptToScan := event.SessionRef
  1541			if subagentTranscriptPath != "" {
  1542				transcriptToScan = subagentTranscriptPath
  1543			}

  1546			case fileErr != nil && opts.analyzerFilesOnly:

  1548				// worktree-diff backup in analyzer-only mode), so a transient
  1549				// read error here must fail the capture rather than complete a
  1550				// zero-file record that permanently misstates the task as
  1551				// read-only. Returning BEFORE completion leaves the record live,
  1552				// so the SessionEnd sweep retries it.
  1553				logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to extract modified files from subagent; aborting final capture",
  1554					slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
  1555					slog.String("tool_use_id", event.ToolUseID),
  1556					slog.String("error", fileErr.Error()))

  1558			case fileErr != nil:
  1559				// Foreground path: the worktree-diff merge below is the backup
  1560				// file source, so the capture proceeds without the analyzer.
  1561				logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to extract modified files from subagent",
  1562					slog.String("error", fileErr.Error()))

  1564				modifiedFiles = mergeUnique(modifiedFiles, files)
  1565			}

  1213			if readErr != nil || metadata == nil {

  1215			}

  1217				continue // Skip sessions that used the filesTouched fallback
  1218			}

  1122	// logUnclaimedCheckpointTrailer records a commit whose Entire-Checkpoint
  1123	// trailer no session condensed into. The case worth catching is a
  1124	// trailer/condense divergence: PrepareCommitMsg stamped a session it judged
  1125	// eligible and PostCommit then declined to condense it, leaving `entire
  1126	// explain` on that commit resolving to nothing. Both halves individually look
  1127	// like routine skips, so the divergence is invisible without this line.

  1132	// rebase replay, where the trailer rides along from a source commit whose
  1133	// session may not exist in this worktree at all.

  1136	// never from its *commitCondensedSignal: newCommitCondensedSignal returns nil
  1137	// for an amend that re-condenses a checkpoint it already reported, so the
  1138	// telemetry signal is absent in exactly the case that must count as claimed.

  1141	// `git commit -C` copy a trailer out of an existing commit message without

  1147	// Entire minted this trailer for this commit. PrepareCommitMsg writes no

  1171	// updateCombinedAttributionForCheckpoint computes holistic attribution across all sessions.
  1172	// Instead of summing per-session numbers (which inflates totals because each session
  1173	// independently counts the full commit), this diffs parent→HEAD once and classifies
  1174	// lines as agent or human based on the union of all sessions' files_touched.
  1175	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) updateCombinedAttributionForCheckpoint(
  1176		ctx context.Context,
  1177		repo *git.Repository,
  1178		checkpointID id.CheckpointID,
  1179		headTree, parentTree *object.Tree,
  1180		repoDir string,
  1181	) error {
  1182		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "attribution")
  1183		// The hook store envelope (see hookCheckpointStoreOptions): the attribution
  1184		// backfill's absence probe fetches a ref that exists remotely but not
  1185		// locally, and on a partial clone the checkpoint's own blobs need fetching
  1186		// too. Bounded budgets keep a dead network from stalling the post-commit
  1187		// hook: the ref store memoizes a failed ref fetch (gitRefsStore.fetchFailure)
  1188		// and hookBlobFetcher memoizes an exhausted blob fetch, so the two paths are
  1189		// bounded independently.
  1190		stores, err := checkpoint.Open(ctx, repo, s.hookCheckpointStoreOptions(ctx))
  1191		if err != nil {
  1192			return fmt.Errorf("open checkpoint store: %w", err)
  1193		}
  1194		store := stores.Persistent
  1195	
  1196		summary, err := store.Read(ctx, checkpointID)
  1197		if err != nil {
  1198			return fmt.Errorf("reading checkpoint summary: %w", err)
  1199		}
  1200		if summary == nil || len(summary.Sessions) <= 1 {
  1201			return nil
  1202		}
  1203	
  1204		// Collect union of files_touched from sessions that had real checkpoints (SaveStep ran).
  1205		// Sessions with no SaveStep steps (e.g., commit-only sessions) use a fallback that
  1206		// includes ALL committed files, which would incorrectly classify human-created files as agent work.
  1207		// Gate on SaveStepCount (the honest "SaveStep ran" signal), not CheckpointsCount —
  1208		// CheckpointsCount is now a prompt count floored at 1, so it's no longer 0 for these sessions.
  1209		// Old metadata lacks SaveStepCount → 0 → conservatively skipped, matching prior behavior.
  1210		agentFiles := make(map[string]struct{})
  1211		for i := range len(summary.Sessions) {
  1212			metadata, readErr := store.ReadSessionMetadata(ctx, checkpointID, i)
  1213			if readErr != nil || metadata == nil {
  1214				continue
  1215			}
  1216			if metadata.SaveStepCount == 0 {
  1217				continue // Skip sessions that used the filesTouched fallback
  1218			}
  1219			for _, f := range metadata.FilesTouched {
  1220				agentFiles[f] = struct{}{}
  1221			}
  1222		}
  1223	
  1224		if len(agentFiles) == 0 {
  1225			return nil
  1226		}
  1227	
  1228		// Get all files changed in this commit (parent → HEAD)
  1229		allChangedFiles, err := getAllChangedFiles(ctx, parentTree, headTree, repoDir, "", "")
  1230		if err != nil {
  1231			logging.Warn(logCtx, "combined attribution: failed to enumerate changed files",
  1232				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
  1233			return nil
  1234		}
  1235	
  1236		// Classify each changed file as agent or human and count lines
  1237		var agentAdded, agentRemoved, humanAdded, humanRemoved int
  1238		for _, filePath := range allChangedFiles {
  1239			// Skip CLI/agent config metadata — not human or agent code work
  1240			if strings.HasPrefix(filePath, ".entire/") || strings.HasPrefix(filePath, paths.EntireMetadataDir+"/") ||
  1241				strings.HasPrefix(filePath, ".claude/") {
  1242				continue
  1243			}
  1244	
  1245			parentContent := getFileContent(parentTree, filePath)
  1246			headContent := getFileContent(headTree, filePath)
  1247			_, added, removed := diffLines(parentContent, headContent)
  1248	
  1249			if _, isAgent := agentFiles[filePath]; isAgent {
  1250				agentAdded += added
  1251				agentRemoved += removed
  1252			} else {
  1253				humanAdded += added
  1254				humanRemoved += removed
  1255			}
  1256		}
  1257	
  1258		totalLinesChanged := agentAdded + agentRemoved + humanAdded + humanRemoved
  1259		totalCommitted := agentAdded + humanAdded
  1260	
  1261		var agentPercentage float64
  1262		if totalLinesChanged > 0 {
  1263			agentPercentage = float64(agentAdded+agentRemoved) / float64(totalLinesChanged) * 100
  1264		}
  1265	
  1266		combined := &checkpoint.Attribution{
  1267			CalculatedAt:      time.Now().UTC(),
  1268			AgentLines:        agentAdded,
  1269			AgentRemoved:      agentRemoved,
  1270			HumanAdded:        humanAdded,
  1271			HumanRemoved:      humanRemoved,
  1272			TotalCommitted:    totalCommitted,
  1273			TotalLinesChanged: totalLinesChanged,
  1274			AgentPercentage:   agentPercentage,
  1275			MetricVersion:     2,
  1276		}
  1277	
  1278		logging.Info(logCtx, "combined attribution calculated",
  1279			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
  1280			slog.Int("sessions", len(summary.Sessions)),
  1281			slog.Int("agent_files", len(agentFiles)),
  1282			slog.Int("agent_lines", agentAdded),
  1283			slog.Int("human_added", humanAdded),
  1284			slog.Float64("agent_percentage", agentPercentage),
  1285		)
  1286	
  1287		if err := store.Write(ctx, checkpoint.CheckpointAttribution{CheckpointID: checkpointID, Attribution: combined}); err != nil {
  1288			return fmt.Errorf("persisting combined attribution: %w", err)
  1289		}
  1290	
  1291		return nil
  1292	}

  1294	// postCommitProcessSessionLocked handles a single session within the PostCommit loop.
  1295	// Pre-resolved git objects (headTree, parentTree) are shared across all sessions;
  1296	// per-session shadow ref/tree are resolved once here and threaded through sub-calls.
  1297	//

  1299	// It is distinct from the second (the telemetry signal, which is nil for an
  1300	// amend re-condensing an already-reported checkpoint) and cannot be inferred
  1301	// from state afterwards: carry-forward on a partial commit clears
  1302	// LastCheckpointID that condenseAndUpdateState had just set, so the post-loop
  1303	// state of a successful partial condensation is indistinguishable from never
  1304	// having condensed.
  1305	//

  1309	// resolveShadowRefAndTree pre-resolves a session's shadow branch ref and tree.
  1310	// These are read 4+ times across sessionHasNewContent, filesOverlapWithContent,
  1311	// CondenseSession, filesWithRemainingAgentChanges, and
  1312	// calculateSessionAttributions. Both are nil when the branch does not exist.
  1313	func resolveShadowRefAndTree(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, shadowBranchName string) (*plumbing.Reference, *object.Tree) {

  1317		var shadowTree *object.Tree
  1318		if ref, refErr := repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName), true); refErr == nil {
  1319			shadowRef = ref
  1320			if sc, scErr := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash()); scErr == nil {
  1321				if st, stErr := sc.Tree(); stErr == nil {
  1322					shadowTree = st
  1323				}
  1324			}
  1325		}
  1326		return shadowRef, shadowTree
  1327	}

  1329	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) postCommitProcessSessionLocked(
  1330		ctx context.Context,
  1331		repo *git.Repository,
  1332		state *SessionState,

  1341		shadowBranchesToDelete map[string]struct{},
  1342		uncondensedActiveOnBranch map[string]bool,
  1343		allAgentFiles map[string]struct{},
  1344		sessionsWithCommittedFiles int,
  1345		condensedTelemetry *commitCondensedEmitter,
  1346	) (newSkillEvents []agent.SkillEvent, condensedSignal *commitCondensedSignal, condensed bool) {

  1348		shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
  1349		reservedCheckpointID := state.PendingCondensationID()
  1350		if reservedCheckpointID != id.EmptyCheckpointID && reservedCheckpointID != checkpointID {
  1351			logging.Warn(logCtx, "post-commit: preserving interrupted condensation with a different checkpoint ID",
  1352				slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1353				slog.String("reserved_checkpoint_id", reservedCheckpointID.String()),
  1354				slog.String("commit_checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()))

  1362		// Fail-open: if content check errors, assume new content exists so we
  1363		// don't silently skip data that should have been condensed.
  1364		//
  1365		// For ACTIVE sessions: the commit has a checkpoint trailer (verified above),
  1366		// meaning PrepareCommitMsg already determined this commit is session-related.
  1367		// The trailer is only added when either:

  1122	// logUnclaimedCheckpointTrailer records a commit whose Entire-Checkpoint
  1123	// trailer no session condensed into. The case worth catching is a
  1124	// trailer/condense divergence: PrepareCommitMsg stamped a session it judged
  1125	// eligible and PostCommit then declined to condense it, leaving `entire
  1126	// explain` on that commit resolving to nothing. Both halves individually look
  1127	// like routine skips, so the divergence is invisible without this line.

  1130	// are excluded here: `claimed` covers amend, seeded from LastCheckpointID by

  1132	// rebase replay, where the trailer rides along from a source commit whose
  1133	// session may not exist in this worktree at all.

  1135	// `claimed` must come from postCommitProcessSessionLocked's condensed result,
  1136	// never from its *commitCondensedSignal: newCommitCondensedSignal returns nil
  1137	// for an amend that re-condenses a checkpoint it already reported, so the
  1138	// telemetry signal is absent in exactly the case that must count as claimed.

  1140	// DEBUG, not WARN, because those are not all of them: `git merge --squash` and
  1141	// `git commit -C` copy a trailer out of an existing commit message without
  1142	// being sequencer operations, and PrepareCommitMsg deliberately never stamps a
  1143	// squash (see its source switch), so no local session owns the inherited ID
  1144	// and this cannot tell that from the real bug.

  1147	// Entire minted this trailer for this commit. PrepareCommitMsg writes no
  1148	// session state at all today, so that adds a lock-taking write to a read-only

  1171	// updateCombinedAttributionForCheckpoint computes holistic attribution across all sessions.
  1172	// Instead of summing per-session numbers (which inflates totals because each session
  1173	// independently counts the full commit), this diffs parent→HEAD once and classifies
  1174	// lines as agent or human based on the union of all sessions' files_touched.
  1175	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) updateCombinedAttributionForCheckpoint(
  1176		ctx context.Context,
  1177		repo *git.Repository,
  1178		checkpointID id.CheckpointID,
  1179		headTree, parentTree *object.Tree,
  1180		repoDir string,
  1181	) error {
  1182		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "attribution")
  1183		// The hook store envelope (see hookCheckpointStoreOptions): the attribution
  1184		// backfill's absence probe fetches a ref that exists remotely but not
  1185		// locally, and on a partial clone the checkpoint's own blobs need fetching
  1186		// too. Bounded budgets keep a dead network from stalling the post-commit
  1187		// hook: the ref store memoizes a failed ref fetch (gitRefsStore.fetchFailure)
  1188		// and hookBlobFetcher memoizes an exhausted blob fetch, so the two paths are
  1189		// bounded independently.
  1190		stores, err := checkpoint.Open(ctx, repo, s.hookCheckpointStoreOptions(ctx))
  1191		if err != nil {
  1192			return fmt.Errorf("open checkpoint store: %w", err)
  1193		}
  1194		store := stores.Persistent
  1195	
  1196		summary, err := store.Read(ctx, checkpointID)
  1197		if err != nil {
  1198			return fmt.Errorf("reading checkpoint summary: %w", err)
  1199		}
  1200		if summary == nil || len(summary.Sessions) <= 1 {
  1201			return nil
  1202		}
  1203	
  1204		// Collect union of files_touched from sessions that had real checkpoints (SaveStep ran).
  1205		// Sessions with no SaveStep steps (e.g., commit-only sessions) use a fallback that
  1206		// includes ALL committed files, which would incorrectly classify human-created files as agent work.
  1207		// Gate on SaveStepCount (the honest "SaveStep ran" signal), not CheckpointsCount —
  1208		// CheckpointsCount is now a prompt count floored at 1, so it's no longer 0 for these sessions.
  1209		// Old metadata lacks SaveStepCount → 0 → conservatively skipped, matching prior behavior.
  1210		agentFiles := make(map[string]struct{})
  1211		for i := range len(summary.Sessions) {
  1212			metadata, readErr := store.ReadSessionMetadata(ctx, checkpointID, i)
  1213			if readErr != nil || metadata == nil {
  1214				continue
  1215			}
  1216			if metadata.SaveStepCount == 0 {
  1217				continue // Skip sessions that used the filesTouched fallback
  1218			}
  1219			for _, f := range metadata.FilesTouched {
  1220				agentFiles[f] = struct{}{}
  1221			}
  1222		}
  1223	
  1224		if len(agentFiles) == 0 {
  1225			return nil
  1226		}
  1227	
  1228		// Get all files changed in this commit (parent → HEAD)
  1229		allChangedFiles, err := getAllChangedFiles(ctx, parentTree, headTree, repoDir, "", "")
  1230		if err != nil {
  1231			logging.Warn(logCtx, "combined attribution: failed to enumerate changed files",
  1232				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
  1233			return nil
  1234		}
  1235	
  1236		// Classify each changed file as agent or human and count lines
  1237		var agentAdded, agentRemoved, humanAdded, humanRemoved int
  1238		for _, filePath := range allChangedFiles {
  1239			// Skip CLI/agent config metadata — not human or agent code work
  1240			if strings.HasPrefix(filePath, ".entire/") || strings.HasPrefix(filePath, paths.EntireMetadataDir+"/") ||
  1241				strings.HasPrefix(filePath, ".claude/") {
  1242				continue
  1243			}
  1244	
  1245			parentContent := getFileContent(parentTree, filePath)
  1246			headContent := getFileContent(headTree, filePath)
  1247			_, added, removed := diffLines(parentContent, headContent)
  1248	
  1249			if _, isAgent := agentFiles[filePath]; isAgent {
  1250				agentAdded += added
  1251				agentRemoved += removed
  1252			} else {
  1253				humanAdded += added
  1254				humanRemoved += removed
  1255			}
  1256		}
  1257	
  1258		totalLinesChanged := agentAdded + agentRemoved + humanAdded + humanRemoved
  1259		totalCommitted := agentAdded + humanAdded
  1260	
  1261		var agentPercentage float64
  1262		if totalLinesChanged > 0 {
  1263			agentPercentage = float64(agentAdded+agentRemoved) / float64(totalLinesChanged) * 100
  1264		}
  1265	
  1266		combined := &checkpoint.Attribution{
  1267			CalculatedAt:      time.Now().UTC(),
  1268			AgentLines:        agentAdded,
  1269			AgentRemoved:      agentRemoved,
  1270			HumanAdded:        humanAdded,
  1271			HumanRemoved:      humanRemoved,
  1272			TotalCommitted:    totalCommitted,
  1273			TotalLinesChanged: totalLinesChanged,
  1274			AgentPercentage:   agentPercentage,
  1275			MetricVersion:     2,
  1276		}
  1277	
  1278		logging.Info(logCtx, "combined attribution calculated",
  1279			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
  1280			slog.Int("sessions", len(summary.Sessions)),
  1281			slog.Int("agent_files", len(agentFiles)),
  1282			slog.Int("agent_lines", agentAdded),
  1283			slog.Int("human_added", humanAdded),
  1284			slog.Float64("agent_percentage", agentPercentage),
  1285		)
  1286	
  1287		if err := store.Write(ctx, checkpoint.CheckpointAttribution{CheckpointID: checkpointID, Attribution: combined}); err != nil {
  1288			return fmt.Errorf("persisting combined attribution: %w", err)
  1289		}
  1290	
  1291		return nil
  1292	}

  1294	// postCommitProcessSessionLocked handles a single session within the PostCommit loop.

  1296	// per-session shadow ref/tree are resolved once here and threaded through sub-calls.

  1300	// amend re-condensing an already-reported checkpoint) and cannot be inferred
  1301	// from state afterwards: carry-forward on a partial commit clears
  1302	// LastCheckpointID that condenseAndUpdateState had just set, so the post-loop
  1303	// state of a successful partial condensation is indistinguishable from never
  1304	// having condensed.

  1313	func resolveShadowRefAndTree(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, shadowBranchName string) (*plumbing.Reference, *object.Tree) {

  1317		var shadowTree *object.Tree
  1318		if ref, refErr := repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName), true); refErr == nil {

  1320			if sc, scErr := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash()); scErr == nil {
  1321				if st, stErr := sc.Tree(); stErr == nil {
  1322					shadowTree = st
  1323				}
  1324			}
  1325		}
  1326		return shadowRef, shadowTree
  1327	}

   189	// IsTrailerLine reports whether a line matches git trailer format.

   194	// appendTrailerLine appends a single pre-formatted trailer line (e.g. "Key: value")
   195	// to message in trailer-block-aware format. If the message already ends with a
   196	// trailer paragraph the line is joined directly to it; otherwise a blank line is
   197	// inserted first to start a new trailer block.
   198	func appendTrailerLine(message, trailerLine string) string {
   199		trimmed := strings.TrimRight(message, "\n")
   200	
   201		lines := strings.Split(trimmed, "\n")
   202		i := len(lines) - 1
   203		for i >= 0 && strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(lines[i]), "#") {
   204			i--
   205		}
   206	
   207		hasTrailerBlock := false
   208		if i >= 0 {
   209			last := strings.TrimSpace(lines[i])
   210			if last != "" && IsTrailerLine(last) {
   211				for i > 0 {
   212					i--
   213					above := strings.TrimSpace(lines[i])
   214					if strings.HasPrefix(above, "#") {
   215						continue
   216					}
   217					if above == "" {

   219						break
   220					}
   221					if !IsTrailerLine(above) {

   223					}
   224				}
   225			}
   226		}

   228		if hasTrailerBlock {
   229			return trimmed + "\n" + trailerLine + "\n"
   230		}

  1294	// postCommitProcessSessionLocked handles a single session within the PostCommit loop.
  1295	// Pre-resolved git objects (headTree, parentTree) are shared across all sessions;
  1296	// per-session shadow ref/tree are resolved once here and threaded through sub-calls.
  1297	//
  1298	// The third result reports whether this session condensed into checkpointID.
  1299	// It is distinct from the second (the telemetry signal, which is nil for an
  1300	// amend re-condensing an already-reported checkpoint) and cannot be inferred
  1301	// from state afterwards: carry-forward on a partial commit clears
  1302	// LastCheckpointID that condenseAndUpdateState had just set, so the post-loop
  1303	// state of a successful partial condensation is indistinguishable from never
  1304	// having condensed.
  1305	//
  1306	// MUST be called from inside MutateSessionState. Mutations to state are persisted
  1307	// by the caller's outer save — calling this function standalone silently loses
  1308	// every field change (StepCount, FilesTouched, CheckpointTranscriptStart, …).
  1309	// resolveShadowRefAndTree pre-resolves a session's shadow branch ref and tree.
  1310	// These are read 4+ times across sessionHasNewContent, filesOverlapWithContent,
  1311	// CondenseSession, filesWithRemainingAgentChanges, and
  1312	// calculateSessionAttributions. Both are nil when the branch does not exist.
  1313	func resolveShadowRefAndTree(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, shadowBranchName string) (*plumbing.Reference, *object.Tree) {
  1314		_, span := perf.Start(ctx, "resolve_shadow_branch")
  1315		defer span.End()
  1316		var shadowRef *plumbing.Reference
  1317		var shadowTree *object.Tree
  1318		if ref, refErr := repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName), true); refErr == nil {
  1319			shadowRef = ref
  1320			if sc, scErr := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash()); scErr == nil {
  1321				if st, stErr := sc.Tree(); stErr == nil {
  1322					shadowTree = st
  1323				}
  1324			}
  1325		}
  1326		return shadowRef, shadowTree
  1327	}

  1329	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) postCommitProcessSessionLocked(
  1330		ctx context.Context,
  1331		repo *git.Repository,
  1332		state *SessionState,
  1333		transitionCtx *session.TransitionContext,
  1334		checkpointID id.CheckpointID,
  1335		head *plumbing.Reference,
  1336		commit *object.Commit,
  1337		newHead string,
  1338		repoDir string,
  1339		headTree, parentTree *object.Tree,
  1340		committedFileSet map[string]struct{},
  1341		shadowBranchesToDelete map[string]struct{},
  1342		uncondensedActiveOnBranch map[string]bool,
  1343		allAgentFiles map[string]struct{},
  1344		sessionsWithCommittedFiles int,
  1345		condensedTelemetry *commitCondensedEmitter,
  1346	) (newSkillEvents []agent.SkillEvent, condensedSignal *commitCondensedSignal, condensed bool) {
  1347		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")
  1348		shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
  1349		reservedCheckpointID := state.PendingCondensationID()

  1354				slog.String("commit_checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()))

  1363		// don't silently skip data that should have been condensed.
  1364		//
  1365		// For ACTIVE sessions: the commit has a checkpoint trailer (verified above),
  1366		// meaning PrepareCommitMsg already determined this commit is session-related.
  1367		// The trailer is only added when either:
  1368		//   - No TTY (agent/subagent committing) — added unconditionally
  1369		//   - TTY (human committing) — added after content detection confirmed agent work
  1370		// In both cases, PrepareCommitMsg already validated this commit. We trust
  1371		// that decision here. Transcript-based re-validation is unreliable because
  1372		// subagent transcripts may not be available yet (subagent still running).

  1375		if state.Phase.IsActive() {

  1377		} else {

  1383					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1384					slog.String("error", contentErr.Error()),
  1385				)
  1386			}
  1387		}

  1416			repo:                       repo,
  1417			checkpointID:               checkpointID,
  1418			head:                       head,
  1419			commit:                     commit,
  1420			newHead:                    newHead,
  1421			repoDir:                    repoDir,
  1422			shadowBranchName:           shadowBranchName,
  1423			shadowBranchesToDelete:     shadowBranchesToDelete,
  1424			committedFileSet:           committedFileSet,
  1425			hasNew:                     hasNew,
  1426			filesTouchedBefore:         filesTouchedBefore,
  1427			headTree:                   headTree,
  1428			parentTree:                 parentTree,
  1429			shadowRef:                  shadowRef,
  1430			shadowTree:                 shadowTree,

  1442		// Record checkpoint ID for ACTIVE sessions so HandleTurnEnd can finalize
  1443		// with full transcript. IDLE/ENDED sessions already have complete transcripts.
  1444		// NOTE: This check runs AFTER TransitionAndLog updated the phase. It relies on
  1445		// ACTIVE + GitCommit → ACTIVE (phase stays ACTIVE). If that state machine

  1451		// Carry forward remaining uncommitted files so the next commit gets its
  1452		// own checkpoint ID. This applies to ALL phases — if a user splits their
  1453		// commit across two `git commit` invocations, each gets a 1:1 checkpoint.
  1454		// Uses content-aware comparison: if user did `git add -p` and committed
  1455		// partial changes, the file still has remaining agent changes to carry forward.
  1456		// Guest-linked sessions are excluded: remaining-files would diff the home
  1457		// worktree's shadow tree against THIS worktree's commit, and carry-forward
  1458		// reads file content from THIS worktree — both would rewrite the home
  1459		// worktree's shadow state with foreign data (see condenseAndUpdateState).
  1460		_, carryForwardSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "carry_forward_files")

  1462			remainingFiles := filesWithRemainingAgentChanges(ctx, repo, shadowBranchName, commit, filesTouchedBefore, committedFileSet, overlapOpts{
  1463				headTree:   headTree,
  1464				shadowTree: shadowTree,
  1465			})
  1466			state.FilesTouched = remainingFiles
  1467			logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: carry-forward decision (content-aware)",
  1468				slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1469				slog.Int("files_touched_before", len(filesTouchedBefore)),
  1470				slog.Int("committed_files", len(committedFileSet)),
  1471				slog.Int("remaining_files", len(remainingFiles)),
  1472				slog.Any("remaining", remainingFiles),
  1473				slog.Any("committed_files", committedFileSet),
  1474			)
  1475			if len(remainingFiles) > 0 {
  1476				s.carryForwardToNewShadowBranch(ctx, repo, state, remainingFiles)
  1477			}
  1478	
  1479			// Clear filesystem prompt.txt only when ALL files are committed.
  1480			// If carry-forward files remain, the prompt must persist so the next
  1481			// condensation (triggered by the next commit) can read it.
  1482			if len(state.FilesTouched) == 0 {
  1483				clearFilesystemPrompt(ctx, state.SessionID)
  1484			}
  1485		}
  1486		carryForwardSpan.End()
  1487	
  1488		// Mark ENDED sessions as fully condensed when there's nothing left to do.
  1489		// Either we just condensed (no carry-forward remains) or there was never any
  1490		// new content. PostCommit will skip these on future commits; they persist only
  1491		// for LastCheckpointID (amend trailer restoration).
  1492		if state.Phase == session.PhaseEnded && len(state.FilesTouched) == 0 && (handler.condensed || !hasNew) {
  1493			state.FullyCondensed = true
  1494		}
  1495	
  1496		// Pin a review session to the single checkpoint it was just condensed into.
  1497		// A review is a read-only one-shot: it touches no files, so it never accrues
  1498		// shadow-branch content and the FullyCondensed branch above never fires for
  1499		// it. Left active, it stays in this worktree's session set and gets
  1500		// re-condensed into every subsequent commit — which is how one review ends
  1501		// up attributed to many unrelated checkpoints (its prompt rendering once per
  1502		// checkpoint on the session page). Once condensed, its transcript is captured
  1503		// and it has nothing further to contribute, so mark it terminal here. Gated
  1504		// on handler.condensed so it only fires after the review actually landed in a
  1505		// checkpoint — a review skipped by the read-only gate is never written to a
  1506		// checkpoint and stays eligible to attach to a later one.
  1507		if state.Kind.IsReview() && handler.condensed {

  1509				endedAt := time.Now().UTC()
  1510				state.EndedAt = &endedAt
  1511			}
  1512			state.Phase = session.PhaseEnded
  1513			state.FullyCondensed = true
  1514		}

  1516		// State is saved by the outer MutateSessionState in PostCommit.
  1517	
  1518		// Only preserve shadow branch for active sessions that were NOT condensed.
  1519		// Condensed sessions already have their data on entire/checkpoints/v1.
  1520		if state.Phase.IsActive() && !handler.condensed {
  1521			uncondensedActiveOnBranch[shadowBranchName] = true
  1522		}
  1523	
  1524		return handler.newSkillEvents, handler.condensedSignal, handler.condensed
  1525	}

   479		// NOTE: TTY confirmation (askConfirmTTY) is intentionally NOT wrapped in a span
   480		// because it blocks on user input and would skew timing.
   481		switch source {
   482		case "message":
   483			// Using -m or -F: behavior depends on TTY availability and commit_linking setting
   484			switch {
   485			case !interactive.CanPromptInteractively():
   486				// No TTY (agent subprocess, CI) — auto-link without prompting
   487				message = addCheckpointTrailer(message, checkpointID)
   488			case commitLinking == settings.CommitLinkingAlways:
   489				// User previously chose "always" — auto-link without prompting
   490				message = addCheckpointTrailer(message, checkpointID)
   491			default:
   492				// Human at terminal — prompt interactively
   493				header := "Entire: Active " + string(agentType) + " session detected"

14	// Trailer key constants used in commit messages.
    15	const (
    16		// MetadataTrailerKey points to the metadata directory within a commit tree.
    17		MetadataTrailerKey = "Entire-Metadata"
    18	
    19		// MetadataTaskTrailerKey points to the task metadata directory for subagent checkpoints.
    20		MetadataTaskTrailerKey = "Entire-Metadata-Task"
    21	
    22		// StrategyTrailerKey indicates which strategy created the commit.
    23		StrategyTrailerKey = "Entire-Strategy"
    24	
    25		// BaseCommitTrailerKey links shadow commits to their base code commit.
    26		BaseCommitTrailerKey = "Base-Commit"
    27	
    28		// SessionTrailerKey identifies which session created a commit.
    29		SessionTrailerKey = "Entire-Session"
    30	
    31		// CondensationTrailerKey identifies the condensation ID for a commit (legacy).
    32		CondensationTrailerKey = "Entire-Condensation"
    33	
    34		// SourceRefTrailerKey links code commits to their metadata on a shadow/metadata branch.
    35		// Format: "<branch>@<commit-hash>" e.g. "entire/metadata@abc123def456"
    36		SourceRefTrailerKey = "Entire-Source-Ref"
    37	
    38		// CheckpointTrailerKey links commits to their checkpoint metadata on entire/checkpoints/v1.
    39		// Format: a checkpoint ID — either a legacy 12-hex ID (e.g. "a3b2c4d5e6f7")
    40		// or a 26-char ULID (see checkpoint/id.CheckpointPattern).
    41		// This trailer survives git amend and rebase operations.
    42		CheckpointTrailerKey = "Entire-Checkpoint"
    43	
    44		// EphemeralBranchTrailerKey identifies the shadow branch that a checkpoint originated from.
    45		// Used in manual-commit strategy checkpoint commits on entire/checkpoints/v1 branch.
    46		// Format: full branch name e.g. "entire/2b4c177"
    47		EphemeralBranchTrailerKey = "Ephemeral-branch"
    48	
    49		// AgentTrailerKey identifies the agent that created a checkpoint.
    50		// Format: human-readable agent name e.g. "Claude Code", "Cursor"
    51		AgentTrailerKey = "Entire-Agent"
    52	
    53		// OPFAppliedTrailerKey marks an entire/checkpoints/v1 commit whose blobs
    54		// have been redacted by the OpenAI Privacy Filter (the opt-in 9th,
    55		// network-backed layer, applied on top of the 8 regex layers).
    56		// Format: literal "true"; the trailer is omitted entirely when OPF was
    57		// not applied. The pre-push rewrite path treats commits lacking this
    58		// trailer as candidates to OPF-redact before they reach the remote.
    59		OPFAppliedTrailerKey = "Entire-OPF-Applied"
    60	
    61		// OPFAppliedTrailerValue is the only value that means "OPF ran." Any
    62		// other value (or trailer absence) is treated as "not applied" so a
    63		// future "false" / "skipped" value never accidentally enables OPF.
    64		OPFAppliedTrailerValue = "true"
    65	)
    66	
    67	// Pre-compiled regexes for trailer parsing.
    68	var (
    69		metadataTrailerRegex     = regexp.MustCompile(MetadataTrailerKey + `:\s*(.+)`)
    70		taskMetadataTrailerRegex = regexp.MustCompile(MetadataTaskTrailerKey + `:\s*(.+)`)
    71		sessionTrailerRegex      = regexp.MustCompile(SessionTrailerKey + `:\s*(.+)`)
    72		checkpointTrailerRegex   = regexp.MustCompile(CheckpointTrailerKey + `:\s*(` + checkpointID.CheckpointPattern + `)(?:\s|$)`)
    73	)

    75	// ParseMetadata extracts metadata dir from commit message.
    76	// Returns the metadata directory and true if found, empty string and false otherwise.
    77	func ParseMetadata(commitMessage string) (string, bool) {
    78		matches := metadataTrailerRegex.FindStringSubmatch(commitMessage)
    79		if len(matches) > 1 {
    80			return strings.TrimSpace(matches[1]), true
    81		}
    82		return "", false
    83	}
    84

    87	func ParseTaskMetadata(commitMessage string) (string, bool) {
    88		matches := taskMetadataTrailerRegex.FindStringSubmatch(commitMessage)
    89		if len(matches) > 1 {
    90			return strings.TrimSpace(matches[1]), true
    91		}
    92		return "", false
    93	}
    94	
    95	// ParseSession extracts the session ID from a commit message.
    96	// Returns the session ID and true if found, empty string and false otherwise.
    97	// Note: If multiple Entire-Session trailers exist, this returns only the first one.
    98	func ParseSession(commitMessage string) (string, bool) {
    99		matches := sessionTrailerRegex.FindStringSubmatch(commitMessage)
   100		if len(matches) > 1 {
   101			return strings.TrimSpace(matches[1]), true
   102		}
   103		return "", false
   104	}
   105	
   106	// ParseCheckpoint extracts the checkpoint ID from a commit message.
   107	// Returns the CheckpointID and true if found, empty ID and false otherwise.
   108	func ParseCheckpoint(commitMessage string) (checkpointID.CheckpointID, bool) {
   109		matches := checkpointTrailerRegex.FindStringSubmatch(commitMessage)
   110		if len(matches) > 1 {
   111			idStr := strings.TrimSpace(matches[1])
   112			// Validate it's a proper checkpoint ID
   113			if cpID, err := checkpointID.NewCheckpointID(idStr); err == nil {
   114				return cpID, true
   115			}
   116		}
   117		return checkpointID.EmptyCheckpointID, false
   118	}
   119	
   120	// ParseAllCheckpoints extracts all checkpoint IDs from a commit message.
   121	// Returns a slice of CheckpointIDs (may be empty if none found).
   122	// Duplicate IDs are deduplicated while preserving order.
   123	// This is useful for squash merge commits that contain multiple Entire-Checkpoint trailers.
   124	func ParseAllCheckpoints(commitMessage string) []checkpointID.CheckpointID {
   125		matches := checkpointTrailerRegex.FindAllStringSubmatch(commitMessage, -1)
   126		if len(matches) == 0 {
   127			return nil
   128		}
   129	
   130		seen := make(map[string]bool)
   131		ids := make([]checkpointID.CheckpointID, 0, len(matches))
   132		for _, match := range matches {
   133			if len(match) > 1 {
   134				idStr := strings.TrimSpace(match[1])
   135				if !seen[idStr] {
   136					if cpID, err := checkpointID.NewCheckpointID(idStr); err == nil {
   137						seen[idStr] = true
   138						ids = append(ids, cpID)
   139					}
   140				}
   141			}
   142		}
   143		return ids
   144	}

   146	// FormatSourceRef creates a formatted source ref string for the trailer.
   147	// Format: "<branch>@<commit-hash-prefix>" (hash truncated to ShortIDLength chars)
   148	func FormatSourceRef(branch, commitHash string) string {
   149		shortHash := commitHash
   150		if len(shortHash) > checkpointID.ShortIDLength {
   151			shortHash = shortHash[:checkpointID.ShortIDLength]
   152		}
   153		return fmt.Sprintf("%s@%s", branch, shortHash)
   154	}

   156	// FormatShadowCommit creates a commit message for manual-commit strategy checkpoints.
   157	// Includes Entire-Metadata, Entire-Session, and Entire-Strategy trailers.
   158	func FormatShadowCommit(message, metadataDir, sessionID string) string {

   165		return sb.String()
   166	}

   174		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%s: %s\n", MetadataTaskTrailerKey, taskMetadataDir)
   175		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%s: %s\n", SessionTrailerKey, sessionID)
