    14	
    15	// BackendTypeGitBranch is the built-in git-branch checkpoint backend: it stores
    16	// the committed record on a git branch (entire/checkpoints/v1) in this repo. It
    17	// is git-backed (see registeredBackend.gitBacked) and is the default primary
    18	// when no backend is configured.
    19	const BackendTypeGitBranch = "git-branch"
    20	
    21	// BackendTypeGitRefs is the built-in git-refs checkpoint backend: it stores the
    22	// committed record as one git ref per checkpoint (refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/
    23	// <id>) in this repo. Like git-branch it is git-backed, so it may be the primary;
    24	// the two can run side by side (git-refs primary + git-branch mirror) during the
    25	// branch->refs rollout, since the one-of-each-type rule permits distinct
    26	// git-backed backends in the same topology.
    27	const BackendTypeGitRefs = "git-refs"
    28	
    29	// OpenEnv carries the construction context a backend factory may need.
    30	// Git-backed backends require Repo and use Refs/BlobFetcher/RefFetcher/
    31	// RemoteRefLister; other backends ignore the git-shaped fields and read their
    32	// own configuration from cfg.
    33	type OpenEnv struct {
    34		Repo                  *git.Repository
    35		BlobFetcher           BlobFetchFunc
    36		RefFetcher            RefFetchFunc
    37		RemoteRefLister       RemoteRefListFunc
    38		MetadataBranchFetcher MetadataBranchFetchFunc
    39		Refs                  PersistentRefs
    40		// ReadRemotes is the ordered checkpoint read-candidate chain; see
    41		// OpenOptions.ReadRemotes.
    42		ReadRemotes []string
    43	}
    44	
    45	// Factory constructs a persistent store for one backend type. cfg is the
    46	// backend-specific JSON "config" block from settings (nil when absent).
    47	type Factory func(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, cfg json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error)
    48	
    49	// registeredBackend is a factory plus the capabilities the topology layer needs.
    50	type registeredBackend struct {
    51		factory Factory
    52		// gitBacked reports whether the backend stores the committed record in this
    53		// repo's git object store. Only git-backed backends may be the primary,
    54		// because the checkpoint lifecycle (resume bootstrap, doctor reconcile,
    55		// explain tree-read, push, cleanup, pre-push OPF) drives the primary's record
    56		// through the repo and its refs — see buildPrimary. A backend that is not
    57		// git-backed has no such ref for those paths to operate on, so it is
    58		// mirror-only (write fan-out) until that lifecycle moves behind the store.
    59		// Whether a backend may be a *mirror* is governed separately by the
    60		// one-of-each-type topology rule in buildMirrors, not by this flag (a
    61		// git-backed backend can mirror alongside a different git-backed primary).
    62		gitBacked bool
    63	}
    64	
    65	var (
    66		registryMu sync.RWMutex
    67		// registry maps backend type to its factory and capabilities. Git-backed
    68		// backends are built in (registered here). Other backends add themselves
    69		// through Register — in practice only test-only backends do, via their
    70		// RegisterForTesting helpers, so a production binary can never select them.
    71		registry = map[string]registeredBackend{
    72			BackendTypeGitBranch: {factory: gitBranchBackendFactory, gitBacked: true},
    73			BackendTypeGitRefs:   {factory: gitRefsBackendFactory, gitBacked: true},
    74		}
    75	)
    76	
    77	// Register adds a non-git-backed backend factory under typ. Such backends can
    78	// serve as mirrors but not as the primary (see registeredBackend.gitBacked).
    79	// Git-backed backends are built in and not registered through this path. It
    80	// panics on a duplicate type to surface wiring mistakes.
    81	func Register(typ string, f Factory) {
    82		registryMu.Lock()
    83		defer registryMu.Unlock()
    84		if _, exists := registry[typ]; exists {
    85			panic(fmt.Sprintf("checkpoint: backend type %q already registered", typ))
    86		}
    87		registry[typ] = registeredBackend{factory: f, gitBacked: false}
    88	}
    89	
    90	// lookupBackend returns the registered backend for typ, or a clear error
    91	// (naming the registered types) when the type is unknown.
    92	func lookupBackend(typ string) (registeredBackend, error) {
    93		registryMu.RLock()
    94		b, ok := registry[typ]
    95		registryMu.RUnlock()
    96		if !ok {
    97			return registeredBackend{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown checkpoint backend type %q (registered: %s)", typ, registeredTypes())
    98		}
    99		return b, nil
   100	}
   101	
   102	// ValidatePrimaryBackend reports an error unless typ names a registered backend
   103	// that may serve as the primary. An unknown type is rejected with an error
   104	// listing the registered backend types; a registered but non-git-backed type is
   105	// rejected separately, since only git-backed backends may be the primary. This
   106	// is the single source of the "primary must be git-backed" rule — buildPrimary
   107	// delegates here, and selection surfaces (entire enable / configure
   108	// --checkpoint-backend) call it to reject a bad backend before writing it to
   109	// settings, rather than failing later in Open.
   110	func ValidatePrimaryBackend(typ string) error {
   111		b, err := lookupBackend(typ)
   112		if err != nil {
   113			return err
   114		}
   115		if !b.gitBacked {
   116			return fmt.Errorf("checkpoint backend %q cannot be the primary: only git-backed backends (e.g. %q, %q) may be the primary", typ, BackendTypeGitBranch, BackendTypeGitRefs)
   117		}
   118		return nil
   119	}
   120	
   121	// build constructs the store for the named backend type.
   122	func build(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, typ string, cfg json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {
   123		b, err := lookupBackend(typ)
   124		if err != nil {
   125			return nil, err
   126		}
   127		store, err := b.factory(ctx, env, cfg)
   128		if err != nil {
   129			return nil, fmt.Errorf("construct %q checkpoint backend: %w", typ, err)
   130		}
   131		return store, nil
   132	}
   133	
   134	func registeredTypes() string {
   135		registryMu.RLock()
   136		defer registryMu.RUnlock()
   137		types := make([]string, 0, len(registry))
   138		for t := range registry {
   139			types = append(types, t)
   140		}
   141		sort.Strings(types)
   142		return strings.Join(types, ", ")
   143	}

   145	// gitBranchBackendFactory builds the git-branch persistent store from the open
   146	// environment. It ignores cfg: git topology comes from env.Refs, not settings.
   147	func gitBranchBackendFactory(_ context.Context, env OpenEnv, _ json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {

   157			store.SetMetadataBranchFetcher(env.MetadataBranchFetcher)
   158		}
   159		return store, nil
   160	}

   172	// the primary's record through the repo and its refs, so a non-git-backed
   173	// primary is rejected rather than silently half-supported.

   183	// the primary's type or another mirror's. This is the conservative form of "no
   184	// two backends may write the same target": today two backends of the same type

   188	// repo/refs) could relax this; for now it is one of each type.

     2	
     3	import (
     4		"context"
     5		"encoding/json"
     6		"errors"
     7		"fmt"
     8		"sort"
     9		"strings"
    10		"sync"
    11	
    12		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6"
    13	)
    14	
    15	// BackendTypeGitBranch is the built-in git-branch checkpoint backend: it stores
    16	// the committed record on a git branch (entire/checkpoints/v1) in this repo. It
    17	// is git-backed (see registeredBackend.gitBacked) and is the default primary
    18	// when no backend is configured.
    19	const BackendTypeGitBranch = "git-branch"
    20	
    21	// BackendTypeGitRefs is the built-in git-refs checkpoint backend: it stores the
    22	// committed record as one git ref per checkpoint (refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/
    23	// <id>) in this repo. Like git-branch it is git-backed, so it may be the primary;
    24	// the two can run side by side (git-refs primary + git-branch mirror) during the
    25	// branch->refs rollout, since the one-of-each-type rule permits distinct
    26	// git-backed backends in the same topology.
    27	const BackendTypeGitRefs = "git-refs"
    28	
    29	// OpenEnv carries the construction context a backend factory may need.
    30	// Git-backed backends require Repo and use Refs/BlobFetcher/RefFetcher/
    31	// RemoteRefLister; other backends ignore the git-shaped fields and read their
    32	// own configuration from cfg.
    33	type OpenEnv struct {
    34		Repo                  *git.Repository
    35		BlobFetcher           BlobFetchFunc
    36		RefFetcher            RefFetchFunc
    37		RemoteRefLister       RemoteRefListFunc
    38		MetadataBranchFetcher MetadataBranchFetchFunc
    39		Refs                  PersistentRefs
    40		// ReadRemotes is the ordered checkpoint read-candidate chain; see
    41		// OpenOptions.ReadRemotes.
    42		ReadRemotes []string
    43	}
    44	
    45	// Factory constructs a persistent store for one backend type. cfg is the
    46	// backend-specific JSON "config" block from settings (nil when absent).
    47	type Factory func(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, cfg json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error)
    48	
    49	// registeredBackend is a factory plus the capabilities the topology layer needs.
    50	type registeredBackend struct {
    51		factory Factory
    52		// gitBacked reports whether the backend stores the committed record in this
    53		// repo's git object store. Only git-backed backends may be the primary,
    54		// because the checkpoint lifecycle (resume bootstrap, doctor reconcile,
    55		// explain tree-read, push, cleanup, pre-push OPF) drives the primary's record
    56		// through the repo and its refs — see buildPrimary. A backend that is not
    57		// git-backed has no such ref for those paths to operate on, so it is
    58		// mirror-only (write fan-out) until that lifecycle moves behind the store.
    59		// Whether a backend may be a *mirror* is governed separately by the
    60		// one-of-each-type topology rule in buildMirrors, not by this flag (a
    61		// git-backed backend can mirror alongside a different git-backed primary).
    62		gitBacked bool
    63	}
    64	
    65	var (
    66		registryMu sync.RWMutex
    67		// registry maps backend type to its factory and capabilities. Git-backed
    68		// backends are built in (registered here). Other backends add themselves
    69		// through Register — in practice only test-only backends do, via their
    70		// RegisterForTesting helpers, so a production binary can never select them.
    71		registry = map[string]registeredBackend{
    72			BackendTypeGitBranch: {factory: gitBranchBackendFactory, gitBacked: true},
    73			BackendTypeGitRefs:   {factory: gitRefsBackendFactory, gitBacked: true},
    74		}
    75	)
    76	
    77	// Register adds a non-git-backed backend factory under typ. Such backends can
    78	// serve as mirrors but not as the primary (see registeredBackend.gitBacked).
    79	// Git-backed backends are built in and not registered through this path. It
    80	// panics on a duplicate type to surface wiring mistakes.
    81	func Register(typ string, f Factory) {
    82		registryMu.Lock()
    83		defer registryMu.Unlock()
    84		if _, exists := registry[typ]; exists {
    85			panic(fmt.Sprintf("checkpoint: backend type %q already registered", typ))
    86		}
    87		registry[typ] = registeredBackend{factory: f, gitBacked: false}
    88	}
    89	
    90	// lookupBackend returns the registered backend for typ, or a clear error
    91	// (naming the registered types) when the type is unknown.
    92	func lookupBackend(typ string) (registeredBackend, error) {
    93		registryMu.RLock()
    94		b, ok := registry[typ]
    95		registryMu.RUnlock()
    96		if !ok {
    97			return registeredBackend{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown checkpoint backend type %q (registered: %s)", typ, registeredTypes())
    98		}
    99		return b, nil
   100	}
   101	
   102	// ValidatePrimaryBackend reports an error unless typ names a registered backend
   103	// that may serve as the primary. An unknown type is rejected with an error
   104	// listing the registered backend types; a registered but non-git-backed type is
   105	// rejected separately, since only git-backed backends may be the primary. This
   106	// is the single source of the "primary must be git-backed" rule — buildPrimary
   107	// delegates here, and selection surfaces (entire enable / configure
   108	// --checkpoint-backend) call it to reject a bad backend before writing it to
   109	// settings, rather than failing later in Open.
   110	func ValidatePrimaryBackend(typ string) error {
   111		b, err := lookupBackend(typ)
   112		if err != nil {
   113			return err
   114		}
   115		if !b.gitBacked {
   116			return fmt.Errorf("checkpoint backend %q cannot be the primary: only git-backed backends (e.g. %q, %q) may be the primary", typ, BackendTypeGitBranch, BackendTypeGitRefs)
   117		}
   118		return nil
   119	}
   120	
   121	// build constructs the store for the named backend type.
   122	func build(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, typ string, cfg json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {
   123		b, err := lookupBackend(typ)
   124		if err != nil {
   125			return nil, err
   126		}
   127		store, err := b.factory(ctx, env, cfg)
   128		if err != nil {
   129			return nil, fmt.Errorf("construct %q checkpoint backend: %w", typ, err)
   130		}
   131		return store, nil
   132	}
   133	
   134	func registeredTypes() string {
   135		registryMu.RLock()
   136		defer registryMu.RUnlock()
   137		types := make([]string, 0, len(registry))
   138		for t := range registry {
   139			types = append(types, t)
   140		}
   141		sort.Strings(types)
   142		return strings.Join(types, ", ")
   143	}
   144	
   145	// gitBranchBackendFactory builds the git-branch persistent store from the open
   146	// environment. It ignores cfg: git topology comes from env.Refs, not settings.
   147	func gitBranchBackendFactory(_ context.Context, env OpenEnv, _ json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {
   148		if env.Repo == nil {
   149			return nil, errors.New("git-branch checkpoint backend requires a repository")
   150		}
   151		store := NewGitStore(env.Repo, env.Refs)
   152		if env.BlobFetcher != nil {
   153			store.SetBlobFetcher(env.BlobFetcher)
   154		}
   155		store.SetReadRemotes(env.ReadRemotes)
   156		if env.MetadataBranchFetcher != nil {
   157			store.SetMetadataBranchFetcher(env.MetadataBranchFetcher)
   158		}
   159		return store, nil
   160	}
   161	
   162	// gitRefsBackendFactory builds the git-refs persistent store from the open
   163	// environment. It ignores cfg and env.Refs: each checkpoint resolves its own ref
   164	// (refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>) rather than a single configured ref.
   165	func gitRefsBackendFactory(_ context.Context, env OpenEnv, _ json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {
   166		if env.Repo == nil {
   167			return nil, errors.New("git-refs checkpoint backend requires a repository")
   168		}
   169		store := newGitRefsStore(env.Repo)
   170		if env.BlobFetcher != nil {
   171			store.SetBlobFetcher(env.BlobFetcher)
   172		}
   173		if env.RefFetcher != nil {
   174			store.SetRefFetcher(env.RefFetcher)
   175		}
   176		if env.RemoteRefLister != nil {
   177			store.SetRemoteRefLister(env.RemoteRefLister)
   178		}
   179		return store, nil
   180	}

   109	// settings, rather than failing later in Open.

   121	// build constructs the store for the named backend type.
   122	func build(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, typ string, cfg json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {
   123		b, err := lookupBackend(typ)

   135	// real configuration today, since buildPrimary only accepts git-backed backends)
   136	// yields both freshly built git stores.
   137	func buildKindReadStores(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, primaryType string, primary PersistentStore) (branch, refs PersistentStore, err error) {
   138		switch primaryType {
   139		case BackendTypeGitBranch:
   140			branch = primary
   141			refs, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitRefs, nil)
   142		case BackendTypeGitRefs:
   143			refs = primary
   144			branch, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitBranch, nil)
   145		default:
   146			if branch, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitBranch, nil); err == nil {
   147				refs, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitRefs, nil)
   148			}
   149		}
   150		return branch, refs, err
   151	}

   170	// buildPrimary constructs the primary persistent store. The primary must be a
   171	// git-backed backend: attach, resume, push, doctor, cleanup, and OPF all drive
   172	// the primary's record through the repo and its refs, so a non-git-backed
   173	// primary is rejected rather than silently half-supported.
   174	func buildPrimary(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, typ string, raw json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {
   175		if err := ValidatePrimaryBackend(typ); err != nil {
   176			return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.primary: %w", err)
   177		}
   178		return build(ctx, env, typ, raw)
   179	}
   180	
   181	// buildMirrors constructs the mirror writers. Each backend type may appear at
   182	// most once across the topology (primary + mirrors), so a mirror cannot reuse
   183	// the primary's type or another mirror's. This is the conservative form of "no
   184	// two backends may write the same target": today two backends of the same type
   185	// share the same refs/storage, so a duplicate type is a guaranteed collision
   186	// (e.g. a git-branch mirror under a git-branch primary would double-write the v1
   187	// branch). A future per-mirror config (same backend type pointed at a distinct
   188	// repo/refs) could relax this; for now it is one of each type.
   189	func buildMirrors(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, cfg *settings.CheckpointsConfig, primaryType string) ([]Writer, error) {
   190		if cfg == nil || len(cfg.Mirrors) == 0 {
   191			return nil, nil
   192		}
   193		seen := map[string]bool{primaryType: true}
   194		mirrors := make([]Writer, 0, len(cfg.Mirrors))
   195		for i, m := range cfg.Mirrors {
   196			if _, err := lookupBackend(m.Type); err != nil {
   197				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: %w", i, err)
   198			}
   199			if seen[m.Type] {
   200				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: backend type %q is already used by the primary or another mirror; each backend type may appear at most once", i, m.Type)
   201			}
   202			seen[m.Type] = true
   203			// Mirrors are best-effort write-only copies whose failures are logged
   204			// and dropped; never pay on-demand ref-fetch network probes for them.
   205			mirrorEnv := env
   206			mirrorEnv.RefFetcher = nil
   207			store, err := build(ctx, mirrorEnv, m.Type, m.Config)
   208			if err != nil {
   209				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: %w", i, err)
   210			}
   211			mirrors = append(mirrors, store)
   212		}
   213		return mirrors, nil
   214	}

   217		if opts.Refs != nil {
   218			return *opts.Refs
   219		}
   220		return ResolveRefs(ctx)
   221	}

    14	
    15	// BackendTypeGitBranch is the built-in git-branch checkpoint backend: it stores
    16	// the committed record on a git branch (entire/checkpoints/v1) in this repo. It
    17	// is git-backed (see registeredBackend.gitBacked) and is the default primary
    18	// when no backend is configured.
    19	const BackendTypeGitBranch = "git-branch"
    20	
    21	// BackendTypeGitRefs is the built-in git-refs checkpoint backend: it stores the
    22	// committed record as one git ref per checkpoint (refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/
    23	// <id>) in this repo. Like git-branch it is git-backed, so it may be the primary;
    24	// the two can run side by side (git-refs primary + git-branch mirror) during the
    25	// branch->refs rollout, since the one-of-each-type rule permits distinct
    26	// git-backed backends in the same topology.
    27	const BackendTypeGitRefs = "git-refs"
    28	
    29	// OpenEnv carries the construction context a backend factory may need.
    30	// Git-backed backends require Repo and use Refs/BlobFetcher/RefFetcher/
    31	// RemoteRefLister; other backends ignore the git-shaped fields and read their
    32	// own configuration from cfg.
    33	type OpenEnv struct {
    34		Repo                  *git.Repository
    35		BlobFetcher           BlobFetchFunc
    36		RefFetcher            RefFetchFunc
    37		RemoteRefLister       RemoteRefListFunc
    38		MetadataBranchFetcher MetadataBranchFetchFunc
    39		Refs                  PersistentRefs
    40		// ReadRemotes is the ordered checkpoint read-candidate chain; see
    41		// OpenOptions.ReadRemotes.
    42		ReadRemotes []string
    43	}
    44	
    45	// Factory constructs a persistent store for one backend type. cfg is the
    46	// backend-specific JSON "config" block from settings (nil when absent).
    47	type Factory func(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, cfg json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error)
    48	
    49	// registeredBackend is a factory plus the capabilities the topology layer needs.
    50	type registeredBackend struct {
    51		factory Factory
    52		// gitBacked reports whether the backend stores the committed record in this
    53		// repo's git object store. Only git-backed backends may be the primary,
    54		// because the checkpoint lifecycle (resume bootstrap, doctor reconcile,
    55		// explain tree-read, push, cleanup, pre-push OPF) drives the primary's record
    56		// through the repo and its refs — see buildPrimary. A backend that is not
    57		// git-backed has no such ref for those paths to operate on, so it is
    58		// mirror-only (write fan-out) until that lifecycle moves behind the store.
    59		// Whether a backend may be a *mirror* is governed separately by the
    60		// one-of-each-type topology rule in buildMirrors, not by this flag (a
    61		// git-backed backend can mirror alongside a different git-backed primary).
    62		gitBacked bool
    63	}
    64	
    65	var (
    66		registryMu sync.RWMutex
    67		// registry maps backend type to its factory and capabilities. Git-backed
    68		// backends are built in (registered here). Other backends add themselves
    69		// through Register — in practice only test-only backends do, via their
    70		// RegisterForTesting helpers, so a production binary can never select them.
    71		registry = map[string]registeredBackend{
    72			BackendTypeGitBranch: {factory: gitBranchBackendFactory, gitBacked: true},
    73			BackendTypeGitRefs:   {factory: gitRefsBackendFactory, gitBacked: true},
    74		}
    75	)
    76	
    77	// Register adds a non-git-backed backend factory under typ. Such backends can
    78	// serve as mirrors but not as the primary (see registeredBackend.gitBacked).
    79	// Git-backed backends are built in and not registered through this path. It
    80	// panics on a duplicate type to surface wiring mistakes.
    81	func Register(typ string, f Factory) {
    82		registryMu.Lock()
    83		defer registryMu.Unlock()
    84		if _, exists := registry[typ]; exists {
    85			panic(fmt.Sprintf("checkpoint: backend type %q already registered", typ))
    86		}
    87		registry[typ] = registeredBackend{factory: f, gitBacked: false}
    88	}
    89	
    90	// lookupBackend returns the registered backend for typ, or a clear error
    91	// (naming the registered types) when the type is unknown.
    92	func lookupBackend(typ string) (registeredBackend, error) {
    93		registryMu.RLock()
    94		b, ok := registry[typ]
    95		registryMu.RUnlock()
    96		if !ok {
    97			return registeredBackend{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown checkpoint backend type %q (registered: %s)", typ, registeredTypes())
    98		}
    99		return b, nil
   100	}
   101	
   102	// ValidatePrimaryBackend reports an error unless typ names a registered backend
   103	// that may serve as the primary. An unknown type is rejected with an error
   104	// listing the registered backend types; a registered but non-git-backed type is
   105	// rejected separately, since only git-backed backends may be the primary. This
   106	// is the single source of the "primary must be git-backed" rule — buildPrimary
   107	// delegates here, and selection surfaces (entire enable / configure
   108	// --checkpoint-backend) call it to reject a bad backend before writing it to
   109	// settings, rather than failing later in Open.
   110	func ValidatePrimaryBackend(typ string) error {
   111		b, err := lookupBackend(typ)
   112		if err != nil {
   113			return err
   114		}
   115		if !b.gitBacked {
   116			return fmt.Errorf("checkpoint backend %q cannot be the primary: only git-backed backends (e.g. %q, %q) may be the primary", typ, BackendTypeGitBranch, BackendTypeGitRefs)
   117		}
   118		return nil
   119	}
   120	
   121	// build constructs the store for the named backend type.
   122	func build(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, typ string, cfg json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {
   123		b, err := lookupBackend(typ)
   124		if err != nil {
   125			return nil, err
   126		}
   127		store, err := b.factory(ctx, env, cfg)
   128		if err != nil {
   129			return nil, fmt.Errorf("construct %q checkpoint backend: %w", typ, err)
   130		}
   131		return store, nil
   132	}
   133	
   134	func registeredTypes() string {
   135		registryMu.RLock()
   136		defer registryMu.RUnlock()
   137		types := make([]string, 0, len(registry))
   138		for t := range registry {
   139			types = append(types, t)
   140		}
   141		sort.Strings(types)
   142		return strings.Join(types, ", ")
   143	}
   144	
   145	// gitBranchBackendFactory builds the git-branch persistent store from the open
   146	// environment. It ignores cfg: git topology comes from env.Refs, not settings.
   147	func gitBranchBackendFactory(_ context.Context, env OpenEnv, _ json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {
   148		if env.Repo == nil {
   149			return nil, errors.New("git-branch checkpoint backend requires a repository")
   150		}
   151		store := NewGitStore(env.Repo, env.Refs)
   152		if env.BlobFetcher != nil {
   153			store.SetBlobFetcher(env.BlobFetcher)
   154		}
   155		store.SetReadRemotes(env.ReadRemotes)
   156		if env.MetadataBranchFetcher != nil {
   157			store.SetMetadataBranchFetcher(env.MetadataBranchFetcher)
   158		}
   159		return store, nil
   160	}
   161	
   162	// gitRefsBackendFactory builds the git-refs persistent store from the open
   163	// environment. It ignores cfg and env.Refs: each checkpoint resolves its own ref
   164	// (refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>) rather than a single configured ref.
   165	func gitRefsBackendFactory(_ context.Context, env OpenEnv, _ json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {
   166		if env.Repo == nil {
   167			return nil, errors.New("git-refs checkpoint backend requires a repository")
   168		}
   169		store := newGitRefsStore(env.Repo)
   170		if env.BlobFetcher != nil {
   171			store.SetBlobFetcher(env.BlobFetcher)
   172		}
   173		if env.RefFetcher != nil {
   174			store.SetRefFetcher(env.RefFetcher)
   175		}
   176		if env.RemoteRefLister != nil {
   177			store.SetRemoteRefLister(env.RemoteRefLister)
   178		}
   179		return store, nil
   180	}

    17	// ErrInvalidCheckpointsConfig is returned when a present "checkpoints" settings
    18	// block is malformed (e.g. a backend with no type).
    19	var ErrInvalidCheckpointsConfig = errors.New("invalid checkpoints config")
    20	
    21	// Environment overrides for checkpoint backend selection. When EnvCheckpointsPrimary
    22	// is set, it (and the optional comma-separated EnvCheckpointsMirrors) fully
    23	// replaces any checkpoints block in settings — env wins over file, matching the
    24	// other ENTIRE_* overrides (ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL, ENTIRE_TOKEN, …). Primarily for
    25	// driving e2e/CI and rollout against a specific backend without editing settings.
    26	const (
    27		EnvCheckpointsPrimary = "ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_PRIMARY"
    28		EnvCheckpointsMirrors = "ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_MIRRORS"
    29	)
    30	
    31	// CheckpointsConfig selects checkpoint storage backends: one primary (source of
    32	// truth, serves all reads and writes) and zero or more mirrors (independent
    33	// backends that receive best-effort write fan-out). When absent, the checkpoint
    34	// layer defaults to the built-in git-branch backend with no mirrors.
    35	type CheckpointsConfig struct {
    36		Primary BackendConfig   `json:"primary"`
    37		Mirrors []BackendConfig `json:"mirrors,omitempty"`
    38	}
    39	
    40	// BackendConfig is a discriminated backend selector: Type names the registered
    41	// backend and Config carries the backend-specific options block (opaque here,
    42	// decoded by the backend factory).
    43	type BackendConfig struct {
    44		Type   string          `json:"type"`
    45		Config json.RawMessage `json:"config,omitempty"`
    46	}
    47	
    48	// checkpointsEnvelope extracts only the "checkpoints" key, leaving every other
    49	// settings field untouched so unrelated malformed/unknown settings cannot break
    50	// checkpoint backend resolution.
    51	type checkpointsEnvelope struct {
    52		Checkpoints json.RawMessage `json:"checkpoints"`
    53	}
    54	
    55	// LoadCheckpointsConfig reads the checkpoint backend selection from settings
    56	// without the strict whole-settings validation that Load performs. It is
    57	// deliberately fail-soft: a missing settings file, a whole-file JSON syntax
    58	// error, or unrelated invalid fields all resolve to "no checkpoints config"
    59	// (nil), so checkpoint construction falls back to the default git backend. It
    60	// errors only when a "checkpoints" block is present but itself invalid.
    61	//
    62	// Precedence mirrors Load: a "checkpoints" block in settings.local.json
    63	// replaces the one in settings.json wholesale (this is a selection config, not
    64	// a deep-merged document). Clone preferences carry no checkpoint config and are
    65	// not consulted.
    66	func LoadCheckpointsConfig(ctx context.Context) (*CheckpointsConfig, error) {
    67		// Env override wins over any settings file (precedence like ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL).
    68		if cfg, ok := checkpointsConfigFromEnv(); ok {
    69			if err := cfg.validate(); err != nil {
    70				return nil, err
    71			}
    72			return cfg, nil
    73		}
    74	
    75		base, local, err := checkpointsSettingsPaths(ctx)
    76		if err != nil {
    77			return nil, err
    78		}
    79	
    80		// "local replaces base wholesale": prefer a checkpoints block from local
    81		// settings; fall back to base only when local has none. We extract the raw
    82		// blocks fail-soft, then decode/validate just the one that wins — so a
    83		// malformed block in the overridden file never blocks the file that wins.
    84		raw, src := rawCheckpointsBlock(ctx, local), local
    85		if raw == nil {
    86			raw, src = rawCheckpointsBlock(ctx, base), base
    87		}
    88		if raw == nil {
    89			return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // no checkpoints block present => default git backend
    90		}
    91	
    92		var cfg CheckpointsConfig
    93		dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(raw))
    94		// DisallowUnknownFields surfaces typos (e.g. "primry") instead of silently
    95		// ignoring them. The trade-off is that this CLI is not forward-compatible
    96		// with checkpoints fields added by a newer CLI: an unknown field errors here.
    97		// Adding a field is therefore a coordinated rollout — ship the reader before
    98		// any writer emits the field. The error below points users at that cause.
    99		dec.DisallowUnknownFields()
   100		if err := dec.Decode(&cfg); err != nil {
   101			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w in %s: %w; an unrecognized field can also mean this file was written by a newer CLI — confirm you are on the latest version", ErrInvalidCheckpointsConfig, src, err)
   102		}
   103		if err := cfg.validate(); err != nil {
   104			return nil, err
   105		}
   106		return &cfg, nil
   107	}
   108	
   109	// rawCheckpointsBlock returns the raw "checkpoints" JSON block from filePath, or
   110	// nil when the file is absent/unreadable, has a whole-file syntax error, or has
   111	// no checkpoints block. It never errors: unrelated breakage in a settings file
   112	// must not block checkpoint construction (the strict Load path surfaces it for
   113	// normal commands).
   114	func rawCheckpointsBlock(ctx context.Context, filePath string) json.RawMessage {
   115		data, err := readConfined(filePath)
   116		if err != nil {
   117			if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
   118				// A non-ENOENT read error (bad perms, settings.json is a directory or
   119				// an escaping symlink, etc.) is a broken/untrusted setup; stay
   120				// fail-soft so checkpoint construction defaults to git rather than
   121				// newly failing resume/explain/hooks.
   122				logging.Debug(ctx, "checkpoints config unreadable; defaulting to git backend",
   123					slog.String("path", filePath), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   124			}
   125			return nil
   126		}
   127	
   128		var env checkpointsEnvelope
   129		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &env); err != nil {
   130			// Whole-file parse failure is unrelated breakage; stay fail-soft.
   131			return nil
   132		}
   133		if len(env.Checkpoints) == 0 {
   134			return nil
   135		}
   136		return env.Checkpoints
   137	}
   138	
   139	// checkpointsConfigFromEnv builds a CheckpointsConfig from the environment when
   140	// EnvCheckpointsPrimary is set. Mirrors are taken from EnvCheckpointsMirrors as a
   141	// comma-separated list of backend types (no per-backend config blocks — the env
   142	// override is for backend selection only). Returns ok=false when no primary is
   143	// set, leaving file-based resolution in charge.
   144	func checkpointsConfigFromEnv() (*CheckpointsConfig, bool) {
   145		primary := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(EnvCheckpointsPrimary))
   146		if primary == "" {
   147			return nil, false
   148		}
   149		cfg := &CheckpointsConfig{Primary: BackendConfig{Type: primary}}
   150		for _, m := range strings.Split(os.Getenv(EnvCheckpointsMirrors), ",") {
   151			if t := strings.TrimSpace(m); t != "" {
   152				cfg.Mirrors = append(cfg.Mirrors, BackendConfig{Type: t})
   153			}
   154		}
   155		return cfg, true
   156	}
   157	
   158	func (c *CheckpointsConfig) validate() error {
   159		if c.Primary.Type == "" {
   160			return fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoints.primary.type is required", ErrInvalidCheckpointsConfig)
   161		}
   162		for i, m := range c.Mirrors {
   163			if m.Type == "" {
   164				return fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoints.mirrors[%d].type is required", ErrInvalidCheckpointsConfig, i)
   165			}
   166		}
   167		return nil
   168	}

   174			base, local = worktreeSettingsPaths(worktreeRoot)
   175			return base, local, nil
   176		}
   177		return settingsAbsPaths(ctx)

    16	// CheckpointID identifies a checkpoint. It comes in two formats: a legacy
    17	// 12-character lowercase hex ID and a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (see
    18	// Kind / CheckpointPattern). It links code commits to their checkpoint metadata.
    19	//
    20	//nolint:recvcheck // UnmarshalJSON requires pointer receiver, others use value receiver - standard pattern
    21	type CheckpointID string
    22	
    23	// EmptyCheckpointID represents an unset or invalid checkpoint ID.
    24	const EmptyCheckpointID CheckpointID = ""
    25	
    26	// Pattern is the regex pattern for a legacy checkpoint ID: exactly 12 lowercase
    27	// hex characters. Exported for use in other packages (e.g., trailers) to avoid
    28	// pattern duplication. It is also reused by investigate/provenance for *run IDs*,
    29	// which are always 12-hex — do NOT widen this to include ULIDs; use
    30	// CheckpointPattern for matching a checkpoint ID that may be either format.
    31	const Pattern = `[0-9a-f]{12}`
    32	
    33	// ulidPattern is the regex SHAPE of a ULID checkpoint ID: 26 Crockford base32
    34	// characters (digits plus uppercase A-Z excluding I, L, O, U). It exists only to
    35	// compose CheckpointPattern for extracting a candidate ID from free text; it is
    36	// deliberately NOT exported and NOT the validator. Authoritative validation
    37	// decodes the value via oklog/ulid (see KindOf/isULID), which additionally
    38	// rejects e.g. a timestamp overflow the char class alone would accept.
    39	const ulidPattern = `[REDACTED]{26}`
    40	
    41	// CheckpointPattern matches a checkpoint ID in free text in either format
    42	// (legacy 12-hex or ULID). Use this — not Pattern — when scanning text such as
    43	// the Entire-Checkpoint commit trailer for a candidate checkpoint ID, then
    44	// validate the captured token via NewCheckpointID/Validate (CheckpointPattern is
    45	// a loose shape, not authoritative validation).
    46	const CheckpointPattern = `(?:` + Pattern + `|` + ulidPattern + `)`
    47	
    48	// prefixShapeRegex matches strings shaped like a checkpoint ID or a prefix of
    49	// one: 1-12 lowercase hex characters (legacy) or 1-26 Crockford base32
    50	// characters starting with 0-7 (a ULID's leading timestamp character cannot
    51	// exceed 7, per isULID/ParseStrict). Kept next to Pattern/ulidPattern as a
    52	// reminder to update them together when the ID formats change.
    53	var prefixShapeRegex = regexp.MustCompile(`^(?:[0-9a-f]{1,12}|[0-7][REDACTED]{0,25})$`)
    54	
    55	// CouldBePrefix reports whether s is shaped like a checkpoint ID or a prefix
    56	// of one. It is a cheap gate for callers deciding whether a free-form target
    57	// could name a checkpoint before paying for a store lookup; it is not
    58	// validation (see Validate).
    59	func CouldBePrefix(s string) bool {
    60		return prefixShapeRegex.MatchString(s)
    61	}

    63	// ShortIDLength is the standard length for truncating IDs for display purposes.
    64	// Used for tool use IDs, session IDs, and commit hashes in logs and messages.
    65	const ShortIDLength = 12
    66	
    67	// MaxIDLength is the longest a valid checkpoint ID can be — a 26-character ULID.

    69	// checkpoint ID or a prefix of one, since IDs are no longer fixed-width. Tied to
    70	// oklog/ulid's own encoded-size constant so the three ULID-width sites (this,
    71	// ulidPattern's {26}, and the library) cannot drift apart.

    76	
    77	// isULID reports whether s is a ULID in canonical form, decoded via oklog/ulid —
    78	// the same library that will generate ULIDs — so validation and generation agree
    79	// by construction. ParseStrict enforces the 26-char length, the Crockford
    80	// alphabet, and the timestamp-overflow bound (first character must be 0-7). The
    81	// round-trip (v.String() == s) additionally requires the canonical uppercase
    82	// encoding: it rejects lowercase and Crockford-normalized aliases (e.g. I/L→1,
    83	// O→0) that ParseStrict would otherwise accept but we never emit.
    84	func isULID(s string) bool {
    85		v, err := ulid.ParseStrict(s)

    87	}

    89	// Kind classifies a checkpoint ID by its format: legacy 12-hex or ULID.
    90	type Kind int
    91	
    92	const (
    93		// KindUnknown is a string matching neither the legacy hex nor the ULID format.
    94		KindUnknown Kind = iota
    95		// KindLegacy is a 12-character lowercase hex ID (the format Generate emits).
    96		KindLegacy
    97		// KindULID is a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID.

   102	// string is KindUnknown, which callers handle conservatively.

   106			return KindLegacy

   108			return KindULID
   109		default:
   110			return KindUnknown
   111		}
   112	}
   113	
   114	// Kind classifies this checkpoint ID.
   115	func (id CheckpointID) Kind() Kind {
   116		return KindOf(string(id))
   117	}
   118	
   119	// ShardFor returns the two-character shard for storing this ID under a
   120	// per-checkpoint git ref (refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>): the LAST two
   121	// characters of the ID, for BOTH supported formats.
   122	//
   123	// A single positional rule (independent of the ID's Kind) keeps ref naming
   124	// robust for legacy and ULID IDs alike and impossible to compute inconsistently
   125	// between callers. The suffix spreads checkpoints evenly across buckets for
   126	// either format: a legacy hex ID is random throughout, and a ULID's leading
   127	// characters encode its timestamp (barely varying between nearby checkpoints)
   128	// while its trailing characters are random — so sharding on the suffix keeps the
   129	// distribution even while the ID itself stays lexicographically sortable.
   130	//
   131	// This is the git-refs ref namespace only; the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch tree
   132	// keeps its own independent first-two layout (see Path). For an ID shorter than
   133	// two characters the whole ID is returned.
   134	func (id CheckpointID) ShardFor() string {
   135		s := string(id)

   137			return s
   138		}
   139		return s[len(s)-2:]
   140	}
   141	
   142	// NewCheckpointID creates a CheckpointID from a string, validating its format.
   143	// Returns an error unless the string is a valid checkpoint ID (12-char hex or ULID).
   144	func NewCheckpointID(s string) (CheckpointID, error) {
   145		if err := Validate(s); err != nil {
   146			return EmptyCheckpointID, err
   147		}
   148		return CheckpointID(s), nil
   149	}
   150	
   151	// MustCheckpointID creates a CheckpointID from a string, panicking if invalid.
   152	// Use only when the ID is known to be valid (e.g., from trusted sources).
   153	func MustCheckpointID(s string) CheckpointID {
   154		id, err := NewCheckpointID(s)
   155		if err != nil {
   156			panic(err)
   157		}
   158		return id
   159	}
   160	
   161	// Generate creates a new random 12-character hex checkpoint ID.
   162	//
   163	// Generation stays 12-hex regardless of storage backend. Emitting ULIDs is a
   164	// separate, store-coupled change (new checkpoints get a ULID only under the
   165	// git-refs store); this package only recognizes/validates both formats.
   166	func Generate() (CheckpointID, error) {
   167		bytes := make([]byte, 6) // 6 bytes = 12 hex chars
   168		if _, err := rand.Read(bytes); err != nil {
   169			return EmptyCheckpointID, fmt.Errorf("failed to generate random checkpoint ID: %w", err)
   170		}
   171		return CheckpointID(hex.EncodeToString(bytes)), nil
   172	}
   173	
   174	// GenerateULID creates a new 26-character Crockford base32 ULID checkpoint ID:
   175	// a millisecond timestamp prefix plus crypto-random entropy, so IDs are unique
   176	// and lexicographically time-sortable. It is the format the git-refs store uses
   177	// (chosen by checkpoint.GenerateCheckpointID); the value is canonical and passes
   178	// KindOf/Validate as KindULID.
   179	//
   180	// The timestamp is Unix epoch milliseconds (via ulid.Now), so it is inherently
   181	// timezone-independent — the machine's local zone does not affect the ID.
   182	func GenerateULID() (CheckpointID, error) {
   183		u, err := ulid.New(ulid.Now(), rand.Reader)
   184		if err != nil {
   185			return EmptyCheckpointID, fmt.Errorf("failed to generate ULID checkpoint ID: %w", err)
   186		}
   187		return CheckpointID(u.String()), nil
   188	}
   189	
   190	// Validate checks if a string is a valid checkpoint ID format: either a legacy
   191	// 12-character lowercase hex ID or a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID.
   192	// Returns an error if invalid, nil if valid.
   193	func Validate(s string) error {

   196		}
   197		return nil
   198	}

   200	// String returns the checkpoint ID as a string.
   201	func (id CheckpointID) String() string {
   202		return string(id)
   203	}

   211	// Non-ID strings (e.g. "temporary") are trimmed like the legacy case.
   212	func (id CheckpointID) DisplayShort() string {
   213		s := string(id)
   214		if KindOf(s) == KindULID {
   215			return s
   216		}
   217		if len(s) > ShortIDLength {
   218			return s[:ShortIDLength]
   219		}
   220		return s
   221	}
   222	
   223	// IsEmpty returns true if the checkpoint ID is empty or unset.
   224	func (id CheckpointID) IsEmpty() bool {
   225		return id == EmptyCheckpointID
   226	}

- what gets written into normal Git history versus hidden/special refs
- storage layout
- synchronization/push/pull behavior

Please trace real code paths, naming important packages, types, functions, files, and interfaces.

content.text:
The investigation is now separating two storage planes that are easy to conflate:

- Ephemeral checkpoints are full worktree snapshots on per-worktree “shadow” refs.
- Persistent checkpoints are metadata/transcript records keyed by a stable checkpoint ID; the code supports both the legacy shared metadata branch and newer per-checkpoint Git refs.

Next I’m pinning down the exact record schema and the promotion/commit path between those planes.

   146	func checkpointSubtreePath(base string, segs ...string) string {

   162	// per-checkpoint-ref layout or "<shard>/<id>/" for the v1 branch layout. A nil
   163	// subtree (new checkpoint) yields an empty map.

   199	// root tree hash. The v1 branch always shards on the first two ID characters.

   230	// attribution on the checkpoint's current subtree, returning the new subtree
   231	// hash. Returns ErrCheckpointNotFound when the checkpoint has no root summary.
   232	func (s *treeWriter) applyAttributionBackfill(ctx context.Context, existing *object.Tree, basePath string, combinedAttribution *Attribution) (plumbing.Hash, error) {

   280	func detectFileChanges(ctx context.Context, previouslyUntracked []string, statusFn func(context.Context, *git.Repository) (git.Status, error)) (*FileChanges, error) {
   281		repo, err := openRepository(ctx)
   282		if err != nil {
   283			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open repository: %w", err)
   284		}
   285		defer repo.Close()
   286	
   287		status, err := statusFn(ctx, repo)
   288		if err != nil {
   289			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get status: %w", err)
   290		}
   291	
   292		// Build set of pre-existing untracked files for quick lookup
   293		var preExisting map[string]bool
   294		if previouslyUntracked != nil {
   295			preExisting = make(map[string]bool, len(previouslyUntracked))
   296			for _, f := range previouslyUntracked {
   297				preExisting[f] = true
   298			}
   299		}
   300	
   301		var changes FileChanges
   302		for file, st := range status {
   303			if shouldIgnoreSessionTrackingPath(file) {
   304				continue
   305			}
   306	
   307			switch {
   308			case st.Worktree == git.Untracked:
   309				if preExisting != nil {
   310					if !preExisting[file] {
   311						changes.New = append(changes.New, file)
   312					}
   313				} else {
   314					changes.New = append(changes.New, file)
   315				}
   316			case st.Worktree == git.Deleted || st.Staging == git.Deleted:
   317				changes.Deleted = append(changes.Deleted, file)
   318			case st.Worktree == git.Modified || st.Staging == git.Modified ||
   319				st.Worktree == git.Added || st.Staging == git.Added:
   320				changes.Modified = append(changes.Modified, file)
   321			}
   322		}
   323	
   324		return &changes, nil
   325	}

   327	// filterToUncommittedFiles removes files from the list that are already committed to HEAD
   328	// with matching content. This prevents re-adding files that an agent committed mid-turn
   329	// (already condensed by PostCommit) back to FilesTouched via SaveStep. Files not in
   330	// HEAD or with different content in the working tree are kept. Fails open: if any git
   331	// operation errors, returns the original list unchanged.
   332	func filterToUncommittedFiles(ctx context.Context, files []string, repoRoot string) []string {
   333		if len(files) == 0 {
   334			return files
   335		}
   336	
   337		repo, err := openRepository(ctx)
   338		if err != nil {
   339			return files // fail open
   340		}
   341		defer repo.Close()
   342	
   343		head, err := repo.Head()
   344		if err != nil {
   345			return files // fail open (empty repo, detached HEAD, etc.)
   346		}
   347	
   348		commit, err := repo.CommitObject(head.Hash())
   349		if err != nil {
   350			return files // fail open
   351		}
   352	
   353		headTree, err := commit.Tree()
   354		if err != nil {
   355			return files // fail open
   356		}
   357	
   358		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "filter-uncommitted")
   359	
   360		var result []string
   361		for _, relPath := range files {
   362			headFile, err := headTree.File(relPath)
   363			if err != nil {
   364				// File not in HEAD — it's uncommitted
   365				logging.Debug(logCtx, "file not in HEAD tree, keeping",
   366					slog.String("file", relPath),
   367					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   368				result = append(result, relPath)
   369				continue
   370			}
   371	
   372			// File is in HEAD — compare content with working tree, through the
   373			// worktree's shared root. relPath comes from git, so it is already the
   374			// coordinate the root reads in.
   375			workingContent, ok := readWorktreeFileSafely(repoRoot, relPath)
   376			if !ok {
   377				// Can't read working tree file (deleted?) — keep it
   378				result = append(result, relPath)
   379				continue
   380			}
   381	
   382			headContent, err := headFile.Contents()
   383			if err != nil {
   384				result = append(result, relPath)
   385				continue
   386			}
   387	
   388			if string(workingContent) != headContent {
   389				// Working tree differs from HEAD — uncommitted changes
   390				result = append(result, relPath)
   391			}
   392			// else: content matches HEAD — already committed, skip
   393		}
   394	
   395		return result
   396	}

   474	func untrackedFilesOrSkip(ctx context.Context) (untrackedFiles []string, scanSkipped bool) {

content.text:
At the capture layer, the important mental model is “two witnesses”:

1. The transcript identifies agent-intended edits, prompts, tool/subagent activity, model, skills, and tokens.
2. Git status identifies the actual working-tree delta, including edits made through tools the adapter does not recognize.

Turn-end merges those witnesses, filters infrastructure/out-of-repo paths, and snapshots only uncommitted work. This is why capture can degrade gracefully when one source is incomplete without silently treating every pre-existing untracked file as agent-created.

Refuse what os.Root only confined

The anchors landed in the previous three commits. This is the tail, and
most of it is one bug wearing several hats: os.Root contains a path
without saying anything about what the path is.

fs.WalkDir takes its walk root's DirEntry from fs.Stat, which follows a
symlink, and only the entries below it from ReadDir, which does not.
Every symlink guard here inspected d.Type() inside the callback, so none
of them covered the root: a symlinked .entire/metadata/<session> was
descended into and its target redacted, committed and pushed.
filepath.Walk lstat'd its root, so this was lost in the conversion, not
absent from the start. osroot.WalkDirNoSymlinks lstats the root and
refuses a symlink at both levels; the two checkpoint metadata walks,
clean's tmp walk and doctor's reporter use it. redact.LoadPacks gets the
same check through fs.ReadLinkFS, which os.Root.FS() implements, so it
keeps its fs.FS-only API and its dependency-free position. A symlinked
.entire is refused rather than followed now, so doctor and CLAUDE.md stop
telling the user that intentional setups keep working.

jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicIn leaves <base>.<16 hex>.tmp beside its target,
and .entire/metadata/<session> is copied wholesale into every checkpoint
tree. A hook killed between the create and the rename left an orphan that
was committed on every checkpoint from then on, and ParseChunkIndex read
it back as a transcript CHUNK: fmt.Sscanf("%03d") stops at the first
non-digit, so full.jsonl.123abc...tmp parsed as chunk 123 and was
reassembled into the transcript. Both walks skip jsonutil.IsTempName, and
a chunk suffix must now be entirely digits.

SessionStore resolved its root through osroot.Shared, a registry that
never evicts. searchTranscriptInProjectDirs opens a store for every
candidate directory it walks under an agent's session base dir, so each
probe retained a directory fd for the life of the process, measured at
one per directory against zero for the os.Stat it replaced. A store is
not a long-lived anchor: it opens a root per operation and closes it
again. plugin_install_remote took a shared root on a staging directory it
then RemoveAll'd, with no Forget.

Smaller, same theme: createBlobFromFile read WORKTREE files through
entiredir, binding them to .entire's policy; removeEntireDirectory
guessed cwd for a recursive delete on any WorktreeRoot failure rather
than only on git's positive not-a-repository verdict; the session-state
read path opened a child root with no symlink check, which
osroot.OpenChild now performs; and settings.readConfinedIn was a second
copy of osroot.OpenNoFollow.

The external-agent discovery tests built a fake .git directory and leaned
on settings.Load falling back to a cwd-relative path when the anchor
failed. That fallback is gone, so they name the worktree root in the
context instead. One of them was passing for the wrong reason: a disabled
setting and an unreadable one both end at IsExternalAgentsEnabled
returning false.

Give every tree Entire writes to a single os.Root anchor

Entire does filesystem I/O in six trees, and until now each read and write
assembled its own absolute path and handed it to os.ReadFile/os.WriteFile.
Containment was therefore a property each call site had to keep honouring
by hand, and several of them carried comments saying so outright:
PluginDataDir "guarantees ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR always points inside the
managed data subtree", investigate.RunDir noted that "an unvalidated id
would be a path-traversal sink" feeding os.RemoveAll.

Each tree now has one package that owns a shared *os.Root over it, and the
names that reach those roots are relative to them:

  .entire                    entiredir
  git common dir             gitdir
  the working tree           worktreedir
  an agent's session store   agent.SessionStore
  per-user config / cache    userdirs.ConfigRoot / CacheRoot
  managed plugin tree        pluginRoot

The roots memoize through one registry, osroot.Shared, replacing three
separate copies of that map. Directory creation goes through
osroot.MkdirAllNoSymlink, which refuses a component that already exists as
a symlink -- os.Root blocks a symlink that escapes a root but follows one
pointing elsewhere inside it, and an escaping one otherwise surfaces as an
opaque errno far from the cause. entire doctor reports the symlinks that
are already there.

Two anchors are worth calling out because they close a real gap rather
than formalising an existing one. agent.SessionStore is where a hook
payload's session ID becomes a path via the agent's own
ResolveSessionFile; SessionFile converts the result back to a name inside
the store and rejects an ID that walked out of it, which a plain
filepath.Join produced silently. worktreedir covers the checkpoint tree
entries rewind restores, which may have been fetched from a remote --
rewind's restore half already opened a root for that reason; the reads
beside it did not.

paths.WorktreeRoot is now the single answer to "where is the repository",
and entiredir.anchor falls back to the current directory only on git's
positive ErrNotARepository verdict. The fallback it replaces fired on any
resolve failure, `git` off $PATH included, and then silently gave an agent
working in a subdirectory of a real repo its own .entire beside itself. A
root is only as trustworthy as the directory it is opened on, so a base
that cannot be resolved is not a base to guess at.

settings.readConfined keeps its symlink refusal on every branch, through
one readConfinedIn: the .entire branch briefly read straight through
osroot.ReadFile, which follows an in-root symlink silently -- precisely
the .entire/settings.local.json -> planted.json case the check exists for.

The identifier rename in the previous commit left the prose behind. This
is the prose, plus a handful of comments that described the restore path
#2178 deleted.

points found." and "Pending rewind points are created automatically
during active agent sessions."; the --pending flag help and the command's
Long text advertised "shadow-branch rewind points"; the two error paths
said "failed to find rewind points". All now say pending checkpoints.
Two assertions in checkpoint_list_test.go pinned the empty-list string
and are updated with it -- they are the only tests that pin any string
this commit touches, and both are exact-match Contains calls, so nothing
else could have silently drifted.

The first-turn context injection told every agent to leave "(enable,
disable, clean, rewind, auth)" to the user. `entire rewind` has not
existed since #1747, so a third of that warning pointed at nothing.
trail_injection_text_test.go asserts only the prefix "Leave setup and
destructive commands", so it still passes; deprecated_strings_test.go
keeps "entire rewind" on its never-advertise list, which is the one place
the name should survive.

Comments. Three were wrong about mechanisms rather than just names, and
those were checked against the code rather than reworded:

  - gitrepo/status.go named "review, rewind" as the paths that keep the
    unbounded Status walk. The rewind one is gone; the two real callers
    are review_target.go and detectFileChangesUnbounded (`session
    adopt`), and the comment now names both.
  - manual_commit_session.go attributed FindSessionsForCommit and
    ClearSessionState to "the rewind reset command". They are called by
    `entire clean` (clean.go:177) and `entire doctor` (doctor.go:406)
    respectively -- different commands, so they get different comments.
  - common.go's DeleteBranchCLI cited HardResetWithProtection as the
    sibling go-git v5 workaround. That function does not exist anywhere
    in the tree; the real one is CheckoutBranch in git_operations.go, and
    the comment now points there.

The rest are vocabulary: agent.go's ProtectedDirs and the mirrored
comments in checkpoint/, session/state.go, api/checkpoint/metadata.go
(comment only -- nothing exported in api/ is renamed), explain.go,
resume.go, transcript.go and strategy/.

Historical references stay, because they explain why the current shape is
what it is: every `rewind --list` mention in checkpoint_list.go and
checkpoint_group.go (that bridge is the reason the JSON is frozen), the
"former interactive rewind picker" that pendingCheckpointLabel inherited
its format from, and manual_commit_workflow_test.go's note about the
assertions that replaced the rewind observations. Also untouched: every
"rewind" that means moving a git ref backwards (fetch_rewind_protection_test.go,
safely_advance_local_ref_test.go, checkpoint_remote_test.go, the
explain fetch tests) and internal/remotehelper/transport/proxy.go, whose
rewinding is of HTTP request bodies.

Skill and scripts. The harness verb list-rewind-points is now
list-pending-checkpoints, which is two characters wider than the old
longest verb, so the usage block's description column was re-padded to
match. scripts/test-attribution-e2e.sh only ever echoed the phrase; it
already called `checkpoint list --pending --json`.

Docs. CLAUDE.md's method list and Key Files entries pick up the new
identifiers and file name, and sessions-and-checkpoints.md's "## Rewind"
section is "## Pending Checkpoints" with a sentence defining the term
against condensation rather than against a command that no longer exists.
AGENTS.md is a symlink and untouched.

    13	// one ref per checkpoint: refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>. Each ref points

    16	const CheckpointRefPrefix = "refs/entire/checkpoints/"
    17	
    18	// RefName returns the per-checkpoint git ref for a checkpoint ID:
    19	// refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>, where <shard> is id.ShardFor() (the
    20	// last two characters of the ID for both legacy hex and ULID formats). The full
    21	// ID is always the leaf, so the ref round-trips through ParseRef.
    22	//
    23	// It errors on an empty or unrecognized checkpoint ID rather than returning a
    24	// malformed ref (e.g. "refs/entire/checkpoints//"), so callers at trust
    25	// boundaries — and future ones — can't silently push, fetch, or look up a bad
    26	// ref.
    27	func RefName(cid id.CheckpointID) (plumbing.ReferenceName, error) {
    28		if cid.Kind() == id.KindUnknown {
    29			return "", fmt.Errorf("cannot build checkpoint ref: invalid checkpoint ID %q", cid)
    30		}
    31		return plumbing.ReferenceName(CheckpointRefPrefix + cid.ShardFor() + "/" + cid.String()), nil
    32	}
    33	
    34	// ParseRef extracts the checkpoint ID from a per-checkpoint ref name,
    35	// reporting whether name is a well-formed checkpoint ref. A ref is well-formed
    36	// when it has the CheckpointRefPrefix, exactly a <shard>/<id> tail, and the
    37	// shard matches the ID's own ShardFor — so refs the resolver did not write
    38	// (mismatched shard, extra path segments) are rejected rather than silently
    39	// resolved to the wrong bucket. It does not require the ID to be a recognized
    40	// kind, so a future ID format still parses as long as it shards consistently.
    41	func ParseRef(name plumbing.ReferenceName) (id.CheckpointID, bool) {
    42		s := name.String()
    43		tail, ok := strings.CutPrefix(s, CheckpointRefPrefix)
    44		if !ok {
    45			return id.EmptyCheckpointID, false
    46		}
    47		shard, rest, ok := strings.Cut(tail, "/")
    48		if !ok || shard == "" || rest == "" {
    49			return id.EmptyCheckpointID, false
    50		}
    51		// Reject extra path segments: the tail must be exactly <shard>/<id>.
    52		if strings.Contains(rest, "/") {

    54		}

    56		if cid.ShardFor() != shard {

    58		}

   107			return nil, err
   108		}
   109		mirrors, err := buildMirrors(ctx, env, cfg, primaryType)
   110		if err != nil {
   111			return nil, err
   112		}
   113		writer := newFanoutStore(primary, mirrors)
   114	
   115		// Kind routing: resolve id-keyed reads and backfill writes by the
   116		// checkpoint's format across both git backends (a ULID lives in refs, a hex
   117		// ID on the branch or a migrated ref), so a coexisting / mid-migration repo
   118		// handles either format without reconfiguring. Creates still go through
   119		// writer (configured primary + mirrors).
   120		branchStore, refsStore, err := buildKindReadStores(ctx, env, primaryType, primary)
   121		if err != nil {
   122			return nil, err
   123		}
   124	
   125		return &Stores{
   126			Persistent: newKindRoutingStore(writer, branchStore, refsStore, primaryType),
   127			ephemeral:  newEphemeralStore(repo, refs),
   128			refs:       refs,
   129		}, nil
   130	}

   132	// buildKindReadStores returns the git-branch and git-refs read stores used for
   133	// id-kind read routing, reusing the already-built primary for whichever kind it
   134	// is and constructing the sibling. A non-branch/refs git-backed primary (not a
   135	// real configuration today, since buildPrimary only accepts git-backed backends)
   136	// yields both freshly built git stores.
   137	func buildKindReadStores(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, primaryType string, primary PersistentStore) (branch, refs PersistentStore, err error) {
   138		switch primaryType {
   139		case BackendTypeGitBranch:
   140			branch = primary
   141			refs, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitRefs, nil)
   142		case BackendTypeGitRefs:
   143			refs = primary
   144			branch, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitBranch, nil)
   145		default:
   146			if branch, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitBranch, nil); err == nil {
   147				refs, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitRefs, nil)
   148			}
   149		}
   150		return branch, refs, err
   151	}

   157			return cfg.Primary.Type
   158		}
   159		return BackendTypeGitBranch

   170	// buildPrimary constructs the primary persistent store. The primary must be a
   171	// git-backed backend: attach, resume, push, doctor, cleanup, and OPF all drive
   172	// the primary's record through the repo and its refs, so a non-git-backed
   173	// primary is rejected rather than silently half-supported.
   174	func buildPrimary(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, typ string, raw json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {
   175		if err := ValidatePrimaryBackend(typ); err != nil {
   176			return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.primary: %w", err)
   177		}
   178		return build(ctx, env, typ, raw)
   179	}
   180	
   181	// buildMirrors constructs the mirror writers. Each backend type may appear at
   182	// most once across the topology (primary + mirrors), so a mirror cannot reuse
   183	// the primary's type or another mirror's. This is the conservative form of "no
   184	// two backends may write the same target": today two backends of the same type
   185	// share the same refs/storage, so a duplicate type is a guaranteed collision
   186	// (e.g. a git-branch mirror under a git-branch primary would double-write the v1
   187	// branch). A future per-mirror config (same backend type pointed at a distinct
   188	// repo/refs) could relax this; for now it is one of each type.
   189	func buildMirrors(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, cfg *settings.CheckpointsConfig, primaryType string) ([]Writer, error) {
   190		if cfg == nil || len(cfg.Mirrors) == 0 {
   191			return nil, nil
   192		}
   193		seen := map[string]bool{primaryType: true}
   194		mirrors := make([]Writer, 0, len(cfg.Mirrors))
   195		for i, m := range cfg.Mirrors {
   196			if _, err := lookupBackend(m.Type); err != nil {
   197				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: %w", i, err)
   198			}
   199			if seen[m.Type] {
   200				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: backend type %q is already used by the primary or another mirror; each backend type may appear at most once", i, m.Type)
   201			}
   202			seen[m.Type] = true
   203			// Mirrors are best-effort write-only copies whose failures are logged
   204			// and dropped; never pay on-demand ref-fetch network probes for them.
   205			mirrorEnv := env
   206			mirrorEnv.RefFetcher = nil
   207			store, err := build(ctx, mirrorEnv, m.Type, m.Config)
   208			if err != nil {
   209				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: %w", i, err)
   210			}
   211			mirrors = append(mirrors, store)
   212		}
   213		return mirrors, nil
   214	}

   218			return *opts.Refs
   219		}
   220		return ResolveRefs(ctx)
   221	}

    14	
    15	// BackendTypeGitBranch is the built-in git-branch checkpoint backend: it stores
    16	// the committed record on a git branch (entire/checkpoints/v1) in this repo. It
    17	// is git-backed (see registeredBackend.gitBacked) and is the default primary
    18	// when no backend is configured.
    19	const BackendTypeGitBranch = "git-branch"
    20	
    21	// BackendTypeGitRefs is the built-in git-refs checkpoint backend: it stores the
    22	// committed record as one git ref per checkpoint (refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/
    23	// <id>) in this repo. Like git-branch it is git-backed, so it may be the primary;
    24	// the two can run side by side (git-refs primary + git-branch mirror) during the
    25	// branch->refs rollout, since the one-of-each-type rule permits distinct
    26	// git-backed backends in the same topology.
    27	const BackendTypeGitRefs = "git-refs"
    28	
    29	// OpenEnv carries the construction context a backend factory may need.
    30	// Git-backed backends require Repo and use Refs/BlobFetcher/RefFetcher/
    31	// RemoteRefLister; other backends ignore the git-shaped fields and read their
    32	// own configuration from cfg.
    33	type OpenEnv struct {
    34		Repo                  *git.Repository
    35		BlobFetcher           BlobFetchFunc
    36		RefFetcher            RefFetchFunc
    37		RemoteRefLister       RemoteRefListFunc
    38		MetadataBranchFetcher MetadataBranchFetchFunc
    39		Refs                  PersistentRefs
    40		// ReadRemotes is the ordered checkpoint read-candidate chain; see
    41		// OpenOptions.ReadRemotes.
    42		ReadRemotes []string
    43	}
    44	
    45	// Factory constructs a persistent store for one backend type. cfg is the
    46	// backend-specific JSON "config" block from settings (nil when absent).
    47	type Factory func(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, cfg json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error)
    48	
    49	// registeredBackend is a factory plus the capabilities the topology layer needs.
    50	type registeredBackend struct {
    51		factory Factory
    52		// gitBacked reports whether the backend stores the committed record in this
    53		// repo's git object store. Only git-backed backends may be the primary,
    54		// because the checkpoint lifecycle (resume bootstrap, doctor reconcile,
    55		// explain tree-read, push, cleanup, pre-push OPF) drives the primary's record
    56		// through the repo and its refs — see buildPrimary. A backend that is not
    57		// git-backed has no such ref for those paths to operate on, so it is
    58		// mirror-only (write fan-out) until that lifecycle moves behind the store.
    59		// Whether a backend may be a *mirror* is governed separately by the
    60		// one-of-each-type topology rule in buildMirrors, not by this flag (a
    61		// git-backed backend can mirror alongside a different git-backed primary).
    62		gitBacked bool
    63	}
    64	
    65	var (
    66		registryMu sync.RWMutex
    67		// registry maps backend type to its factory and capabilities. Git-backed
    68		// backends are built in (registered here). Other backends add themselves
    69		// through Register — in practice only test-only backends do, via their
    70		// RegisterForTesting helpers, so a production binary can never select them.
    71		registry = map[string]registeredBackend{
    72			BackendTypeGitBranch: {factory: gitBranchBackendFactory, gitBacked: true},
    73			BackendTypeGitRefs:   {factory: gitRefsBackendFactory, gitBacked: true},
    74		}
    75	)
    76	
    77	// Register adds a non-git-backed backend factory under typ. Such backends can
    78	// serve as mirrors but not as the primary (see registeredBackend.gitBacked).
    79	// Git-backed backends are built in and not registered through this path. It
    80	// panics on a duplicate type to surface wiring mistakes.
    81	func Register(typ string, f Factory) {
    82		registryMu.Lock()
    83		defer registryMu.Unlock()
    84		if _, exists := registry[typ]; exists {
    85			panic(fmt.Sprintf("checkpoint: backend type %q already registered", typ))
    86		}
    87		registry[typ] = registeredBackend{factory: f, gitBacked: false}
    88	}
    89	
    90	// lookupBackend returns the registered backend for typ, or a clear error
    91	// (naming the registered types) when the type is unknown.
    92	func lookupBackend(typ string) (registeredBackend, error) {
    93		registryMu.RLock()
    94		b, ok := registry[typ]
    95		registryMu.RUnlock()
    96		if !ok {
    97			return registeredBackend{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown checkpoint backend type %q (registered: %s)", typ, registeredTypes())
    98		}
    99		return b, nil
   100	}
   101	
   102	// ValidatePrimaryBackend reports an error unless typ names a registered backend
   103	// that may serve as the primary. An unknown type is rejected with an error
   104	// listing the registered backend types; a registered but non-git-backed type is
   105	// rejected separately, since only git-backed backends may be the primary. This
   106	// is the single source of the "primary must be git-backed" rule — buildPrimary
   107	// delegates here, and selection surfaces (entire enable / configure
   108	// --checkpoint-backend) call it to reject a bad backend before writing it to
   109	// settings, rather than failing later in Open.
   110	func ValidatePrimaryBackend(typ string) error {
   111		b, err := lookupBackend(typ)
   112		if err != nil {
   113			return err
   114		}
   115		if !b.gitBacked {
   116			return fmt.Errorf("checkpoint backend %q cannot be the primary: only git-backed backends (e.g. %q, %q) may be the primary", typ, BackendTypeGitBranch, BackendTypeGitRefs)
   117		}
   118		return nil
   119	}
   120	
   121	// build constructs the store for the named backend type.
   122	func build(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, typ string, cfg json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {
   123		b, err := lookupBackend(typ)
   124		if err != nil {
   125			return nil, err
   126		}
   127		store, err := b.factory(ctx, env, cfg)
   128		if err != nil {
   129			return nil, fmt.Errorf("construct %q checkpoint backend: %w", typ, err)
   130		}
   131		return store, nil
   132	}
   133	
   134	func registeredTypes() string {
   135		registryMu.RLock()
   136		defer registryMu.RUnlock()
   137		types := make([]string, 0, len(registry))
   138		for t := range registry {
   139			types = append(types, t)
   140		}
   141		sort.Strings(types)
   142		return strings.Join(types, ", ")
   143	}
   144	
   145	// gitBranchBackendFactory builds the git-branch persistent store from the open
   146	// environment. It ignores cfg: git topology comes from env.Refs, not settings.
   147	func gitBranchBackendFactory(_ context.Context, env OpenEnv, _ json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {
   148		if env.Repo == nil {
   149			return nil, errors.New("git-branch checkpoint backend requires a repository")
   150		}
   151		store := NewGitStore(env.Repo, env.Refs)
   152		if env.BlobFetcher != nil {
   153			store.SetBlobFetcher(env.BlobFetcher)
   154		}
   155		store.SetReadRemotes(env.ReadRemotes)
   156		if env.MetadataBranchFetcher != nil {
   157			store.SetMetadataBranchFetcher(env.MetadataBranchFetcher)
   158		}
   159		return store, nil
   160	}
   161	
   162	// gitRefsBackendFactory builds the git-refs persistent store from the open
   163	// environment. It ignores cfg and env.Refs: each checkpoint resolves its own ref
   164	// (refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>) rather than a single configured ref.
   165	func gitRefsBackendFactory(_ context.Context, env OpenEnv, _ json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {
   166		if env.Repo == nil {
   167			return nil, errors.New("git-refs checkpoint backend requires a repository")
   168		}
   169		store := newGitRefsStore(env.Repo)
   170		if env.BlobFetcher != nil {
   171			store.SetBlobFetcher(env.BlobFetcher)
   172		}
   173		if env.RefFetcher != nil {
   174			store.SetRefFetcher(env.RefFetcher)
   175		}
   176		if env.RemoteRefLister != nil {
   177			store.SetRemoteRefLister(env.RemoteRefLister)
   178		}
   179		return store, nil
   180	}
